Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5739, related to delivery approval error in UV SO due to incomplete Activity.
Please find the summary below:
{color:#ffffff}__{color}
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5739|
|Description|delivery approval error in UV SO due to incomplete Activity|
|Root Cause (RCA)|Please note that the Activity status in UV Sales Order is set to 'Work Completed' when Job Card is closed. After that user can manually set the status of Activity to 'Closed'. In both these cases where Activity status is 'Work Completed' or 'Closed', the Activity is considered to be completed.
So, the status of Activity being set as 'Closed' is not the issue in this case.
We have replicated this issue on FDP UAT-1 environment. Please find below the user steps:
1.) User created a Activity in UV Sales Order and created a Job Card for this Activity.
2.) User then set the status of Job Card to 'Canceled'.
3.) The Activity for this Job Card remained in UV Sales Order with status as 'Open'. User manually updated the status of this Activity to 'Closed'.
While completing the delivery approval request, the system check for he valid active Job Card linked to the Activity. In the affected record, since the Activity status is 'Closed' but the mapped JC was already cancelled, the system could not find a valid active JC. Due to this validation failure error message was displayed.
In this case user should manually update the status of this Activity to 'Cancel Request'.|
|Recovery status|Recovery has been completed.|
|Fix Plan|No fix required. When user Cancel the Job Card, the status of the Activity linked to this Job Card should be manually set to 'Cancel Request'.|
If you require further clarification or assistance, please feel free to reach out.
Regards
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A delivery approval error occurred in UV Sales Order because an Activity was marked Closed while its mapped Job Card had been canceled. During delivery approval, the system validates that an active Job Card is linked to the Activity; no valid active Job Card was found. Recovery was completed by updating the Activity status to Work Completed, and no product fix was required.
important_findings: An Activity in UV Sales Order is considered completed when its status is Work Completed or Closed.
Closing the Job Card normally sets the related Activity status to Work Completed.
The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 by canceling a Job Card and then manually changing the related Activity from Open to Closed.
Delivery approval validates that the Activity has a valid active linked Job Card.
A canceled mapped Job Card caused the validation failure because the Activity was Closed without an active Job Card.
When a Job Card is canceled, the linked Activity must be manually set to Cancel Request.
investigation_report.root_cause: The linked Job Card was canceled, but the related UV Sales Order Activity was manually set to Closed instead of Cancel Request, causing delivery approval validation to fail because no valid active Job Card was linked.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed by setting the Activity status to Work Completed. No fix was required; for canceled Job Cards, users must manually set the linked Activity status to Cancel Request.

important_findings: The MFTBCFFR-5210 change correctly set the vehicle "Service Person" field to blank by default; previously it was set to "Siebel Administrator".
The MFTBCFFR-5210 implementation unintentionally impacted standard ODI functionality.
The impact was that the Asset number was not updated/captured in the Serial Number field.
In Sales Order, header VIN# is obtained from "Vehicle No C#" on the Vehicle Screen, while Form Applet VIN# is obtained from "Key" on the Vehicle Screen.
Records requiring recovery were identified and recovered.
Incidents 5642, 5674, and 5737 were caused by similar issues and were fixed in the production environment.
investigation_report.root_cause: The fix implemented for AMS CR MFTBCFFR-5210 unintentionally affected standard ODI functionality, preventing the Asset number from being captured in the Serial Number field.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In UAT1, spreadsheet 1-502819545 appeared not to send an approval request after recovery in SR# 5709, although a pending request remained in the approver's Inbox. Recovery changed the spreadsheet from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed its approval history without removing the associated Inbox request entity. When the approver approved the remaining request, the spreadsheet changed to Spreadsheet Approved; JVs were created for the affected Job Cards. The system was determined to be behaving as expected, and the recovery procedure will be updated to deactivate pending approval requests during recovery.
important_findings: Recovery in SR# 5709 changed the spreadsheet status from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed approval history.
The request entity remained in the designated approver's Inbox after approval history was removed.
A subsequent approval submission did not create approval history, creating the appearance that no approval request had been sent.
Approving the remaining Inbox request changed spreadsheet 1-502819545 in UAT1 to Spreadsheet Approved.
JVs were created for 37 Job Cards associated with the Insurance Spreadsheet, totaling 148 Journal Voucher Items.
Future recovery procedures must deactivate pending approval requests to prevent hidden approvals.
investigation_report.root_cause: The recovery performed in SR# 5709 removed the spreadsheet approval history but did not remove the pending approval request entity from the approver's Inbox, disrupting the normal approval-history flow.
investigation_report.resolution: Created JVs for the 37 affected Job Cards (148 Journal Voucher Items) and updated the recovery procedure requirement to deactivate pending approval requests to designated approvers during spreadsheet recovery.

Dear Tsunoda-San,
以下の改善につきましては、Kaizenとして既に実装・リリース済みです。
# 定期実行される TOB ODI パッケージのデータロード履歴のアーカイブ
 実施内容
 TOBおよびD2Sから受信したデータをSiebelへ取り込む処理において、以前は同じODIパッケージを再実行すると、過去の取込履歴がデータベース上で上書きされていました。そのため、過去データの調査や参照ができない状況でした。
この課題に対応するため、以下の改善を実施しました。
すべてのデータ取込履歴を保持するアーカイブテーブルを作成しました。
アーカイブテーブルには、受注番号／資産番号、取込ステータス、取込元ファイル名、パッケージ名など、今後の調査に必要な情報を保存します。
データ取込処理を更新し、毎回の取込時にアーカイブテーブルへ自動で履歴が保存されるようにしました。
データ取込に失敗した場合は、サポートチームへ自動でメール通知を送信する仕組みを追加し、迅速な調査・対応ができるようにしました。
 上記は、既に実装済みのKaizen内容となります。
 今回の事象について調査した結果、同様の事象をさらに防止するために追加で実施可能なシステム改修は、現時点ではございません。
 ご不明な点やご質問等がございましたら、お知らせください。
 
よろしくお願いいたします。
comments.text_enu:
Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered, and re-executing the same D21F file under identical conditions successfully created the Recycle Order. The investigation could not determine a definitive cause because historical import data for the incident was no longer available. Re-executing the same D21F file under identical conditions completed successfully and created the Recycle Order without errors.
The affected D21F file was received at approximately the same time as a previous related incident.
Before the Kaizen change, re-executing the same ODI package overwrote or deleted past import history in the database, preventing retrospective investigation.
The implemented Kaizen archives data import history, including order number/asset number, import status, source file name, and package name.
The archive capability supports future investigation and analysis but did not establish the root cause of this incident.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered all affected records. Deployed the RITM1971770 Kaizen improvement to FDP Production to archive TOB and D2S import history and automatically notify the support team when data imports fail.

Mr. Tsunoda
Thank you for your help.
Problem:
The shipment was created, but the status of the chassis order was not updated.
Cause analysis:
This issue occurred because duplicate vehicles were created. Duplicate chassis orders were then created.
The cause of this problem is that the model code of the existing vehicle has been changed. This resulted in different model codes for existing vehicles and existing chassis orders. 
When a new D21A file was received with model code information based on the existing chassis order, a new vehicle was created and a new chassis order with the old model code was also created.
Combination 1: Ordering a vehicle with model code 2 and a chassis with model code 1 (PO Number: B000350487)
Combination 2: Order vehicle and chassis with model code 1 (PO Number: B000362896)
As a result, two vehicles with different model codes and two chassis orders with the same model code were created. Then, upon receiving the D21N file, combination 2 was shipped and combination 1 remained in C# contact. 
correction plan
In order to fix this problem, we made the following modifications to UAT.
# D21A file will be received from TOB.
# The D21A file confirms whether a chassis has been ordered.
# If there is a chassis order that has not been canceled, the system checks the model code of the chassis order.
# The system compares the model code of the vehicle with the model code of the chassis order and updates the vehicle model code using the model code of the chassis order as the master. This only runs on D21A files.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders, causing a shipment to be created while the chassis-order status was not updated. The established analysis attributes the duplication to a Model Code change that caused a mismatch between an existing Vehicle and its Chassis Order when a D21A file was received from TOB. important_findings: Duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders were created for C# 20287.
A Model Code change on an existing Vehicle resulted in different Model Codes between the Vehicle and the existing Chassis Order.
When D21A was received from TOB, the mismatch caused creation of a new Vehicle and a new Chassis Order with the old Model Code.
After D21N was received, the combination associated with PO Number B000362896 was shipped, while the combination associated with PO Number B000350487 remained in C# contact.
The SC fix matches the incoming TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record, and simultaneously updates the Vehicle Model Code.
The final feedback states that shipping had not been updated and required reconfirmation.

comments.text:
The reason why the record was not processed and JV for this was not created is because there was a character missing in the data that we received in the Invoice File(DT01*).
Received record for processing:
{{220FP84HG 500043 NWA2111010000000 T0048600{ 250614SHUSEI 7204 5FP84HGR3XCWB F}}
* In this record, the segment {{NWA2111010000000}} contains the order type indicator.
The character *“A” (at position 3 within this segment)* denotes that this is an *Additional Body order*.
* As per current logic, for *Additional Body (A)* and *Option* records, the system reads the *product identifier from the 66th position (from the start of the record)*.
* In this case, the value at the 66th position (expected product identifier field) is *blank/null*.
Observed segment around this position:
{{250614SHUSEI (__) 7204}} → the required field between these values is missing.
* Due to the absence of this value, the system was *unable to determine the product*, resulting in the *line type being set to NULL*.
* Conclusion: The incoming data record *does not conform to the expected format/configuration*.
* Action Taken: Enhancements have been implemented on the *Siebel side* to handle such cases where the expected field is blank.
* Impact: *No changes required from TOB side*. Similar records will be handled correctly going forward.
Best Regards,
Saad

*概要：* 
本件は、2月分のTOB請求書に対するJVの連携に関する問題です。 
毎月の第1週、特に月初の最初の営業日に、TOBより前月分のシャーシおよびリサイクルの請求データがSiebelへ送信されます。これらのデータは、JV作成およびKBシステムとの連携のために使用されます。 
Siebel側へは以下の2種類のファイルが送信されます。 
DT01 - シャーシ請求書 
DT27 - リサイクル請求書 
これら2種類のファイルは、それぞれ8つのFDP環境向けに送信されています。
*問題内容：* 
Incident# 5691で報告されている問題は、岡山FDP環境におけるシャーシ請求処理に関するものです。 
DT01ファイルには、以下の請求データ文字列が含まれていました。 
そのうち、C#：FP84HG-500043（黄色でハイライトされているデータ）に対応するデータが正常に処理されず、その結果、該当データに対するJVが作成されませんでした。 
*調査内容：* 
本件について詳細な調査した結果、以下の結論に至りました。 
各データ文字列において、青色で示された位置（左から25文字目）の値を使用して、請求データの種類を判別しています。 
現在のSiebel設定では、TOB請求データに対して以下の識別設定が定義されています。 
1：型式コード 
4：色 
8：S-架装 
C：変更（シャーシ） 
A：Post-OP 
その他コード：Options 
データ種別を識別した後、システムは文字列内の別の位置情報を使用して製品タイプを判定します。 
今回のデータはPost-OPタイプに該当していました。Post-OPタイプの場合、システムはオレンジ色で示された位置の値を使用して製品タイプを判定します。 
しかし、当該位置にNull値が設定されているケースについて、現行設定で適切にハンドリングされていませんでした。 
その結果、JV作成処理が失敗していました。 
*結論：* 
原因調査の結果を踏まえ、現在は設定変更を実施し、TOBデータにおける本ケースを適切に処理できるよう対応しました。 
同様の問題は、今後発生しない見込みです。

*Overview:*
This issue is related to JV coordination for February's TOB invoice. 
During the first week of each month, specifically the first business day of the month, the TOB sends the previous month's chassis and recycling billing data to Siebel. These data will be used for JV creation and coordination with the KB system. 
The following two types of files are sent to Siebel. 
DT01 - Chassis Invoice
DT27 - Recycling bill
These two types of files are being submitted for 8 FDP environments each.
*Question details:*
The issue reported in Incident# 5691 is related to chassis billing in an Okayama FDP environment. 
The DT01 file contained the following billing data string: 
Among them, the data corresponding to C#: FP84HG-500043 (data highlighted in yellow) was not processed correctly, and as a result, a JV was not created for the data. 
*Survey details:*
After conducting a detailed investigation into this matter, we have come to the following conclusions. 
In each data string, the value in the blue position (25th character from the left) is used to determine the type of billing data. 
The current Siebel configuration defines the following identification settings for TOB billing data: 
1: Model code
4: Color
8: S-bodywork
C: Change (chassis)
A：Post-OP
Other codes: Options
After identifying the data type, the system uses additional position information within the string to determine the product type. 
This data corresponded to the Post-OP type. For Post-OP types, the system uses the orange position value to determine the product type. 
However, the current settings did not handle cases where a Null value was set at the relevant position. 
As a result, the JV creation process was failing. 
*Conclusion:*​
Based on the results of the investigation into the cause, we have now made changes to the settings so that this case can be handled appropriately in the TOB data. 
Similar issues are not expected to occur in the future.

現在の機能および想定動作では、TOB請求ファイル内のデータはSiebelシステム内のデータと照合されます。一致するデータが見つかった場合、照合された金額に対してJVが作成されます。
 
不一致の場合は、TOB請求ファイルのデータを使用してJVが作成されます。このようなケースでは一致するデータが存在しないため、JVには「プロジェクトコード（CSJS211）」および「プロジェクトコード（CSJS311）」に対してAA00000000を使用されます。

The TOB invoicing is performed for Chassis Order Line Items. However, the TOB invoice data received in this case does not exist in the corresponding Chassis Order Line Items. Therefore, during the reconciliation process, no matching Chassis Order Line Item could be found based on the invoice data.

San,
 
Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
We would like to report the results of investigating the logic and related data regarding this matter.
 
TOB billing processing is performed for chassis order details. However, the details corresponding to the TOB billing data received in this case did not exist in the target chassis order details.

As a future measure, we will monitor TOB claim processing in order to detect such rare cases at an early stage.
 
If a JV is not created for a record in the TOB request file (DT01 file), we will detect it through monitoring and create a JV manually if necessary.
 
Based on the above investigation results, we would appreciate your approval to close this incident.
 
Please let us know if you have any questions or additional questions.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A TOB chassis invoice record in DT01 for C#: FP84HG-500043 did not create a Journal Voucher (JV). The record resulted in a NULL line type/product type because the relevant product-type field was NULL and Siebel did not have logic to create a JV for that condition. Subsequent analysis also found that the invoice line had no matching Chassis Order Line Item, causing the default Project Code AA00000000 rather than a chassis order number. Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions.
important_findings: The affected record was FP84HG-500043 in the DT01 Chassis Invoice file for the Okayama FDP environment.
The billing-data type is identified from the 25th character; the affected record was identified as Post-OP.
For the Post-OP record, the 2-character product-type value after the 66th character was NULL, causing the line type/product type to be NULL.
Siebel did not contain logic to create a JV when the line type was NULL, so no JV was created.

The corresponding invoice data did not exist in the Chassis Order Line Items, although it existed in an associated Sales Order line item; therefore reconciliation could not set the Chassis Order Number as Project Code (CSJS211).
When no matching Chassis Order Line Item is found, AA00000000 is assigned as the default project code; manual recovery was confirmed to process all TOB invoices without omission.
investigation_report.root_cause: The DT01 Post-OP invoice record had a NULL product-type field, which produced a NULL line type; Siebel had no JV-creation logic for records with a NULL line type. The related invoice line also had no matching Chassis Order Line Item for reconciliation.
investigation_report.resolution: Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions. Future TOB invoice processing will be monitored, and a JV will be created manually when a DT01 record does not produce a JV.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The D2S Invoice Mismatch screen had slow loading caused by inefficient processing in the PDQ. Initial indexing and removal of the sort specification did not fully resolve the production issue. The PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)" was subsequently optimized, significantly improving screen loading time while preserving export functionality.
important_findings: The PDQ scanned the full available dataset because unmatched records from all periods must remain available for review and export.
Initial analysis identified sorting on _D2S SO Number_, _D2S Line Number_, and _Part Number_ as a performance factor because the fields were not indexed.
An index based on the sort order was deployed to UAT and then production, but additional performance improvements were still required.
The configured sort order was D2S Order Number, Sales Order Item, and Part Number; the sort specification was removed, but the issue persisted after production release.
Optimizing PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)" significantly improved loading performance, and export functionality was verified successfully.
investigation_report.root_cause: Inefficient PDQ processing over the full dataset, including sorting operations on unindexed fields, caused slow loading of the D2S Invoice Mismatch screen.
investigation_report.resolution: Optimized PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)"; screen loading performance improved and export functionality was verified.

Thanks for your support.
*Recovery Status:*
The recovery is completed for the affected records across all FDP’s.
*RCA:*
This issue occurred due to the data received from the D2S team on 14th in the price master file was inconsistent, where the end date was provided with the year as “9998” instead of the expected “9999”. 
Please find below the sample data from the file received from D2S:
, 
So the data discrepancy happened in our system for these records where the year was received as “9998”. In our system logic, an end date with year “9999” is treated as an open-ended validity and is set as blank (NULL) on the UI. However, since the received data contained “9998”, it did not meet this condition and was processed differently by the system.
As a result, the system set the end date in previous record and new record processing was stopped due to the error. 
For example, Part#: ML356628:
The following data was received in the file - 
This led to inconsistencies in the Siebel system and caused the batch processing job to fail. Due to this failure, new records with updated start dates could not be created, while existing records had their end dates updated based on the current logic. 
*Fix:*
We have handled this condition in our new package processing so that no discrepancies occur in future based on Date. This issue has been fixed on FDP-PROD.
We’ll also ask Hirata san to investigate on D2S side that why the end date was sent as “9998” instead of “9999” for some records.
Meanwhile please let us know in case of any other queries.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The initial analysis attributed inconsistent price-master processing to D2S records containing end year "9998" instead of "9999", which caused existing records to receive end dates and prevented creation of new records. A change was deployed to new package processing on FDP-PROD to handle the date condition. However, the reported root cause and recovery were challenged because the mismatch differed by FDP and recovery was stated to be incomplete; further analysis was requested.
important_findings: The system treats an end date with year "9999" as open-ended validity and displays it as blank (NULL) on the UI.
Price-master records received with end year "9998" were processed differently, updating the previous record end date and stopping new-record processing.
The processing issue caused inconsistencies in the Siebel system and failure of the batch processing job.
A fix for the date condition was deployed in new package processing on FDP-PROD.
The D2S-file explanation was not confirmed because mismatches varied by FDP, and recovery was reported as incomplete for specified parts in Okayama and Aomori.

Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: ODI packages completed normally, but expected database updates and line-item creation were not reflected for affected records in Shikoku, Chugoku, and Okinawa. Re-executing the same file under the same conditions created the line items successfully, and no reproducible defect or process anomaly was identified. Data recovery was completed, and a Kaizen change was deployed to retain import history for future investigation; however, stakeholders stated that this was an event-confirmation/recovery-support measure rather than recurrence prevention and requested continued analysis.
important_findings: The same scenario affected incidents MFTBCFFR-5625, MFTBCFFR-5630, MFTBCFFR-5632, MFTBCFFR-5635, and MFTBCFFR-5701.
ODI packages and required processing conditions were confirmed as normal, but database updates were not reflected for the affected processing.
Re-executing the same file under identical conditions completed without errors and created the expected line items.
Before the Kaizen change, import history was deleted or overwritten after ODI package execution, leaving insufficient historical data for root-cause investigation.

The deployed Kaizen archives TOB and D2S import history, including order number/asset number, import status, source file name, and package name, and sends email notifications to the support team when import fails.
No reproducible defect or confirmed root cause was identified; stakeholders did not accept the archival change as a recurrence-prevention solution.

Dear Tsunoda-San,
以下の改善につきましては、Kaizenとして既に実装・リリース済みです。
# 定期実行される TOB ODI パッケージのデータロード履歴のアーカイブ
 実施内容
 TOBおよびD2Sから受信したデータをSiebelへ取り込む処理において、以前は同じODIパッケージを再実行すると、過去の取込履歴がデータベース上で上書きされていました。そのため、過去データの調査や参照ができない状況でした。
この課題に対応するため、以下の改善を実施しました。
すべてのデータ取込履歴を保持するアーカイブテーブルを作成しました。
アーカイブテーブルには、受注番号／資産番号、取込ステータス、取込元ファイル名、パッケージ名など、今後の調査に必要な情報を保存します。
データ取込処理を更新し、毎回の取込時にアーカイブテーブルへ自動で履歴が保存されるようにしました。
データ取込に失敗した場合は、サポートチームへ自動でメール通知を送信する仕組みを追加し、迅速な調査・対応ができるようにしました。
 上記は、既に実装済みのKaizen内容となります。
 今回の事象について調査した結果、同様の事象をさらに防止するために追加で実施可能なシステム改修は、現時点ではございません。
 ご不明な点やご質問等がございましたら、お知らせください。
 
よろしくお願いいたします。
comments.text_enu:
Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

Dear Tsunoda-San,
以下の改善につきましては、Kaizenとして既に実装・リリース済みです。
# 定期実行される TOB ODI パッケージのデータロード履歴のアーカイブ
 実施内容
 TOBおよびD2Sから受信したデータをSiebelへ取り込む処理において、以前は同じODIパッケージを再実行すると、過去の取込履歴がデータベース上で上書きされていました。そのため、過去データの調査や参照ができない状況でした。
この課題に対応するため、以下の改善を実施しました。
すべてのデータ取込履歴を保持するアーカイブテーブルを作成しました。
アーカイブテーブルには、受注番号／資産番号、取込ステータス、取込元ファイル名、パッケージ名など、今後の調査に必要な情報を保存します。
データ取込処理を更新し、毎回の取込時にアーカイブテーブルへ自動で履歴が保存されるようにしました。
データ取込に失敗した場合は、サポートチームへ自動でメール通知を送信する仕組みを追加し、迅速な調査・対応ができるようにしました。
 上記は、既に実装済みのKaizen内容となります。
 今回の事象について調査した結果、同様の事象をさらに防止するために追加で実施可能なシステム改修は、現時点ではございません。
 ご不明な点やご質問等がございましたら、お知らせください。
 
よろしくお願いいたします。
comments.text_enu:
Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered in the Iwate Prod environment. Investigation on the Siebel side was limited because historical import data for the incident was not retained after ODI package execution. A Kaizen under RITM1971770 was deployed to FDP Production to archive future import histories and notify support of import failures, but the requester did not accept this as a recurrence-prevention resolution.
important_findings: The affected record was recovered in the Iwate Prod environment.
Before the Kaizen, re-executing the same TOB ODI package caused previous import history to be overwritten or deleted from the database, preventing investigation of past imports.
No historical data remained for this incident, so Siebel stated that no further incident-specific investigation could be performed.
RITM1971770 added an archive table to retain import history including order number/asset number, import status, source file name, and package name.
The data import process was updated to automatically archive each import, and failed imports now trigger email notifications to the support team.
The Kaizen was deployed to the FDP Production environment, but the requester stated that it supports event confirmation rather than preventing recurrence.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Sales Quotation BIP displayed an incorrect Branch Manager Name because its mapping logic did not use the branch associated with the quotation. Earlier logic derived Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position, which could return the wrong branch manager when the creator moved between branches. The logic was revised in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, then deployed to Production through the June 2 emergency release.
important_findings: The initial BIP mapping for Branch Sales Manager name was incorrect.
The prior BIP logic displayed the Last Name of the Sales Rep's Parent Position as Manager Name.
The required logic is to display the Branch-Head of the branch from which the quotation originated, rather than the quotation creator's current branch or position hierarchy.
Using the creator/Sales Rep as the reference could display a different branch manager when the creator moved from branch A to branch B.
After the Production deployment, BIP displays blank when no branch manager exists in the target organization hierarchy.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect Sales Quotation BIP mapping logic derived Branch Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position instead of the branch associated with the quotation.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the BIP logic to display the Branch-Head of the quotation's originating branch, validated the change in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, and deployed it to Production via the June 2 emergency release.

*Root Cause:*

いつも大変お世話になっております。
MFTBCFFR-5575 について、分析した結果は以下の通りです。
根本原因分析
初回のD21Aファイルは、2025年11月20日に型式コードが紐付かない状態で受領されました。
当時は型式コードが未登録であったため、システムは型式情報を紐付けずにシャシーオーダーを作成しました。
その後、2025年12月17日に型式マスターファイルが受領され、同日中に該当する型式コードが生成・登録されました。
続いて、2025年12月18日に再度D21Aファイルが受領されました。この時点では既に型式コードが存在していたため、システムは当該ファイルを処理し、型式コードを含む新たなシャシーオーダーを作成しました。
その結果、同一のD21A入力に対して、型式コードなしのシャシーオーダーと、型式コードありのシャシーオーダーの2件が作成され、プール原価オーダーの重複作成が発生しました。
|Chassis Order|Pool Cost Order|VIN #|Fuso Rec#|
|B000303862|B000338198|MS06GP-20016|038765|
|B000332117|B000339371| | |
何かご不明な点がございましたらご連絡ください。
宜しくお願い致します。
Shubham Agarwal
Dear San,
Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed the issue and below are the key findings along with the root cause.
The initial D21A file was received on 20 November 2025 without an associated model code. Since the model code was not available at that time, the system proceeded to create a chassis order without linking any model information.
Later, the model master file was received on 17 December 2025, after which the system generated and registered the corresponding model code on the same date.
Following this, the D21A file was received again on 18 December 2025. However, since the model code had already been created by that time, the system processed the file and generated a new chassis order, this time including the model code.
|Chassis Order|Pool Cost Order|VIN #|Fuso Rec#|
|B000303862|B000338198|MS06GP-20016|38765|
|B000332117|B000339371| | |
As a result, two separate chassis orders were created for the same D21A input—one without the model code and another with the model code—leading to duplicate pool cost order creation.
Best Regards,
Shubham Agarwal

いつも大変お世話になっております。
 
原因調査の結果、観測されたシステム動作は、現在のデザインおよびファイル処理シーケンスと一致していることが確認されました。
 
 
|ファイル受信日|ファイル名|オーダー詳細/モデルコード詳細|ステータス|システム動作|
|2025年11月18日|D21A_19112025200850 (TOB)|B000303862 (モデルコードなし)|シャシーオーダーはモデルコード情報付きで受領されましたが、
当該モデルコードはその時点ではシステムのマスターデータに存在していませんでした。|モデルコードなしで作成されたシャシーオーダー|
|2025年12月17日|TCH01 (業務側からの追加要件)|MS06GPQGUCV-9 
(以前のD21Aファイルにあったモデル )|該当モデルコードのマスターデータがシステムに作成されました|システム上でマスターデータが更新されました|
|2025年12月18日|D21A_17122025200816 (TOB)|B000332117 (モデルコード付き)|同一のシャシーオーダー情報が再受領され、
今回はモデルコードがシステム上で既に利用可能な状態でした。|モデルコード付きで新しいシャシーオーダーが作成されます|
 
 
説明：
 
2025年11月18日、モデルコード（MS06GPQGUCV-9）付きのD21AファイルD21A_19112025200850（TOB）を受信しました。
 
しかし、処理中に、モデルコードMS06GPQGUCV-9がシステムマスタデータに存在しませんでした。そのため、シャーシオーダー（B000303862）はモデルコードなしで作成されました。
 
2025年12月17日、業務側からの依頼によりTCH01ファイルが実行され、モデルコードMS06GPQGUCV-9がシステムに正常に作成されました。
その後、2025年12月18日に、同じモデルコードMS06GPQGUCV-9を含むD21AファイルD21A_17122025200816（TOB）が再度受信されました。この時点でモデルコードは既にシステムにあったため、システムはモデルコードが入力された新しいシャーシオーダ（B000332117）を作成しました。
 
重要な指摘事項：
 
TCH01ファイルは毎日受信されますが、該当モデルコードMS06GPQGUCV-9は通常の毎日のファイル処理では入手できなかったため、業務側の要求に基づいて特別に実行されました。
 
システム変更依頼に関して：
 
業務要件として、システム上で後からモデルコードが取得可能となった場合には、既存のシャシーオーダーに対して当該モデルコードを自動的に更新（アップサート）することが求められています。
 
ただし、D21A処理は以下の両方の作成を担っているため本改修は現行システムデザインの範囲内では実現不可です。
 
車両データ
シャーシオーダデータ
 
 既に作成されたシャシーオーダーに対して更新を導入する場合、それに依存する複数の他システムおよび関連する業務プロセスに影響を及ぼす可能性があります。
 
また、将来的にこのような不具合を回避するため、TOBにおいてMC-9のモデルコードを日次のTCH01ファイルに含めることが可能です。現在、MC-9に該当するモデルコードカテゴリは日次ファイル処理に含まれていないため、初回のD21A処理時点では必要なモデルコードがシステム上で利用できない状態となっていました。
 
 参考までに、詳細なタイムライン分析を添付いたしましたので、ご確認お願い致します。
本インシデントをクローズさせていただきたく存じます。
 
ご不明な点がございましたら、ご連絡お願い致します。
よろしくお願いいたします。

Description:
 
On November 18, 2025, we received D21A file D21A_19112025200850 (TOB) with model code (MS06GPQGUCV-9).
 
However, during processing, model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was not present in the system master data. Therefore, a chassis order (B000303862) was created without a model code.
 
On December 17, 2025, the TCH01 file was executed at the request of the business side, and model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was successfully created in the system.
Then, on December 18, 2025, the D21A file D21A_17122025200816 (TOB) containing the same model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was received again. Since the model code was already in the system at this point, the system created a new chassis order (B000332117) with the model code entered.
 
Important points:
 
Although TCH01 files are received daily, the corresponding model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was not available through normal daily file processing, so it was specifically executed based on the business's request.
 
Regarding system change requests:
 
As a business requirement, if a model code becomes available later on the system, it is required to automatically update (upsert) the model code to an existing chassis order.
 
However, since D21A processing is responsible for creating both of the following, this modification is not possible within the scope of the current system design.
 
vehicle data
Chassis order data
 
If you implement an update to a chassis order that has already been created, it may impact multiple other systems and related business processes that depend on it.
 
Additionally, to avoid such problems in the future, TOB can include the MC-9 model code in the daily TCH01 file. Currently, the model code category corresponding to MC-9 is not included in daily file processing, so the required model code was not available on the system at the time of the first D21A processing.
 
For your reference, we have attached a detailed timeline analysis, so please take a look.
We would like to close this incident.
 
If you have any questions, please contact us.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate chassis orders and pool cost orders were created when the same D21A chassis information was processed before and after its model code became available in master data. D21A_19112025200850 (TOB) created chassis order B000303862 without model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 because the code was absent from master data; after TCH01 created the code, D21A_17122025200816 (TOB) created B000332117 with the model code. The behavior matches the current system design, but a permanent corrective measure was not agreed or completed.
important_findings: D21A processing created a chassis order even when the received model code was not present in system master data.
Model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was created by TCH01 on 17 December 2025 after a business request, rather than through normal daily file processing.
When the same chassis information was re-received through D21A after the model code became available, the system created a new chassis order instead of updating the existing order.
The duplicate chassis orders resulted in duplicate pool cost orders.

The requested automatic upsert of a newly available model code to an existing chassis order is not possible within the current D21A/Siebel design because D21A creates both vehicle data and chassis order data and changes may affect dependent systems and business processes.
Including MC-9 model codes in daily TCH01 processing was proposed as a future prevention option, but it was rejected as not being a solution.
investigation_report.root_cause: The model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was unavailable in system master data during the initial D21A processing, so the system created a chassis order without the model code. After TCH01 created the model code, re-receipt of the same D21A information was processed as a new chassis order rather than an update, causing duplicate chassis and pool cost orders.

Please find below the updates on this incident:
We have fixed the issue occurring in all the UV 2-05 FDP reports and reports are correctly visible now. Please find below the RCA and countermeasure:
*RCA:*
•The issue is caused by a applied hidden filter on SO# in the reports during the deployment of Profit column logic last year in 2025.
•However, that SO# is not available in any of the FDPs except Okinawa.
•Because of this mismatch, the backend query is processing unnecessary data.
•As a result, the query is exceeding resource limits and throwing an error to display the data.
*Countermeasures:*
# We will revalidate the Power BI filters after deployment in both UAT and PROD environments.
# Additionally, we will verify whether all reports are displaying data correctly post-deployment.
# These post-deployment sanity checks will be included in the release communication.
Since no further action is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this ticket and let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report.investigation_summary: All UV 2-05 FDP reports failed to display data because a hidden SO# filter applied during the 2025 deployment of Profit column logic caused backend queries to process unnecessary data and exceed resource limits. The filter was removed/fixed, and the reports are now correctly visible. Future deployments will include Power BI filter validation and post-deployment report checks in UAT and PROD.
important_findings: A hidden SO# filter was applied to the reports during the 2025 deployment of Profit column logic.
The filtered SO# is not available in any FDP except Okinawa.
The mismatch caused backend queries to process unnecessary data, exceed resource limits, and return an error when displaying data.
The issue affected all UV 2-05 FDP reports.
Power BI filters and report visibility will be revalidated after deployments in UAT and PROD.
investigation_report.root_cause: A hidden SO# filter applied during the 2025 Profit column logic deployment referenced an SO# unavailable in FDPs other than Okinawa, causing backend queries to process unnecessary data and exceed resource limits.
investigation_report.resolution: The report issue was fixed and all UV 2-05 FDP reports are correctly visible. Post-deployment Power BI filter validation and report-display sanity checks in UAT and PROD will be added to release communication.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved inconsistent behavior when setting the "Bill to Basic Account Code" field in Siebel. Analysis identified missing explicit sequencing of field-value setting, similar to a prior issue involving "Bill to Basic Account Name". The sequencing fix was implemented at the Business Component level, validated in UAT, and released to production on the 23rd.
important_findings: AR and AP Account Ids depend on the User Account Id being set first.
Incorrect field-value setting order previously caused failures when fetching AR and AP Account Ids for "Bill to Basic Account Name".
The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field did not have equivalent explicit sequence handling and was identified as the cause of inconsistent results.
The fix was implemented at the Business Component level, covering MF Job Card Detail Applet, MF JC List Applet (@JC), and MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master).
MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order) already had the required sequencing and required no change.
The change was deployed to all FDP-PRODs and applied to the production environment in the release on the 23rd.
investigation_report.root_cause: The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field lacked explicit sequencing to set the User Account Id before retrieving dependent AR and AP Account Ids, resulting in inconsistent behavior.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented the required field-value sequencing at the Business Component level, tested it in UAT, and deployed the change to all FDP-PRODs.
technical_entities: MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master)
MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order)

comments.text:
Dear Tsunoda San,
いつもお世話になっております。
MFTBCFFR-5509について、Hoshinoさんからのご質問に対する回答を以下にご連絡いたします。
1．計算ロジックに問題がないとのことですが、その根拠をご提示ください。
計算ロジックの検証に使用した証跡および計算ロジックの説明については、既に共有済みです。
計算ロジックは以下の通り動作します。
「登録手数料税額（Registration Commission Fee Tax）」は、「登録手数料合計（Registration Total Commission Fee）」の10%として自動計算されます。
また、本項目はユーザーによる手動更新が行われない限り、「登録手数料合計」の10%として正しい値が維持されます。
2．ロジックは正しいものの、画面への反映が正常に行われていない可能性はありますか。
計算結果はリアルタイムで更新・表示される仕組みとなっています。
そのため、計算ロジックが正しく実行された場合は、更新後の値が即座に画面へ反映されます。
したがって、計算ロジックは正しいにもかかわらず、画面に更新後の値が反映されないという事象は発生しません。
実際に動作確認を実施し、計算ロジックに基づいて画面上の値が即時更新されることを確認しております。
3．今回対象となっているレコードに関する証跡をご提示ください。

角田さん 
既にご説明しておりますとおり、調査の結果、請求書BIP上の消費税は、NV見積書の「登録手数料税額」項目から算出されていることを確認いたしました。
Siebelでは当該税額は正しく計算されておりましたが、ユーザーによって当該項目の値が手動で変更されており、その変更後の値が後続の見積およびSOへ引き継がれた結果、請求書 BIPにも同じ値が反映されていることを確認しております。
UAT環境にて、手動で`項目値を変更する同様のシナリオを再現し、各種テストケースおよび回帰テストを実施しました。値が変更されたのはユーザーによる手動更新が行われた場合のみであり、それ以外の場合には値は正しく計算・保持されていました。また、当該値が変更される他の要因も特定されませんでした。したがって、本件はSiebelの機能上の問題ではなく、ユーザーによるデータ変更であることを確認しました。
*対策について*
会議でもご説明したとおり、現時点での対策案として、既存の「登録手数料税額」項目を参照専用とし、同一画面上に別の編集可能な項目を追加することを提案しております。これにより、ユーザーが手動で変更した値を明確に把握でき、今後同様の差異が発生した際の原因特定が容易になると考えております。
Siebel側としては、本件に関する調査は完了しており、現行機能に問題は確認されておらず、現時点で追加の予防策が必要となる事象も確認されておりません。また、本事象は現時点では1件のみで発生していることから、Siebelの機能起因の問題とは判断しておりません。
よろしくお願いいたします。
Tanish
comments.text_enu:
Mr. Tsunoda
As we have already explained, as a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that the consumption tax on the BIP invoice is calculated from the "Registration fee tax amount" item on the NV estimate.
The tax amount was calculated correctly in Siebel, but the value of the item was manually changed by the user, and as a result of the changed value being carried over to subsequent estimates and SO, we have confirmed that the same value is reflected in the invoice BIP.
In the UAT environment, we reproduced a similar scenario of manually changing item values ​​and conducted various test cases and regression tests. The value only changed when the user made a manual update, otherwise the value was calculated and maintained correctly. Also, no other factors were identified that could change this value. Therefore, we have confirmed that this issue is not a functional issue with Siebel, but rather a data modification by the user.
*About countermeasures*
As explained at the meeting, the current countermeasure is to make the existing "Registration Fee Tax Amount" item for reference only and add another editable item on the same screen. We believe that this will allow users to clearly understand the values ​​that have been manually changed, and will make it easier to identify the cause of similar discrepancies in the future.
On Siebel's side, the investigation into this matter has been completed, and no issues have been identified with current functionality, nor are there any events that require additional preventive measures at this time. Additionally, since this event has only occurred in one case so far, we have not determined that the issue is due to Siebel functionality.
Thank you for your support.
Tanish

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Consumption Tax on the BIP invoice is sourced from the NV Quote field "Registration Commission Fee Tax," which is calculated as 10% of "Registration Total Commission Fee." Testing in UAT-1 and code/UI regression testing reported that the calculated value displays and updates correctly unless the editable field is manually changed, and changed values propagate to subsequent Quotes and Sales Orders. However, the discussion did not provide conclusive evidence that a user manually changed the affected production record, and the proposed read-only change was not approved.
important_findings: "Registration Commission Fee Tax" is automatically calculated as 10% of "Registration Total Commission Fee."
Consumption Tax in the invoice/Expense BIP is derived from "Registration Commission Fee Tax" in the NV Quote.
The field is editable in the UI by design for FDP, allowing manual value changes.
A changed "Registration Commission Fee Tax" value is synchronized to subsequent Quote revisions and Sales Orders, then reflected in BIP invoices.
The behavior was reproduced in FDP UAT-1 using Quote# 1-85UN3O and Sales Order# A001303334.
Testing reported no calculation or screen-refresh defect, but no conclusive production-record evidence of manual user modification was provided.

important_findings: NV Sales Order# A000413141 has Product Class of Vehicle set to 'Trailer'.
Trailer and Forklift Product Classes were not handled in NV Order Sheet-3, causing the vehicle base price to remain blank.
The initial BRD-based explanation that Order Sheet-3 output should be blank for non-Bus vehicles did not meet the required behavior equivalent to specification 2.
The fix was implemented and verified in UAT-1 using NV Sales Order# A001301436.
The fixed changes were applied to the Production environment in the March 25 FDP regular release.
investigation_report.root_cause: NV Order Sheet-3 did not handle Trailer and Forklift Product Classes, resulting in a blank vehicle base price for Trailer sales orders.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated NV Order Sheet-3 to handle Trailer and Forklift Product Classes; validated the change in UAT-1 and deployed it to Production on March 25.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Planned Delivery Date in the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order. This caused an incorrect invoice payment date when the Quote and Sales Order planned delivery dates differed. The mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation was changed to use the Sales Order and was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to PROD in the May 13 release.
important_findings: The affected invoice showed PaymentDueDate 2026-03-31 because Payment Term was 1 and the Quote Planned Delivery Date was 2026-02-25.
As an immediate recovery, the Quote Planned Delivery Date was updated to 2026-03-17, matching the Sales Order date, and the invoice displayed the correct value after regeneration.
The confirmed defect was that Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate/Planned Payment Date was sourced from NV Quote rather than NV Sales Order.

UAT1 tests confirmed that when the Sales Order Planned Delivery Date was present, PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Sales Order date; the test response was sent to KB for invoice report generation.

Holiday handling was clarified to include Saturdays, Sundays, and defined public holidays; adding holiday-aware Planned Payment Date calculation was identified as a separate Project Change Request requirement.
The mapping fix was released to PROD in the May 13 release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Planned Delivery Date used to calculate Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was mapped from the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Planned Delivery Date mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation from Sales Quote/NV Quote to Sales Order/NV Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to PROD on May 13.

Thank you for your continued support.
We would like to share the analysis details for incident MFTBCFFR-5488, regarding the sync issue in the UV Sales Order.
Issue:
The Profit of the Sales Order and the latest Quote revision are not aligned.
Root Cause Analysis (RCA):
The issue occurred because Sub Quote 1-7DUHTZ was synced to the UV Sales Quote after the sales quote had already been approved and synced to the Sales Order. This was possible because the "Update Customer Quote" button on the Sub Quote detail view remains active even after the Sales Quote status is set to "Initial Approval Completed".
We have successfully replicated this issue in the FDP UAT-1 environment (Reference Record: UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ, UV SO#: E001303159).
Steps to Reproduce:
# Create a UV Sales Quote and add an Activity.
# Create a Job Card from the Activity.
# In the UV Sales Quote, click 'Generate Approval' and proceed to create the UV Sales Order.
# In the Job Card, complete the Work Order and create a Service Quote.
# Click "Update Sales Quote" button in the Service Quote to create a Sub Quote under the UV Sales Quote.
# Observe that the UV Sales Quote status is "Initial Approval Completed", but the "Update Customer Quote" button remains active.
# Click "Update Customer Quote" to sync Service items to the UV Sales Quote.
# Note that these items are not synced to the UV Sales Order.
Fix Plan:
Once the UV Sales Quote status is "Initial Approval Completed", if a user attempts to click the "Update Customer Quote" button in the Sub Quote tab, a validation message will be displayed:
"Sales Quote has already been completed."
Recovery Status: Recovery has been completed.
Kindly review the proposed fix plan and let us know if you have any questions or concerns.
Regards,
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate vehicle records were created when a vehicle was initially registered without a model code because the model code was unavailable in the Production environment. After the model code was added, the update process searched by model code and could not match the original record, so it created a new record. Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles were recovered, and monitoring was deployed across all FDP environments to detect and recover similar records promptly.
important_findings: The initial vehicle record was created without a model code because the code was not available in the Production environment.
The update process uses the model code to locate an existing vehicle record.
Because the original record lacked the model code, the system could not identify it and created a duplicate vehicle record with the correct model code.

Example impacted record: Hakodate Production vehicle MS06GP-20085; initial record created on 19 Dec 2025, model code added on 23 Dec 2025 under SR MFTBCFFR-5162, and duplicate creation occurred during the 24 Dec 2025 update.
Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles required recovery; recovery of the Hakodate vehicle was completed.
A monitoring script was deployed across all FDP environments to send email alerts for similar records so they can be recovered immediately.
investigation_report.root_cause: The model code was unavailable when the original vehicle record was created, leaving that record without a model code. After the code was added, the system's model-code-based update lookup could not find the original record and created a duplicate vehicle record.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered impacted Sales Orders and vehicle records, and deployed a monitoring script across all FDP environments that sends email alerts for records matching this condition, enabling immediate recovery.

Please find the detailed analysis below:
In NV Sales Order, when a user creates a Registration Request, the Vendor Code is derived from the Registration Request Master based on the Registration Location specified in the NV Sales Order.
For the affected records, the associated Vendor Code did not contain the required Accounts Payable information, which led to the reported issue. After correcting the Vendor Code, the user was able to successfully create the Registration Request with the correct Registration items.
This is clearly a Master Data issue rather than a Siebel System Issue. Hence, no fix is required on the Siebel side.
Additionally, it is understood that the Registration Master data has already been updated, and the user was able to proceed with the registration process successfully. As such, no further master data updates are required at this stage.
Going forward, validation of the Registration Master data through SR MFTBCFFR-5501 will help prevent recurrence of similar issues.
Given the above, all points have been addressed and no further action is pending from our side. We would like to proceed with the closure of this Jira ticket.
Regards,
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Registration Request tax-related line items were not created when the Vendor Code derived from the Registration Request Master had no Account Payable Information. This prevented required values from being maintained and could prevent tax finalization/JV creation. The solution was aligned with the SC version, tested in UAT-1, and released to PROD on 13 May.
important_findings: In NV Sales Order, the Vendor Code for a Registration Request is derived from the Registration Request Master based on the Registration Location.
When the derived Vendor Code lacked Account Payable Information, tax-related Registration Line Items were not generated.
JV creation requires tax Registration Items with Part# S02, S03, or S06 and an actual amount greater than zero.
Before tax finalization, mandatory vendor payment fields are required when the actual amount including tax is greater than zero.
The fix was changed to match the SC version by making Customer Code, Customer Payment Date, and Customer Payment Method editable in Registration Request line items.
The changes were implemented in UAT-1, tested with SO# A001302470 and A001303987, and released to PROD on 13 May.
investigation_report.root_cause: The system did not create tax-related Registration Request line items when the Vendor Code derived from the Registration Request Master lacked Account Payable Information, leaving users unable to maintain required information for tax finalization.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated Registration Request line-item behavior in accordance with the SC version, including editable Customer Code, Customer Payment Date, and Customer Payment Method fields; the change was released to PROD in the 13 May release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Invoices could not be issued because the Payment Date was blank when the source Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote. The investigation established that the system lacked the required fallback logic to derive the invoice payment date from delivery-related dates under the configured payment-deadline conditions. The logic was iteratively corrected and tested in UAT-1, then released to PROD in the 13th May release.
important_findings: Payment Date on the Invoice was blank because the corresponding value was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote.
The original behavior required a manually entered Payment Date after selecting a month in Payment Term Type, which did not satisfy the required invoice behavior.
For Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle = "After Delivery", a null Payment Date must use the planned delivery date before Sales Posting and the Actual Delivery Date after Sales Posting.
The required fallback behavior was expanded beyond Payment Due (Term) Vehicle = "00"; dates also had to be displayed for terms other than "00".
For Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle = "After Deadline", the proposed behavior was to display Payment Scheduled Date when Payment Date was null and make the field mandatory at Quote.
The proposal to replace the Actual Delivery Date with the system-generated actual sales date was rejected.
investigation_report.root_cause: When Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote, the Invoice logic did not derive a payment date from the required delivery-related dates and payment-deadline conditions.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented the corrected payment-date derivation logic based on user feedback, completed UAT-1 testing, and released the change to PROD in the 13th May release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Sales Orders were displayed in the logged-in user's 'My' view even when the user was not the sales person in charge. Investigation determined that visibility was granted to all members listed in the Other Team Members/Sales Order team context. The visibility logic was changed so that only the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association can view the order in 'My'; the change was deployed to Production on 23/04/2026.
important_findings: Entity Transfer added users to the Sales Order team, causing multiple users to be associated with an order.
The issue occurred because Sales Orders were visible in 'My' view for all members shown in the Other Team Members applet.
The required behavior was that selecting 'My' must not display orders belonging to other sales representatives.
The final visibility rule uses the logged-in user as the Primary Employee of the primary position association with the order.
The same correction was applied to the NV Quotes tab.
The production deployment was completed in the release on 23/04/2026.
investigation_report.root_cause: The 'My' view visibility logic allowed all users associated through the Other Team Members/Sales Order team to view a Sales Order, instead of restricting visibility to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented code-level visibility logic restricting Sales Order and NV Quotes tab 'My' view results to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association, then deployed the fix to Production on 23/04/2026.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An incorrect approval flow was triggered for an NV Quote revision because the backend field "Profit Amount High Flag" was set to "Y" incorrectly. The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity, while other approval-flow scenarios operated correctly. A code-level fix was implemented to recalculate the field from the latest Quote revision updates and was deployed to Production in the April 23 FDP release.
important_findings: The incorrect value "Y" in "Profit Amount High Flag" caused the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to be triggered incorrectly.
"Profit Amount High Flag" is a backend field used in approval-flow conditions for NV Quote revisions based on Sales Profit changes.
For revised NV Quotes, the flag should be "Y" when Sales Profit remains the same or increases, and "N" when Sales Profit decreases.
The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity; other tested approval-flow cases were reported as working correctly.
The implemented fix recalculates "Profit Amount High Flag" based on the latest updates made during Quote revision.
The fix was deployed to Production through the FDP release on April 23.
investigation_report.root_cause: During NV Quote revision, "Profit Amount High Flag" was incorrectly updated to "Y" due to multi-browsing activity, causing the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to trigger instead of the applicable flow.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented a code-level fix to recalculate "Profit Amount High Flag" using the latest Quote revision updates, validated the NV Quote approval process in FDP UAT-1, and deployed the change to Production in the April 23 FDP release.

Monitoring and recovery were continued until the production deployment.
investigation_report.root_cause: The logic to calculate Consumption tax was missed in the Siebel IBOS component during CR-4194 development, causing incorrect or missing tax Journal Voucher creation for IBOS Shipment Detail responses.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A delivery approval error occurred for an NV Sales Order after the associated Chassis Order was moved to "Pending" through an SR and then reprocessed to "Ordered." The system attempted to create another Vehicle record; because a Vehicle already existed, the existing Vehicle was unmapped from the Chassis Order and Sales Order. The issue was replicated in UAT-1, the affected record was recovered on February 27, and the user subsequently completed Sales Posting.
important_findings: Approving an NV Sales Order with Product Class "Trailer" automatically created a Chassis Order.
Setting the Chassis Order to "Ordered" created a Vehicle that was mapped to both the Chassis Order and Sales Order.
After the Chassis Order was set to "Pending" through an SR and reprocessed to "Ordered," the system attempted to create a new Vehicle record.
Because a Vehicle record already existed, no new Vehicle was created and the existing Vehicle was unmapped from both related orders.
The behavior was replicated in UAT-1 using SO# A001302411 and Chassis Order# B001302412.
investigation_report.root_cause: Recovery performed under an SR changed the Chassis Order status to "Pending" after a Vehicle had already been created. Reprocessing the order to "Ordered" caused the system to attempt Vehicle creation and unmap the existing Vehicle from the Chassis Order and Sales Order.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected record on February 27; the user successfully completed Sales Posting for the Sales Order.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Tax exemption/Non Tax Flag was always set to "Y" because the corresponding flag was disabled in Siebel configuration, preventing its logic from executing. An initial UAT1 configuration fix did not cover the "Both" case for new registration of accounts receivable and payable when the Tax exemption flag was unchecked. Additional changes were made and verified in UAT1, then deployed to production through an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
important_findings: The Consumption Tax Exempt flag/Non Tax Flag was inactive in Siebel configuration, so its logic processing did not execute and the field defaulted to "Y".
The initial configuration change resolved part of the issue in UAT1 but failed for "New registration of both accounts receivable and payable" when the Tax exemption flag was unchecked.
Necessary changes were made for the "Both" case on UAT1, and user testing confirmed that everything was working as expected.
The validated fix was applied to the production environment in an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Consumption Tax Exempt flag/Non Tax Flag was disabled in Siebel configuration, preventing logical processing and causing the field to default to "Y".
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the required configuration, including changes for the "Both" accounts receivable and payable registration case; the fix was verified in UAT1 and deployed to production via an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
technical_entities: New registration of both accounts receivable and payable

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved duplicate Chassis Orders/Purchase Orders and Recycle Fees, plus blank Pool Cost items in NV Pool Cost Order. Duplicate Purchase Orders were traced to duplicate Vehicle records in Chugoku production for chassis# MS06GP-20140, caused when a Vehicle Model Code update created records with different model codes. Pool Cost Master End Date values were corrected in FDP Chugoku and affected records were recovered, but the recurrence-prevention fix for the duplicate-order issue remained pending deployment to FDP.
important_findings: Receiving multiple D21A files from TOB is normal and was not the confirmed cause of the duplicate-order issue.
Chugoku production contained two Vehicle records for chassis# MS06GP-20140 with different Model Codes, resulting in duplicate Purchase Orders.
Updating the Model Code on a Vehicle was identified as causing duplicate Purchase Order and Vehicle records; a similar issue was recorded in MFTBCFFR-4952.
Pool Cost Master End Date values in FDP Chugoku remained set to 2025, causing blank Pool Cost items; the End Date was corrected and affected records were recovered.
The SC fix changes Model Code matching to use the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and synchronously updates the Vehicle Model Code from the incoming TOB file.
The duplicate-order fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871, but deployment to FDP required SC approval.
investigation_report.root_cause: A Vehicle Model Code update created duplicate Vehicle records with different Model Codes for the same chassis#, which generated duplicate Purchase Orders/Chassis Orders. Separately, Pool Cost Master End Date values in FDP Chugoku had not been updated and remained set to 2025.

important_findings: Approval history timestamps indicated concurrent user actions.
The approver set Action to Approved while the alternative approver simultaneously set Action to Rejected.
The concurrent actions caused other approvals to become Auto Rejected and retained the first approval as Approved.
The scenario was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Quote "1-7XXRK3".
The affected UV Quote was recovered by setting its status to In Progress.
investigation_report.root_cause: Simultaneous Action updates by the approver and alternative approver from multiple browsers, resulting in conflicting Approved and Rejected actions.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected record by changing the current UV Quote status to In Progress, allowing the user to continue the Quote Approval process.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In NV FDP China, trade-in vehicles were not displayed on the Sales Order Sheet, and Stamped Model Code, Registered Year, and C/# number were blank in NV quotations and sales orders. Investigation confirmed that Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0, while Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are sourced from the Product ID of the linked Model Code. The observed values were blank in FDP production and SC production; C/# number is designed to remain blank in both environments.
important_findings: Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0.
The target NV quotation had Trade-In Amount set to 0 on the trade-in vehicle detail line, so the trade-in item was not displayed.
Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are populated from the Product ID of the linked Model Code.
The applicable Model Code had blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code values in both FDP production and SC production.
C/# number is always blank by design in both SC and FDP environments.
SC production SO# A037817024 also had Trade-In Amount of 0 and therefore did not display the trade-in item in Order Sheet BIP.
investigation_report.root_cause: The trade-in vehicle was not displayed because its Trade-In Amount was 0, which does not meet the Order Sheet BIP condition of Trade-In Amount greater than 0. Blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code resulted from blank values on the applicable linked Model Code; C/# number is blank by design.
investigation_report.resolution: No corrective change was applied. The behavior was confirmed as existing Order Sheet BIP logic and existing data/configuration; updating C/# number was offered if requested.

This issue is replicable on UAT, please follow these steps to replicate it on UAT-1 ->
1) Create a New Job Card
 2) Create a work order and add Line Items (Parts, Labor and Lubrication) in it.
 3) Create/Sync Quote and make the quote customer approved.
 4) Now Labor list price will be same in JCO and Quote.
 5) Go to Work Order Line Items cancel one of the labor.
 6) In quote the price of cancelled labor is removed, but in JCO price of cancelled labor is still there. so, there is a difference in
   Labor List Price at Quote and JCO.
 7) Now close the Job Card without syncing service quote to JCO
 
 At this point, we can see a price mismatch:
 Quote shows the reduced labor price
 JCO still shows the higher labor price.
 
 We have performed thorough analysis of this issue and found the root cause:-
RCA:
 When a user cancels any line item (labor/parts/lubricants) in the Work Order, the system immediately updates the total price in the Quote.
 However, the JCO price is not updated at the same time.
 The JCO price is updated only when a quote is created and customer approved after the cancellation of Line Items.
 So, if a line item is cancelled after quote is customer approved, and user does not create and customer approved a new quote but he directly closes the Job Card. Then the JCO continues to display the old price, while the Quote shows the updated price.
 This is why a price difference appears between the Quote and the JCO.
 
Fix Plan:
We are currently evaluating different possible fix options for this issue.
 Please allow us to schedule a meeting with you, so we can discuss the available approaches and decide on the most suitable fix plan.
 Meanwhile Let us know in case of any query.
Regards,
 Ayaz

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In FDP UAT-1, cancelling a Work Order line item after Quote customer approval updated the Quote price but left the JCO price unchanged when the Job Card was closed without creating and approving a new Quote. The issue was compared with SC behavior and a synchronization fix was implemented in UAT-1. The fix was released to the production environment on March 11.
important_findings: The issue was reproducible in UAT-1 when a labor, parts, or lubrication line item was cancelled after the Quote was customer approved.
Cancelling a Work Order line item immediately updated the Quote total, but did not update the corresponding JCO price.
JCO pricing was previously refreshed only when a new Quote was created and customer approved after the line-item cancellation.
The resulting mismatch affected Labor List Price between the Quote and JCO when the Job Card was closed without re-syncing the Service Quote.
In FDP, the JCO Subtotal price is sent to KB, making JCO price synchronization required.
The fix was tested in UAT-1 using SC behavior as the reference and then deployed to production.
investigation_report.root_cause: The FDP JCO price was not synchronized when Work Order line items were cancelled after Quote customer approval; JCO was updated only after a subsequent Quote creation and customer approval.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented a JCO price synchronization fix in FDP UAT-1, aligned with the SC reference behavior, and released it to production on March 11.

 Thank you very much for your continued support.
 Regarding the incident*, the investigation results are as follows.
|Incident number|MFTBCFFR-5317|
|Event Details|The status of the Assessment Request cannot be updated to "Completed" or "Cancelled." |
|RCA|This case is a request for appraisal regarding an Unstock Vehicle.
 
The appraisal request was created by user ID D8HIHARA (role: Branch-Sales-Staff).
After approval, the status of the appraisal request is updated to "Submitted to UV".
 
Then, when UV staff processes the assessment request,
By setting the "Quotation Vehicle Allocation" flag to "Y",
This appraisal request has been determined as an Unstock Vehicle case.
 
With existing functionality, if an appraisal request is created by Branch-Sales-Staff,
Only the following statuses can be edited.
 
Submitted to UV
 
JAAI Assessment In Progress
 
Assessment In Progress
 
Rejected
 
In progress
 
Assessment Completed
 
If a status other than the above is set, the appraisal request will be read-only.
 
In this case, the status of the appraisal request was set to “Vehicle for Quotation”, so
The status was set to Read-Only, and UV staff were unable to update it to "Completed." |
|Recovery status|Based on your instructions, we implemented recovery measures on February 3rd.
The status of the appraisal request has been updated to "Cancelled". |
|Correction Plan|As a result of checking the entire FDP production environment, no other incidents similar to this issue have occurred.
We have confirmed that the phenomenon itself is operating as the existing function.
 
However, in light of this issue, we plan to implement the following modifications.
 
Even if the appraisal request is created by Branch-Sales-Staff,
When the status is set to “Vehicle for Quotation”,
Change the logic to still set the status to Editable.
 
Once we receive approval for this response policy, we will proceed with modifications to the UAT environment. |
|Scheduled date of implementation of UAT|February 10, 2026|
 
Please contact us if you have any questions.
 Thank you for your understanding.
 Himanshu Tandon

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An Assessment Request for an Unstock Vehicle could not be updated to "Completed" because it became read-only after reaching "Vehicle for Quotation". The request was created by user D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role, for which existing functionality permits editing only specific statuses. Recovery was completed on February 3 by updating the Assessment Request to "Cancelled", and a logic change was planned for UAT to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable.
important_findings: The Assessment Request was created by user ID D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role.
The "Quotation Vehicle Allocation" flag was set to "Y", causing the request to be treated as an Unstock Vehicle case.
For Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff, statuses outside the configured editable-status list are read-only.
When the request status became "Vehicle for Quotation", UV staff could not update it to "Completed" because the status was read-only.
A review of the FDP production environment found no other similar incidents.
investigation_report.root_cause: Existing editability logic made Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff read-only when their status was set to "Vehicle for Quotation", preventing UV staff from changing the status to "Completed".
investigation_report.resolution: On February 3, the affected Assessment Request status was updated to "Cancelled". A follow-up change was planned in the UAT environment to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable even when the request was created by Branch-Sales-Staff.

 システムが販売利益計算時に型式コード明細を正しく識別できないため、*型式コードの価格が二重に控除される事象が発生しました。*|

|修正プラン|本件の対応として、非車両明細（Non-Vehicle Line Item） の検索条件を修正しました。
Vehicle ID が空白であり、かつ Product Type が「型式コード」ではないレコード を判定します。
これにより、在庫外車両（Unstock Vehicle）の場合でも、型式の明細が非車両明細として誤判定されることはなくなります。|
