Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5306, related to Profit Calculation Mismatch in UV Sales Quote.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5306|
|Description|UV Sales Quote Profit Mismatch|
|Root Cause (RCA)|This issue occured because the affected Production Record (AR#: H000522508, Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK) is a case of Unstock Vehicle. In this scenario, the Chassis# is not mapped to the assessment.
During profit calculation in UV Sales Quote, Vehicle and Non-Vehicle line item prices are calculated separately based on the Vehicle ID, which is present only in the Model Code line item.
In the case of Vehicle Unstock, Chassis is not present in Model Code line item and thus its Vehicle Id remains blank. Due to this Model Code is considered as Non-Vehicle Line Item. Since the system fails to correctly identify the Model Code line item during Sales Profit calculation, this results in the Model Code price being deducted twice.|
|Recovery status|Recovery has been completed on January 30.|
|Fix Plan|To fix this issue, we have updated the search spec for Non-Vehicle Line Items. Now it will identify records which are having Blank Vehicle Id and the Product Type is not 'Model Code'.
This will ensure that in case of Unstock Vehicle, Model Code Line item is not considered as Non-Vehicle line item.|
|Planned UAT date|The fix has been implemented on UAT1 environment.
Reference record:
AR#: H000052299
UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD|
If you require further clarification or assistance, please feel free to reach out.
Best Regards

investigation_report.investigation_summary: UV Sales Quote profit calculation mismatched for production record AR#: H000522508, Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK, an Unstock Vehicle case. A blank Vehicle ID on the Model Code line item caused it to be classified as a Non-Vehicle Line Item and its price to be deducted twice. The affected record was recovered, and the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification was corrected, validated in UAT1, and released to Production on February 19.
important_findings: The affected record was an Unstock Vehicle, where the chassis number was not mapped to the assessment.
Vehicle and Non-Vehicle line item prices in UV Sales Quote are calculated separately based on the Vehicle ID in the Model Code line item.
For Unstock Vehicle cases, the Model Code line item has no chassis and its Vehicle ID remains blank.
The blank Vehicle ID caused the Model Code line item to be treated as a Non-Vehicle Line Item, resulting in its price being deducted twice during Sales Profit calculation.
The corrected Non-Vehicle Line Item search condition identifies records with blank Vehicle ID only when Product Type is not 'Model Code'.
The fix was implemented in UAT1 using AR#: H000052299 and UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD, then released to Production on February 19.
investigation_report.root_cause: For an Unstock Vehicle, the Model Code line item had a blank Vehicle ID because no chassis was present. The Non-Vehicle Line Item search logic therefore misclassified the Model Code line item as non-vehicle, causing the Model Code price to be deducted twice during UV Sales Quote profit calculation.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected record and updated the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification to exclude records with Product Type 'Model Code' when Vehicle ID is blank. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on February 19.

SV Quote directly stored Adjusted List Price for specified Labor Billing Types, while UV Quote multiplied by Qty in all cases. The SV Quote logic was implemented in UV Quote, validated in UAT-1, and released to Production on February 19.
important_findings: The mismatch affected Total List Price between SV Quote and UV Quote.

For Shaken, 3-month Inspection, 6-month Inspection, 12-month Inspection, 24-month Inspection, MPC Shaken, PDF Shaken, MPC + PDF Shaken, and Spare Tire – Toolbox, SV Quote stores Adjusted List Price directly.
UV Quote applied multiplication by Qty for all Labor Billing Types, including types requiring directly stored Adjusted List Price.
The updated UV Quote pricing behavior was validated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote# 1-7VR5H1 and SV Quote# 1-7VR5I9.
The fix was released to Production in the February 19 FDP release.
investigation_report.root_cause: UV Quote did not implement the SV Quote pricing logic for specified Labor Billing Types and instead multiplied the price by Qty in all cases.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented the SV Quote pricing logic in UV Quote so that Adjusted List Price is stored directly for the affected Labor Billing Types; validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on February 19.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Quote revisions failed when the copied 'Promissory Note Due Date' was earlier than the quote revision/creation date and triggered validation. The underlying cause was an incorrect backend date-field format that made date values non-comparable. The date format was corrected, successfully tested in UAT-1 on Quote '1-2MZIQ2', and deployed to PROD in the 5-Feb-2026 regular release.
important_findings: Validation requires 'Promissory Note Due Date' to be greater than or equal to the quote creating date.
During quote revision, historical promissory-note dates caused validation errors for quotes including 1-6YMFWCN, 1-6Z3N4YR, and 1-6Z3N60P.
Temporary recovery changed affected promissory-note due dates to the current date so users could complete quote revisions, then restored the original dates.

Existing quote-revision behavior creates the revised quote with a blank 'Promissory Note Due Date' when the original date is earlier than the quote revising date; the user can then enter a new date manually.
Quote copy does not copy the 'Promissory Note Due Date'; it is entered manually and must satisfy the quote-creation-date validation.
The proposed change to disable validation during quote revision was not required after identifying the backend date format defect.
investigation_report.root_cause: The backend date field format was incorrect, making 'Promissory Note Due Date' values non-comparable and causing validation errors during quote revision.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the backend date field format, validated the fix in UAT-1 using Quote '1-2MZIQ2', and deployed the fix to PROD in the 5-Feb-2026 regular release.

important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT-1 for Chassis# Test-60VX using Assessment Requests H000052187, H000052188, and H000052190.
Purchase Quote associated with Assessment Request H000052187 was incorrectly selected when processing another Assessment Request.
The affected Production records had the same root cause as the UAT-1 reproduction.
Recovery for the affected records was completed before the permanent code fix.
After the UAT-1 fix, users could create a new Assessment Request for the same Chassis#.
investigation_report.root_cause: An incorrect code-level Search Specification queried Purchase Quote using the wrong Assessment Request number, causing the Purchase Quote for Assessment Request H000052187 to be selected incorrectly.
investigation_report.resolution: The Search Specification was corrected to query Purchase Quote using the correct Assessment Request number. The fix was deployed to UAT-1 on January 27, 2026 and released to Production in the February 5 FDP regular release.

important_findings: Reports with 88 and 90 records generated correctly, while shipment O000181209 with 93 records generated blank pages.
The blank-page issue occurred when shipments had more than 90 line items and the BIP report exceeded 15 pages.
BIP configuration and alignment were not aligned for reports containing more than 90 items.
The initial UAT-1 changes had to be applied to the new delivery-slip format implemented under CR-0869.
The PDF-generation error in the new format was resolved, and the bottom-page feed names Delivered and Quantity Delivered were corrected to display on one line.
The BIP report was confirmed to work correctly for up to 96 line items.
investigation_report.root_cause: BIP configuration and alignment did not correctly support delivery-slip reports with more than 90 line items, causing blank pages in reports exceeding 15 pages.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the BIP changes for the new delivery-slip format, resolved the PDF-generation error and bottom-page feed-name wrapping, and validated the report on UAT-1 for up to 96 line items. Production release was approved and planned for the FDP release scheduled for 2026-07-23.

PBI-UAT initially included Net Operation Time in the Special Sales Price calculation, although this was reported as incorrect for the tested Billing Type.
Testing in UAT1 (FDP Okoyama) found mismatches for JC I001301489: Siebel 43,200 versus differing values in reports 1-01, 1-10A, 1-12A, 1-15A, and no update in 1-02.
ODI code was modified to correct Sales price values in PowerBI Report 1-10A and to align sales-price logic in reports 1-10A, 1-15A, and 1-12A.
investigation_report.root_cause: ODI sales-price calculation logic in PowerBI did not match Siebel logic for special labor and Billing Type scenarios, including incorrect Net Operation Time handling and inconsistent report logic.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Tax amount finalization error was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882. The issue occurred after a user manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax'; the affected YN6M line item was not updated to Invoiced when the invoice was created. The incident was classified as user misoperation, with no affected cases found in any FDP Production Environment; users should revise the UV Sales Quote and restore the correct expense line items.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT-1 with UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882.
Creating an invoice automatically updates standard line items with Type 'Tax' to status Invoiced.
The manually changed line item with Part Number YN6M and Type 'Tax' was not updated to Invoiced.
Tax Finalization requires all line items with Type 'Tax', including manually updated lines, to be Invoiced.
No cases of manually changing an Expense Line item to 'Tax' were found in any FDP Production Environment.
investigation_report.root_cause: User manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax', causing the YN6M line item to remain outside the expected invoicing-status update and not be set to Invoiced before Tax Finalization.
investigation_report.resolution: No system fix or recovery was required. The user should revise the UV Sales Quote and update the correct expense line items.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was reproduced for JC# I001300905 on FDP - UAT1: a Quote Item showed Line Discount % as 0% after manually entering List Unit Price for Dummy Lubricant (..999999), while the synced JCO Order Item showed 100%. Investigation identified differing Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item, associated with a null Lubrication Price. A JCO-side fix was implemented in UAT and deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.
important_findings: The issue was replicated on FDP - UAT1 for JC# I001300905.
When List Unit Price was manually entered for Dummy Lubricant (..999999) while the Quote was In Progress, Quote Item Line Discount % was 0%.
After the Quote became Customer Approved and the JCO was created/synced, the Order Item Line Discount % became 100%.
Quote Item and Order Item used different Line Discount % calculation behavior.
The issue was associated with Lubrication Price being null.
The initially proposed approach to make List Unit Price read-only was rejected; the fix was changed on the JCO side.
investigation_report.root_cause: Different Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item when Lubrication Price was null caused the JCO Order Item Line Discount % to become 100% while the Quote Item remained 0%.
investigation_report.resolution: A JCO-side fix was implemented and validated in UAT, then deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.

Dear Tsunoda-San,
We would like to report on the survey results.
Chassis order was created by TOB file on December 10, 2025. On the other hand, the model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" in the TOB file was created on December 15, 2025, so the model code did not exist at that time, and this event occurred.
Subsequently, on December 26, 2025, we implemented restoration measures for model code creation in all FDP environments, and this issue has been resolved.
Also, regarding TOB master update, there is no mechanism in which all master files are automatically updated.
Regarding this point, a meeting regarding TOB batch processing is scheduled for July 24, 2025.
After the meeting, we will report again on the processing details of the TOB file.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Chassis Orders were created with a blank/missing model code because the relevant model code was not registered when the TOB/D21A processing occurred. The model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025 after the chassis order had been created on 10-Dec-2025. Impacted records were recovered after model-code creation was restored across FDP environments; the investigation also identified that not all TOB master files are automatically updated.
important_findings: The affected chassis order was created on 10-Dec-2025, while model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025.
Model code "MS06GPQUCV-9" was missing from the Chugoku, Wakayama, and Okayama Model Master, preventing chassis-order creation in those environments.
Affected Chassis Orders were recovered by correcting master data and reprocessing the relevant records; recovery was reported complete for all impacted records.
Model codes with MC "9" were manually updated in Chugoku and Wakayama on 26-Dec-2025 after receipt of the required TCH01 file.

TCH01 is the TOB PC Master 2 - Model Master inbound batch interface to Siebel via SFTP and is scheduled as a daily package run in Siebel PROD; not all TOB master interfaces are scheduled for daily PROD processing.
The proposed preventive control is to prevent Chassis Order creation when a model code is absent, notify the AMS team by email, correct data, and reprocess the record.
investigation_report.root_cause: The required model code was not registered in the system when the TOB/D21A file was processed. Specifically, "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created after the corresponding Chassis Order, and TOB master updates were not configured so that all master files were automatically updated.
investigation_report.resolution: Model-code creation was restored and missing model codes were manually updated in the affected FDP environments. The impacted Chassis Orders were recovered and reprocessed after the required master data was available.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The reported amount mismatch between the order form and sales estimate was initially observed as different discount mappings between Quotation BIP and Order Sheet BIP. The final investigation determined that the Quote price was changed after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approval, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order. This was classified as a user mis-operation rather than a product defect.
important_findings: Quotation BIP showed a Discount amount of -819798 from MF Vehicle Discount Amount, while Order Sheet BIP showed -60000 from MF UV Discount.
The Quote price was changed after the Quote had been approved and the Sales Order had been created.
A price change made after Quote approval without re-approval is not reflected in the Sales Order.
The incident was determined not to be a bug and was proposed for rejection.
investigation_report.root_cause: The user changed the Quote price after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approving the Quote, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order.
investigation_report.resolution: Users should avoid changing the Price after Quote Approval; the incident was rejected as a user mis-operation rather than a bug.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation compared the entered Branch Code with the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, preventing invoicing when the codes differed. For I000111578 (D8YOOSEK), the relevant Primary Location Code was "70"; for I000111572 (D8MICSAS), it was "00". CR MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code filter, allowing Individual Invoice issuance from Branch Code "00"; Bulk Invoice was unaffected because it selects Branch from the JC Header.
important_findings: The entered Branch Code was validated against the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, which can be checked in the employee Location Code.
I000111578 (D8YOOSEK) had Primary Location Code "70", while I000111572 (D8MICSAS) had Primary Location Code "00".
Before the MFTBCFFR-4379 release, I000111578 could be invoiced using Branch Code "70".
MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice, allowing invoice issuance from Branch Code "00".
Bulk Invoice was not affected because Branch is selected from the JC Header.
investigation_report.root_cause: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation/filter required the entered Branch Code to match the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, causing failures when the codes differed.
investigation_report.resolution: Deployed CR MFTBCFFR-4379, which removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice.

Dear Tsunoda san
Thank you for your continued support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident# MFTBCFFR-5069 reported on December 04, 2025, related to delivery approval error in NV Sales Order on Wakayama Production environment.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number|MFTBCFFR-5069|
|Description|A delivery approval error was displayed in NV Sales Order, thus preventing the user from completing the process.|
|Root Cause (RCA)|Please note that both affected NV Sales Order# A000009087 and A000011464, have product class as 'Trailer'. In this case, when the Sales Order is Approved, a purchase order having type as 'Trailer & Forklift' is automatically created. 
Subsequently, when the status of this Purchase Order is updated to "Ordered", the system creates a new Vehicle record and populates its Vehicle ID in both the Purchase Order and the corresponding Sales Order.
For the affected records in Wakayama Production, the Sales Orders were approved successfully and the corresponding Purchase Orders were generated. When the Purchase Orders status was updated to "Ordered", new Vehicle records were created as expected.
However, the issue occurred because the Vehicle Id of this newly created Vehicle was populated correctly in the Purchase Order but was not populated in the corresponding Sales Order. During the Delivery Approval process, the system validates the Vehicle information between the Purchase Order and Sales Order. Due to the Vehicle ID mismatch, the validation failed and the Delivery Approval error message was displayed.|
|Recovery status|Completed|
|Fix Plan|We have reviewed this issue at the code level and confirmed that there is no defect in the current implementation and the process is working as expected. We attempted to replicate this issue in UAT environment but this issue could not be replicated.
We have monitored this issue over the past few months, and no recurrence has been observed on any production environment.
Also please note that the affected Purchase Orders were completed in March 2025 whereas the issue was reported in December 2025. Due to the significant time gap , some information is not available to access the issue. As a result, while we were able to identify that the Delivery Approval error was caused by a Vehicle ID mismatch between the Purchase Order and Sales Order, we do not currently have sufficient information to determine why the Vehicle ID was not populated in the Sales Order at that time. 
We will continue to monitor the system, and if a similar issue occurs in the future, we will investigate it immediately and take the necessary corrective actions.
Since there are no pending actions at this time and the issue has not recurred, we would like to proceed with closing this ticket.|
Regards
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Delivery Approval failed for NV Sales Order records A000009087 and A000011464 in the Wakayama Production environment. The failure was traced to a Vehicle ID mismatch between the automatically created Purchase Order and its corresponding Sales Order. The affected records were recovered, but the underlying reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined because required historical system information was no longer retained.
important_findings: Both affected NV Sales Orders had product class "Trailer", which automatically creates a "Trailer & Forklift" Purchase Order after Sales Order approval.
When the Purchase Order status changed to "Ordered", a new Vehicle record was created and its Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order.
Delivery Approval validates Vehicle information between the Purchase Order and Sales Order; the Vehicle ID mismatch caused the validation error and blocked Delivery Approval.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT or FDP UAT, and no similar recurrence was observed in production environments during subsequent monitoring.
The affected Purchase Orders were processed in March 2025 but the incident was reported in December 2025, after the required system-information retention period had expired.
System log retention is planned to be extended from one month to two months to support investigation of future occurrences reported within the retention period.
investigation_report.root_cause: The immediate cause of the Delivery Approval error was a Vehicle ID mismatch: the newly created Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order. The reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined.
investigation_report.resolution: Affected records were recovered. No defect was identified in the current implementation and no reproducible code fix was confirmed; continued monitoring and extension of system log retention from one month to two months were planned for future investigation and recurrence prevention.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: JV Base Amount for Outsource Non IBOS was mapped from the Outsource order's Total Selling Price instead of the Purchase Order Total price. Body Building Order JVs also selected incorrect account codes when Vehicle Type was null. The mapping was changed and validated on UAT1, then released to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release; recovery reverse and corrective JVs were requested for affected BB orders.
important_findings: Outsource Non IBOS JV Base Amount was sourced from Total Selling Price in the Outsource order, which was 5000 for the investigated case.
The required mapping for both IBOS and Non-IBOS cases was Purchase Order Total price; when multiple POs exist in an Outsourcing order, a JV must be created for each PO.
For PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS, a null Vehicle Type caused selection of account code 038, rather than the required Account Code CSJS201: 031 and Subsidiary Account Code CSJS202: 60.
Incorrect Account Item Code CSJS201 records were identified for recovery through reverse JVs and corrected JVs based on the Vehicle Class.
The Purchase Order Total price mapping was fixed and validated on UAT1 using SO# A001300621, then released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Account Item Code CSJS201 & 301 issues were being addressed through CR MFTBCFFR-4627.
investigation_report.root_cause: JV mapping used the Outsource order Total Selling Price rather than Purchase Order Total price, and Body Building Order JV account-code selection defaulted to account code 038 when Vehicle Type was null.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the JV Base Amount mapping to Purchase Order Total price on UAT1, validated the change, and released it to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release. Recovery required reverse and corrected JVs for affected BB orders with posting date 20251211.

Thank you for your continued support.
We have completed our analysis of the reported issue and would like to share our findings. 
RCA (Root Cause Analysis):
During our of Parts Sales Return Orders where the VIN# and Registration# fields were blank, we observed that the corresponding parent Parts Sales Orders and the originating Parts Quotes also contained blank values for these fields. Since the VIN# and Registration# details were not entered at the initial Parts Quote stage, the same was carried forward to the Parts Sales Order and subsequently to the Parts Sales Return Order.
For validation, we created two sample records  on FDP UAT1 for Parts Sales Return Orders:
M001300484 – with VIN# and Registration# populated
M001300482 – with no VIN# and Registration# 
The PBI report(PT5-10) correctly reflected the VIN of M001300484 as VIN values added in Parts quote.
 
Based on our analysis, this behavior is not an issue on the Siebel side or the PBI side. The root cause is that the VIN# and Registration# fields were not entered by the user at the time of creating the initial Parts Quote.
Since it is not a system issue, kindly allow us to reject this incident.  
Please let us know if you require any further information.
Best Regards,

investigation_report.root_cause: The Parts Internal Return process did not populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order for NV and UV Order Department, leaving VIN# and Registration# blank.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Parts Internal Return process to populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order, released the fix in the 17/12/2025 FDP release, and data-patched affected FDP-PROD records.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: When changing the Sales Rep on a Sales Order, the Entity Transfer functionality did not initially display D8OKATAR because the Employee Applet search logic required the same Primary Position Type as the current Sales Rep. Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition allowed users from other locations to appear. The search logic was corrected to display only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code, and the fix was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
important_findings: The original Entity Transfer condition required users to be in the same organization and have the same Primary Position Type as the primary Sales Rep.
D8OKATAR was excluded because its Primary Position Type was Branch-Sales-Staff, while D8TAKOUN and D8THORIK had Branch-Sales-Manager.
The Primary Position Type condition had been added under MFTBCFFR-4341, but the requested behavior was branch-based selection without a job/position-type restriction.
Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition made positions in the Sales Rep's department visible, but also displayed users from other locations.
The Employee Applet search logic was revised so Entity Transfer displays users with the same branch as the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Employee Applet/Entity Transfer search logic used a Sales Rep Primary Position Type condition rather than limiting eligible users solely by the Sales Order branch; after that condition was removed, the logic was still insufficiently constrained and displayed users from other locations.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the Employee Applet search logic to show only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code. The change was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
technical_entities: Sales Rep Primary position Id condition

Thanks for your support.
*RCA*:
*(1) Reason for Payment Terms were included in UAT4–8 but not reflected in PROD:*
 The Payment Condition values displayed in the BIP are based on the PO Sheet master. During the initial setup for Wave-3, the master data for these Payment Conditions was not provided by biz.
 When the incident *MFTBCFFR-4978* was raised, the missing values were added across all UAT environments, and the master data was uploaded based on the values that were already present in *OKAYAMA-PROD*. However, since the required master data was not available during the initial PROD deployment, the Payment Terms were not reflected in the Wave-3 PROD environments.
*(2) Reason for differences across FDP environments (Wave-3 & Chugoku):*
 In the Shikoku and Wakayama PROD environments, hardcoded Payment Condition values already exist in the BIP configuration. Therefore, Payment Terms appear only in these specific FDP environments.
 In contrast, other FDPs i.e. *Iwate, Okinawa, and Chugoku,* do not have such hardcoded values, which results in the observed differences in Payment Term display across Wave-3 PROD environments.
*Fix and release plan:*
As discussed in the meeting, after the issue was fixed on UAT and since all the UAT environments are in sync now, we are planning to release the UAT changes to PROD on *29th November after business hours*.
Kindly review and approve the PROD release for the respective FDPs so that we can proceed with the changes to PROD on *29th November*.

Editing quantity directly in the Sales Order caused the part price to be set to null.
Quantity changes must be performed through the Quote, not the Sales Order.
Epic MFTBCFFR-3485 had made only body tab line-item quantity read-only; this incident required the same restriction for parts line items.
The parts line-item quantity field was made read-only in UAT-1 and deployed to FDP Production.
investigation_report.root_cause: A user edited the quantity of Part MK645741 directly in the Sales Order, causing its price to become null; BIP reports cannot process part line items with a null price.
investigation_report.resolution: Made the quantity field read-only for parts line items in the Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to FDP Production in the 26 November planned FDP release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: After SO Sales Posting, revising an NV/UV Quote to change the Customer Account created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV and omitted the Consumption Tax JV. The issue was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093. The logic was updated and validated on UAT1, then deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.
important_findings: The issue occurred when an NV/UV Quote was revised after SO Sales Posting and the Customer Account changed without a Sales Amount change.
Existing logic created revised Journal Voucher items only when the Sales Amount changed; otherwise, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.
The missing Consumption Tax JV was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093.
The same functionality and affected logic apply to UV and across all FDPs.
Past JVs have been affected because the logic has existed since FDP go-live.
investigation_report.root_cause: Existing revised Journal Voucher logic created Consumption Tax Journal entries only for Journal Voucher items with a Sales Amount change. When only the Customer Account or other non-amount values changed, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the logic to create the Consumption Tax Journal together with the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' Journal even when the Sales Amount is unchanged and fields such as Customer Account change. The fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.

Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue and would like to share our findings with you.
*Root Cause Analysis (RCA):*
 We have successfully replicated the issue on Parts Purchase Return Order *#N001300132* on *FDP-UAT1*.
 Our analysis showed that *Return Good Qty* and *Return Defective Qty* fields become editable when the shipment is processed using the *“Shipped”* button. As a result, users are able to modify these quantities even after the shipment is marked as shipped. This leads to the creation of incorrect actions and transactions for the line item.
*Fix Plan:*
 * We will make *Return Good Qty* and *Return Defective Qty* permanently *read-only*, regardless of shipment status.
 * We will fix this issue on *FDP-UAT1 by 18/11/2025 (EOD)*.
Please let us know if you have any questions or require further clarification.
Best Regards,
Abhinav

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In rare cases, Quote processing failed to calculate the 'Trade In Consumption Tax' after entering a Trade in Amount. Investigation identified a code-efficiency timing issue: the link updating the Quote could complete slower than the line-item tax update script, causing the update to break. The code was optimized with a more efficient link, validated on UAT-1, and released to FDP Production on 26-Nov-25.
important_findings: The issue affected calculation of 'Trade In Consumption Tax' in Quote in rare cases.
Entering a Trade in Amount triggers a tax update in the line item and a linked update in the Quote.
The Quote update failed when the link executed slower than the script; normally, the link completed faster.
The issue was not attributable to user mis-operation or functional mis-operation and could not be replicated.
A more efficient link was implemented to prevent the timing-related failure.
The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 26-Nov-25 planned release.
investigation_report.root_cause: A code-efficiency timing issue caused the link that updates the Quote to run slower than the line-item tax update script, breaking the update and preventing calculation of 'Trade In Consumption Tax'.
investigation_report.resolution: Optimized the code by replacing the link with a more efficient link; the fix was tested on UAT-1 and released to FDP Production on 26-Nov-25.

We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
This issue occurred due to a difference in the Model Codes.
 
The user initially created the Chassis Order B050208984 with the Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830, and the corresponding vehicle record was also created with this Model Code on 30 May 2025.
 
On 7 November 2025, a D21A file was received from TOB, containing the same Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830.
 
However, after the vehicle was created on 30 May 2025, the Model Code in the vehicle record was modified by user from FBA20B21W00F-5-G830 to FBA20B21W00F-4-G830.
 
Due to this mismatch, the current D21A ODI package identified the data as a new record and consequently created a new vehicle and a new chassis order B050481404, resulting in duplication in chassis order and recycle fee order and line items.
This is a case of User mis-operation where user updated the model code in vehicle due to which correct file with MC 5 created a duplicate order. 
Additionally, these type of cases will be handled by Vehicle cleansing CR. Since, recovery is completed and no further action is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this incident.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee order/line items were created when the D21A ODI package processed a TOB file whose Model Code did not match the Model Code stored in the Vehicle record. The affected data was recovered in production, including JV recovery and cancellation of duplicate Chassis Order B050481404. The evidence did not conclusively establish that a user changed the Model Code through the Administration Vehicle screen. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version and proposed for FDP after approval.
important_findings: Chassis Order B050208984 and its Vehicle record were initially created with Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830; the Vehicle record later contained FBA20B21W00F-4-G830.
A TOB D21A file received on 7 November 2025 contained Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830.

Because the D21A ODI package did not match the incoming Model Code to the Vehicle record, it treated the data as new and created duplicate Chassis Order B050481404, a new Vehicle, and duplicate recycle fee order and line items.
JV recovery was completed and the duplicate order was cancelled in the production environment; recycle fee attributes became visible after recovery.
The claimed user mis-operation through the Administration Vehicle screen was disputed and was not proven by the recorded last-updated user or replication results.

The SC-version fix matches the TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and updates the Vehicle Model Code from TOB; equivalent FDP implementation was pending approval.
investigation_report.root_cause: A Model Code mismatch between the incoming TOB D21A file/original Chassis Order Line Item (FBA20B21W00F-5-G830) and the Vehicle record (FBA20B21W00F-4-G830) caused the D21A ODI package to identify the data as new and create duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee records.
investigation_report.resolution: Completed JV recovery and cancelled duplicate Chassis Order B050481404 in production. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871; FDP implementation was proposed pending approval.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Bulk Invoice records for multiple shipments were missing from month-end closing files sent to KB, requiring recovery data to be manually created and transmitted. Investigation found that the post-extraction SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag by order number instead of shipment, causing all shipments under an order to be marked as sent when only one shipment was processed. The SQL was corrected in all production environments, impacted records were recovered, and subsequent December month-end Bulk Data verification found no issues.
important_findings: The issue affected Bulk Invoice data for shipments in FDPs including Okayama, Iwate, and Shikoku that were not included in closing data sent to KB.
After data extraction, an update SQL set the sent-to-KB flag based on the order number rather than the shipment.
When one shipment under an order was selected for KB processing, the SQL updated the flag for all shipments of that order.
Missing November 30 records had X_IF_STATUS set to Y before the SQL fix, causing them to be excluded from Bulk Invoice processing.
Recovery Bulk Invoice data was created and manually sent to KB for identified impacted records.
December month-end Bulk Data was verified and no further issue was found.
investigation_report.root_cause: The post-extraction update SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag, X_IF_STATUS, using the order number instead of the shipment, incorrectly marking all shipments for an order as sent to KB.
investigation_report.resolution: The SQL was corrected in all production environments to update flags by shipment, recovery Bulk Invoice data was generated and sent to KB for impacted records, and month-end Bulk Invoice executions were monitored through December.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A screen in JPN UAT8 failed because it is backed by a database view and JPN applications use SSO database logins. The SSO users lacked permission to access the view, causing an SQL error. Access was granted to the SSO users, and the screen became visible in JPN UAT8.
important_findings: The affected screen is based on a database view rather than a table.
ENU applications access the database directly, while JPN applications use SSO logins.
SSO users did not have access to the database view, resulting in an SQL error.
The issue was isolated to JPN UAT8 and did not occur in other UAT or Prod environments.
Granting the database-view access to SSO users restored screen visibility in JPN UAT8.
investigation_report.root_cause: SSO users used by JPN applications lacked permission to access the database view backing the affected screen.
investigation_report.resolution: Granted the database-view access to SSO users, making the screen visible in JPN UAT8 applications.

comments.author: Divyesh Ghiya
comments.text:
Thank you for your support.
We have thoroughly analyzed this issue, and our findings are as follows:
The user is creating an Insurance Order and then generating the Policy Number through the Ejibai interface. However, the Ejibai response is not being sent back to Siebel. Instead, the policy is created in Ejibai, and the user is manually updating the Liability Insurance Policy # field in the Insurance Order, as it is currently editable.
When the Policy Number is populated in the Insurance Order through the Ejibai response, the backend field User Key gets updated automatically. However, when the Policy Number is entered manually, the User Key remains null. Therefore, when that same policy is sent again from Ejibai to Siebel, the system does not find the original record (due to the missing User Key) and creates a duplicate order.
We successfully replicated this issue on UAT4 with the help of Gayatri-san. Please refer to the Insurance Order Q000037255 and its duplicate Q000037256.
Replication steps performed:
Step 1: Created an Insurance Order in Siebel and proceeded with policy creation on the Ejibai side.
Step 2: Manually updated the Liability Insurance Policy # in the Insurance Order instead of sending the response from the Ejibai interface.
Step 3: Sent the Policy Number again from Ejibai.
Conclusion:
This is not a system defect but a user mis-operation, where the Policy Number is being updated manually rather than being linked through the Ejibai interface. Kindly inform the user to avoid such manual updates to prevent duplication issues.
Since no further action is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this incident. Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate Insurance Orders were created when a Policy Number was manually entered in Siebel rather than returned through the Ejibai interface. Testing on UAT4 reproduced the behavior: manual entry left the backend User Key null, so a subsequent Ejibai policy response could not match the original record and created a duplicate. The issue was determined to be user mis-operation rather than a system defect; users should not manually update the policy number.
important_findings: Insurance Orders are created in Siebel and Policy Numbers are generated through the Ejibai interface.
When the Ejibai response populates the Policy Number, the backend User Key is updated automatically.
Manually updating the Liability Insurance Policy # leaves the User Key null.
A later Policy Number response from Ejibai cannot locate the original record without the User Key and creates a duplicate Insurance Order.
The issue was replicated on UAT4 using Insurance Order Q000037255 and duplicate Q000037256.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Liability Insurance Policy # was manually updated instead of being populated through the Ejibai interface, leaving the backend User Key null and preventing subsequent Ejibai responses from matching the original Insurance Order.
investigation_report.resolution: Instruct users to avoid manual updates to the Liability Insurance Policy # and allow the Ejibai interface response to populate the Policy Number and User Key.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An error occurred when Liability Insurance Information entered by the user did not match a Liability Insurance record in the master. The existing behavior could not resolve the insurance name and displayed an error instead of handling the unmatched master data as a zero-cost item. The fix was implemented in UAT-1 and released to Prod to create a zero-price Liability Insurance Quote Line Item when no matching master record exists.
important_findings: The entered liability insurance information was not maintained in the master for the applicable combination of MD Classification 'M', Insurance Vehicle Type 'Omnibus', and Mainland Category 'Mainland'.
Liability Insurance Term values 1 through 13 were identified as available for the applicable master-data combination.
The initial error message occurred because the system could not find the insurance name, rather than because no insurance information had been entered.
The required behavior was to retain the expense name and display a zero amount when master data does not match, consistent with Taxes and other expenses behavior.
The implemented fix creates a Liability Insurance record in the Quote Line Item with zero price when Liability Insurance is not maintained in the master.
The change was completed on UAT-1 and subsequently released to Prod.
investigation_report.root_cause: No Liability Insurance master record matched the user-entered Liability Insurance Information, and the existing logic treated the unresolved insurance name as an error instead of creating a zero-price item.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified the logic to create a dummy Liability Insurance in the Quote Line Item with zero price when no matching Liability Insurance master record is found; the change was tested on UAT-1 and released to Prod.

Thank you for your support and cooperation.
As per our discussion and demonstration in the meeting. We explained why the Order Detail BIP report failed to generate in case of Trailer & Forklift.
 *Issue* : Failure in generation of Order Detail BIP report.
 *Cause* : Tax rate was null in Sales Order as well as in Sales Quote. *Tax rate* is calculated on the basis of *Planned Delivery Date* in the sales quote which is then passed on to the Sales Order. In case of Trailer and Forklift, the validation on Planned Delivery Date is not present to get the Sales Quote approval due to which, the tax rate is not calculated *whenever the date field is left empty* in the sales quote. As a result null tax rate is passed on to the Sales Order causing the BIP to fail.
 We plan and hope to provide the fix by today EOD on UAT environment.
Best Regards,
 Saad

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Order Detail BIP report failed to generate for Trailer and Forklift sales orders. Investigation found that a missing Planned Delivery Date in the Sales Quote resulted in a null Tax rate being passed to the Sales Order. A fix was deployed to UAT1, approved for production, and released to Prod.
important_findings: The affected function was generation of the Order Detail BIP report.
Tax rate is calculated in the Sales Quote based on the Planned Delivery Date and is passed to the Sales Order.
Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes did not validate Planned Delivery Date before approval.
When Planned Delivery Date was empty, Tax rate remained null in both the Sales Quote and Sales Order.
The null Tax rate caused the BIP report generation failure.
The affected sales order was recovered, allowing BIP to be printed.
investigation_report.root_cause: Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes lacked Planned Delivery Date validation, allowing approval with an empty date. This prevented Tax rate calculation and passed a null Tax rate to the Sales Order, causing the Order Detail BIP report to fail.
investigation_report.resolution: A fix addressing the issue was deployed to UAT1 and then released to Prod after approval; the affected sales order was recovered so BIP could be printed.

comments.author: Soham
comments.text:
Thank you for your support.
*RCA*:
As discussed in the meeting, this issue occurred due to the execution of the file received for the Lubrication Master (i.e. MFTBCFFR - 4830) for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama. The file contained the value ‘N’ for the Generic Flag field. As a result, the pre-default logic in the Lubrication Master led to the 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field being set to ‘N’, since this value is directly derived from the Lubrication Master data.
For Dummy Lubrication Parts, the value of this flag should always be ‘Y’ in the master data.
The recovery has been completed, and we have reset the value of the Generic Flag back to ‘Y’.
*Countermeasure*:
As discussed, whenever the Lubrication Price Master data needs to be uploaded, we kindly request you to:
->Provide only the Price files if updates are required only for the lubrication pricing.
->Provide both Lubrication Master and Lubrication Price Master files if new lubrication data needs to be added in the FDPs.
Additionally, we will update our SOP to include a check for the Generic Flag value for dummy parts whenever a Lubrication Master file is received. We will also inform you in case any data update is required to maintain consistency across systems.
Since this was a data issue and not a system issue, please allow us to close this incident.
Please let us know in case of any queries.
Best Regards,
Soham

Hi Soham san,
Thank you for reporting the incident.
■We understand the root cause.
■The following information has been shared within the Service Team:
1. Changes to Price (List Price/Cost)
　Use "Lubricant Price Master".
2. Changes to Lubrication Master (additions or information changes)
　Use "SVC_LUBR_00_209".
　At this time, only provide the changed records.
3. MEMO
The Generic Flag of Dummy Parts # (...888888/...999999) is used for the default display of the Carry-in Flag.
As you commented, this issue is not a system issue, but rather due to incorrect master data settings.
Therefore, we will close this incident.
Thanks ！
Service Yoshihara

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field in WO was defaulting to 'N' for dummy lubrication parts in UAT-1. Investigation confirmed that the executed Lubrication Master file for MFTBCFFR - 4830 contained Generic Flag = 'N', which directly drove the field's pre-default value. The Generic Flag was reset to 'Y' for the dummy parts, and the issue was confirmed as incorrect master data rather than a system defect.
important_findings: The 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field is pre-defaulted from the Generic Flag in Lubrication Master data.
The default logic was the same in UAT and prod; the discrepancy between UAT-1 and UAT-8 was caused by master data values.
The Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama under MFTBCFFR - 4830 contained Generic Flag = 'N'.
For dummy lubrication parts ..888888 and ..999999, the Generic Flag must always be 'Y' to default the Carry-in Flag correctly.
Price-only updates must use Lubricant Price Master; Lubrication Master additions or information changes must use SVC_LUBR_00_209 with only changed records.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect master data: the Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama contained Generic Flag = 'N' for dummy lubrication parts, causing 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' to default to 'N'.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed by resetting the Generic Flag to 'Y' for the dummy lubrication parts. The SOP will be updated to validate the Generic Flag for dummy parts whenever a Lubrication Master file is received.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Retrofit order B050024442 could not progress from Ordered to Completed because Actual Completion Date 01 was not registered in the TOB Logistics Info tab. Investigation confirmed that TOB did not send the Actual Completion Date via the D21Z file. The order status was manually recovered to Completed, and no further action was required for this Jira.
important_findings: Actual Completion Date 01 is a mandatory condition for updating the order status.
The Actual Completion Date registered through D21Z files is displayed as Actual Completion Date 01 in the TOB Logistics Info tab.
Order B050024442 did not have an Actual Completion Date registered.
TOB confirmed that the Actual Completion Date was not sent for order B050024442.
The status was recovered by changing the order from Ordered to Completed.
investigation_report.root_cause: TOB did not send the Actual Completion Date for retrofit order B050024442 through the D21Z file, leaving Actual Completion Date 01 unregistered and preventing the status update.
investigation_report.resolution: Manually changed order B050024442 status from Ordered to Completed; the ticket was closed after TOB confirmed the missing Actual Completion Date transmission.

The same behavior occurred for both PO modification and PO cancellation scenarios.
The fix was deployed to UAT-1 and validated before release to Prod.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Power BI export failed for JPN when two columns had identical Japanese translations, producing duplicate alias names in the export query. important_findings: Two columns with the same Japanese translation generated the same alias name in the Power BI export query.
Duplicate column names made the export query invalid and caused the error: “File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.”
English Power BI exports handled duplicate aliases by appending suffixes such as _1 and _2.
For JPN, adding _2 to one duplicated field title prevented title duplication.
The fix was deployed to UAT and subsequently released to production.
investigation_report.root_cause: Duplicate Japanese translations caused two exported columns to receive the same alias name, resulting in an invalid Power BI export query with duplicate column names.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated one of the duplicate Japanese field titles by adding _2, then deployed the fix to UAT and production.
technical_entities: File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW", using Change Records to update Manual Discount% after selecting all quote line items with Ctrl+A changed the editable field initially clicked by the user. The behavior was reproduced in Service Quotes and parts quote and was identified as a Siebel Vanilla functionality defect rather than a business-process configuration issue. Users were instructed to initiate the operation from a read-only field or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.
important_findings: The issue occurred when a user clicked an editable field, selected all lines with Ctrl+A, and used Change Records to update Manual Discount%.
After confirming Change Records, the editable field initially selected in step 1 was changed.
The behavior was reproduced on Service Quotes and parts quote, including UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW".
The current business process configuration was confirmed to be correct.
Change Records is a Siebel Vanilla functionality, and the behavior was identified as a Siebel bug.
As a workaround, users should click a read-only field before using Ctrl+A and Change Records, or manually select records if the cursor is in an editable field.
investigation_report.root_cause: A Siebel bug in the vanilla Change Records functionality causes the initially selected editable field to be changed when all records are selected with Ctrl+A and a bulk update is performed.
investigation_report.resolution: Communicate the operational workaround to Hakodate branch users: start the Change Records operation from a read-only field, or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate JVs were created for D2S Invoice records with a blank PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) because the processing flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation. The flag-update logic was corrected and tested in UAT8 so PO-blank records are processed only once. The fix was deployed to Production in the 23rd October FDP release, and recovery data was completed for the affected duplicate JV records.
important_findings: JV creation is triggered when the D2S Invoice flag is not "S".
The existing flag-update logic required PO Num, Invoice Num, and Inv Dt to be non-null.
PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) being blank is normal for D2S invoices received by Siebel.
For PO-blank records, the flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation, allowing duplicate JVs to be created.
The issue affected three records on Chugoku.
Recovery was required for duplicate JV types D2S Inv Amt, D2S Inv CommFee, and D2S Inv CT.
investigation_report.root_cause: The flag-update filter required PO Num to be non-null. When PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) was blank, the D2S Invoice record was not updated to flag "S" after JV creation and was eligible for duplicate JV creation.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the flag-update logic so records with blank PO Num are updated to "S" after processing, tested the change in UAT8, and deployed it to Production in the 23rd October FDP release. Created and completed Production recovery data for the duplicate JVs.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Sales Order did not synchronize to the latest of 9 approved Quote revisions and remained at revision 7. Error logs showed a concurrent-update conflict during the Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization, and the scenario was reproduced in UAT by modifying the same Sales Order line item while synchronization was running. The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod; no system change was implemented, and the proposed prevention was to avoid concurrent updates to the same record.
important_findings: The Sales Order remained at revision 7 after 9 Quote revisions had been created and approved.
The failure occurred in step 'Sync Sales Order' using service 'EAI Siebel Adapter' and method 'Synchronize' with error SBL-BPR-00162.
Business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' failed in 'WriteRecord' with SBL-DAT-00523 and SBL-EAI-04451, indicating the record had been modified after retrieval.

The issue was reproduced in UAT when another user modified a Sales Order line item while Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization was running; the synchronization update succeeded and the manual update received the error.
The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod.
Regression testing in FDP did not reproduce the issue; SC UAT and FDP were identified as different applications.
investigation_report.root_cause: A concurrent update to the same Sales Order line-item record during Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization caused a Siebel record-update conflict, preventing the Sales Order from synchronizing to the latest Quote revision.
investigation_report.resolution: The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod. The proposed preventive measure was to instruct users not to update the same record simultaneously from different sessions or screens.
technical_entities: MF RF Order Entry - Line Items

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Journal Voucher ordering was investigated for records that were grouped in an unexpected sequence. When Timestamp and Global Order Number are identical, sorting falls back to Data Set Separator, which can produce this scenario. Configuration was confirmed identical across all FDPs, and the behavior was reproduced in UAT1 and UAT2; no recovery was required, and the scenario will be monitored through daily AMS monitoring.
important_findings: Journal Voucher sorting order is Timestamp > Global Order Number > Data Set Separator.
When Timestamp and Global Order Number are the same, grouping is determined by Data Set Separator.
The issue was initially observed for a small number of records in Okayama, but no Okayama-specific configuration discrepancy was found.
The scenario was reproduced in UAT1 and UAT2 and is possible for all FDPs.
Implementing a logic fix would require significant changes to the existing logic.
Recovery was not required for the affected orders; similar occurrences will be monitored and recovered if needed.
investigation_report.root_cause: A Journal Voucher sorting tie occurs when both Timestamp and Global Order Number are identical; sorting then uses Data Set Separator, resulting in the observed grouping sequence.
investigation_report.resolution: No recovery was performed because it was not required. The Jira was closed, and the scenario was added to daily AMS monitoring for detection and recovery of future occurrences.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Status Code values differed between SC and FDP because each environment sourced the value from a different table and represented a different status type. Changes were implemented and validated in FDP UAT, with the final Status Code LOV filter update deployed to production for Report #1-15A across all FDPs. Validation in PBI-PROD confirmed the change was correct and the incident was resolved.
important_findings: In FDP, Status Code is sourced from WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F and represents Order Status.
In SC, Status Code is sourced from W_SRVREQ_MD and represents Service Request Status.
The differing source tables caused different Status Code filter values between SC and FDP.
The Order Code LOV displayed correctly in FORCE FDP (UAT), but the line item Order Code (JC Status) was initially not displayed.
The requested LOV change for Report #1-05 was withdrawn because it was technically difficult.
The Status Code LOV for Report #1-15A was changed correctly for all FDPs in PBI-PROD.
investigation_report.root_cause: SC and FDP used different source tables for Status Code: WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F in FDP for Order Status and W_SRVREQ_MD in SC for Service Request Status.
investigation_report.resolution: Deployed the Status Code LOV filter change for Report #1-15A to production for all FDPs; the change was validated successfully in PBI-PROD.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Invoice data for Parts Purchase Order line items was not inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch when the D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file. The insertion logic was corrected on FDP-UAT1, including a filter-condition update for null X_ATTRIB_02 values, and was released to Production on 23rd October. Historical mismatch records were recovered across affected FDPs and their creation dates were aligned to the invoice-received date.
important_findings: D2S Invoice Mismatch excluded invoice data when D2S SO Item Number and Product values in a PO line item did not match the D2S invoice file.
A filter condition failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null, causing incorrect values to be selected for records with blank PO numbers.
After the fix, invoice data was inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch even when PO line items differed from the D2S Invoice file.
D2S Invoice Mismatch records are stored in CX_MISM_TOB / siebel.CX_MISM_TOB.
Recovery was required for mismatch records on Iwate, Aomori, Shikoku, and FDP Chugoku; recovered records had their creation dates updated to the invoice-received date.
Creation dates for invoice 8000115382 items 000010 and 000020 in siebel.CX_MISM_TOB were corrected to August 4, 2025 to match siebel.cx_d2s_recon.
investigation_report.root_cause: D2S Invoice Mismatch insertion logic excluded invoice data when PO line-item D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file; a related filter condition also failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the insertion and filter conditions on FDP-UAT1, released the fix to Production in the 23rd October scheduled FDP release, and recovered affected mismatch records with corrected creation dates.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The "Internal Order (Charge To)" field was not being updated correctly by the existing program, requiring recovery of affected Internal Orders. The issue had existed for an extended period and was not caused by a recent configuration change or release. The program was corrected, validated in FDP-UAT1/UAT-01, and deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
important_findings: Data recovery was required for Internal Orders, with September JC Create Date Required orders prioritized.

For TYPE "22: NV Modification (Transfer)" and "23: NV Stock Modification (Pool)", Internal Order (Charge To) had to be recovered as NV; for TYPE "26: UV Repair (Transfer)", it had to be recovered as SV.
The existing program was not working properly to update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field.
No configuration change was identified as the cause; the issue had existed since at least SR MFRBCFFR-1824.
Orders were prevented from proceeding with JCO when the field was not populated because a validation required the field before JCO.
The fix passed testing in UAT1 and was deployed to Production on 9th October.
investigation_report.root_cause: The existing program did not correctly update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field. The defect was longstanding and was not attributed to a recent configuration change or release.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered affected Internal Orders, updated the program that populates "Internal Order (Charge To)", validated the fix in FDP-UAT1/UAT-01, and deployed it to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

investigation_report.root_cause: Duplicate vehicle values for the registration fields used by Auto Vehicle caused a copied Job Card to update its Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id to a different vehicle, resulting in an incorrect Chassis#.

HelloPlease find the below mentioned details of the issue.
*1.Root Cause:*
Timeout parameter was changed from 1 hour to 2 hours, which led to extended user sessions during peak load, amplifying memory leaks in the system.
*2. Technical Observation:*
During peak traffic, prolonged sessions resulted in higher memory utilization and session retention at web layer.
*3. Oracle / Siebel Recommendation:*
As per Oracle and Siebel best practices, timeout synchronization between web and application layers must be maintained. Setting a long timeout value is not recommended due to possible performance impact.
*4. Action Taken:*
Timeout parameter was reverted from 2 hours back to 1 hour. Post-change, system stability was restored.
*5. Countermeasure / Preventive Action:*
For any future requirement to extend the session time, it is advised to increase the timeout parameter gradually (e.g., in 10-minute intervals) and monitor system stability after each change.
*6. Future Plan:*
If performance instability persists even after gradual adjustment, infrastructure-level tuning will be considered to ensure long-term system stability.
Thank you.
Please let us know in case of some further query.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: System instability during peak traffic was investigated and linked to a timeout parameter increase from 1 hour to 2 hours. The longer session duration increased session retention and memory utilization at the web layer, amplifying existing memory leaks. Reverting the timeout parameter to 1 hour restored system stability.
important_findings: The timeout parameter was changed from 1 hour to 2 hours before the instability occurred.
During peak traffic, prolonged sessions caused higher memory utilization and session retention at the web layer.
Extended sessions amplified memory leaks in the system.
Oracle and Siebel best practices recommend synchronizing timeout settings between web and application layers and avoiding long timeout values.
Reverting the timeout parameter from 2 hours to 1 hour restored stability.
Future timeout increases should be made gradually, such as in 10-minute intervals, with stability monitoring after each change.
investigation_report.root_cause: Changing the timeout parameter from 1 hour to 2 hours extended user sessions during peak load, increasing web-layer session retention and memory utilization and amplifying memory leaks.
investigation_report.resolution: Reverted the timeout parameter from 2 hours to 1 hour, restoring system stability.

Thanks for your support.
 We have thoroughly investigated and this issue is same as MFTBCFFR-4243.
 *User Steps:*
 In Revision 1, the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header was selected as “Y”.
 However in revision 2, user manually unchecked the flag, changing it to “N”.
 If a user intends to delete the Trade-In Assessment, the correct process is to delete the assessment record first and then uncheck the Trade-In flag.
 *RCA:*
 When the Trade-In flag is unchecked in the NV Quote header, the related Trade-In fields become read-only. This prevents deletion, as certain backend field updates required during deletion cannot occur in this state.
 *Recovery Plan:*
 No recovery action is required. The user can resolve the issue by rechecking the Trade-In flag to “Y”. This will allow deletion of the Trade-In Assessment as needed.
Conclusion:
 This is a case of user mis operation, not a system defect. Hence, kindly allow us to reject this incident.
 Please advise the user to follow the steps outlined above. Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
Regards,
 Atul Yadav

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident matched MFTBCFFR-4243 and involved a Trade-In Assessment that could not be deleted after the Trade-In Flag was manually changed from "Y" to "N" in NV Quote Header revision 2. Unchecking the flag makes related Trade-In fields read-only, preventing required backend updates during assessment deletion. The issue is resolved by rechecking the Trade-In Flag to "Y" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment.
important_findings: In revision 1, the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header was set to "Y".
In revision 2, the user manually unchecked the Trade-In Flag, changing it to "N".
When the Trade-In Flag is unchecked, related Trade-In fields become read-only.
Read-only Trade-In fields prevent backend field updates required to delete the Trade-In Assessment.
The correct process is to delete the Trade-In Assessment first, then uncheck the Trade-In Flag.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Trade-In Flag was changed to "N" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates required for deletion.
investigation_report.resolution: Recheck the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header to "Y", delete the Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.

Dear Tsunoda-san,
Thank you for your support.
Issue:
Previously, when the D21F file was processed multiple times for the same dealer, duplicate recycle fee orders were created for the same chassis order. The number of recycle fee orders generated matched the number of times the file was processed, resulting in duplicate recycle orders.
Fix Implemented:
We have updated the recycle fee order creation logic and with this enhancement, once a recycle fee order is created for a chassis order under a specific dealer code, subsequent processing of the same D21F file will no longer generate duplicate recycle fee orders.
Result:
Only one recycle fee order will be created for each chassis order, ensuring that duplicate recycle fee orders are no longer generated.
We kindly request your approval for the Fix plan.
Please let us know if any additional information is required from our side.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate recycle fee orders were repeatedly created when multiple D21F files were processed for the same chassis order. The investigation determined that the recycle fee order creation logic generated a new order for each D21F processing rather than updating an existing order. A logic enhancement was documented to prevent duplicate creation, but the timeline contains no confirmation that the fix was approved or that D21F content updates, such as amount changes, are handled.
important_findings: For C# number 610083, D21F files were received on February 7 and August 4 for the same Chassis Order.
SIEBEL created duplicate recycling orders when the same D21F file or multiple D21F files for the same chassis order were processed.
The number of recycle fee orders created matched the number of D21F processing occurrences.
Repeated operational recoveries removed duplicate orders and updated recycle status/order status to completed, but did not prevent recurrence.
A CR was planned to handle multiple D21F files for the same C# number, and duplicate recycle order checks were added to daily AMS monitoring across FDP production environments.

The proposed logic change prevents subsequent processing from creating another recycle fee order when one already exists for the chassis order and dealer code; handling of D21F updates such as amount changes was queried but not answered.
investigation_report.root_cause: The recycle fee order creation logic was not idempotent: it created a new recycle fee order each time D21F data was processed for the same chassis order instead of identifying and updating the existing order.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident was recovered in Wakayama-PROD. Investigation determined that D21F files could arrive before the corresponding D21A file creates the Chassis Order, due to a TOB-side file sequencing issue. Siebel cannot be modified to prevent this; the permanent correction must be implemented on the TOB side, while FDP records and TOB files are monitored and recovered as needed.
important_findings: Monitoring began on 11th July, but the affected record was created in June and was therefore not captured initially.
The issue is caused by TOB-side file sequencing: D21F is received before D21A creates the Chassis Order.
This is not a Siebel-side issue; a Siebel-side fix is not possible.
D21F files are monitored across FDP environments, and affected files are re-run after the required Chassis Order is created on the TOB side.
The incident is similar to SC Incident INC5105271 and MFTBCFFR-3546; future updates are tracked in MFTBCFFR-3546.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved UV Purchase Orders generating Journal Voucher department code "0000" instead of "TB". Investigation identified that migrated Assessment and Purchase Order records from SC had null X_ORDER_ID values, which triggered existing department-code logic; "MAP: Red Slip" also hardcodes the department code to "0000". Recovery data was prepared and discussed, but the incident was later reopened because root-cause and recovery work were still in progress.
important_findings: For "MAP: Red Slip", the department code is hardcoded to "0000" regardless of the salesperson's department.
For "PO - AP Posting UV Sales Order", the existing logic sets the department code to "0000" when "MF Sales Rep Branch Code" or X_ORDER_ID is null, "INTERNAL", or "Default Organization".
The affected Purchase Orders originated from Assessments migrated from SC, resulting in null X_ORDER_ID values.
The affected order had null "MF Sales Rep Branch Code" and X_ORDER_ID, causing "0000" to be populated in the Journal Voucher.
Recovery and reverse/recovery JV data were requested and prepared, but target recovery data and the recovery method remained under discussion.
The Jira was reopened because the team stated that root-cause investigation was still ongoing.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Button enablement in FDP used an RF status condition even though RF Status is not available in FDP, causing incorrect button behavior. The implementation was revised to control Send Recycle Fee, Modify/Change Order, and CUT/Cancel Order behavior using TOB and Recycle Fee Order statuses, including a one-day rule based on receipt of a successful TOB response. The final changes were tested in UAT1, approved for production, and released in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.
important_findings: The original button logic depended on RF STATUS = Null, but RF Status is not used in FDP.

The requested behavior was to make the Request for modification and CUT buttons unavailable from the day after a successful TOB response when the recycle order status is Completed or Recycle Order Changed.
The One Day Window requirement was corrected: CUT and Modify buttons must be enabled for the full day on which a successful TOB response is received, not the day the TOB request is sent.
For UAT1 verification, a TOB response was simulated for Chassis Order # B001217339 and Recycle Fee Order # B001217574; the record Last Modified date was used to identify the successful-response date.
The implementation also needed to preserve Send Recycle Fee availability after CUT success or a modification TOB error, rather than relying only on TOB response date and TOB status.
The incident was released to Production in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.
investigation_report.root_cause: Legacy RF STATUS-based button-enable conditions were retained although RF Status is not available in FDP, resulting in incorrect enablement control for the TOB-related buttons.
investigation_report.resolution: Reworked the FDP button-control logic to use TOB Status and Recycle Fee Order Status, with CUT and Modify enabled only on the date a successful TOB response is received; the finalized changes were released to Production on 23 October 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was replicated in the UAT1 environment for Sales Quote 1-6FHJ0C and Opportunity 1-6FHIYB. Investigation found that the Model Code had been manually removed from the Vehicle, preventing line-item creation in the UV Quote. The incident was classified as user misoperation rather than a system issue; the user was instructed to correct and re-map the Vehicle before recreating the Quote.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in the UAT1 environment.
Sales Quote 1-6FHJ0C and Opportunity 1-6FHIYB were used for investigation.
The Model Code was manually removed from the Vehicle.
Without a Model Code on the Vehicle, line items were not created in the UV Quote.
The corrective process is to delete the Vehicle from the UV Opportunity, add the appropriate Model Code, re-map the Vehicle, and create the Quote again.
The incident was determined to be user misoperation, not a system issue.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Model Code was manually removed from the Vehicle, causing UV Quote line items not to be created.
investigation_report.resolution: Delete the Vehicle from the UV Opportunity, add the appropriate Model Code to the Vehicle, re-map the Vehicle to the UV Opportunity, and create the Quote from the Opportunity again.
