investigation_report.investigation_summary: Zero-amount Journal Vouchers (JVs) were created because JV-creation filters did not consistently evaluate the same Base Amount fields used by the JV. In Okinawa prod, the fix from MFTBCFFR-3779 was ineffective for two Journal Event types because of an extra space in the deployed filter. The Okinawa fix was released on July 24, 2025, and the corrected filters for the remaining Journal Event types were validated in UAT/UAT1 and released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.
important_findings: Zero-amount JVs were found in FDP prod for multiple Journal Event types where the filter field differed from the JV Base Amount field.
The JV-creation filter is intended to prevent JV creation when Base Amount equals zero.

For Okinawa prod, the MFTBCFFR-3779 fix for "Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable" and "Service Correction Sales Amount Red Slip Non-Taxable" failed because of an extra space in the deployed filter.
The corrective logic uses the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount" and applies a "Base amount not equal to zero" condition.
The fix was validated in UAT1, where zero-amount JVs were no longer created.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect JV-creation filter configuration: filters used fields different from the JV Base Amount fields; additionally, an extra space in the deployed filter prevented the prior MFTBCFFR-3779 fix from working in Okinawa prod.
investigation_report.resolution: Released a corrected "Base amount not equal to zero" filter using the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount". The Okinawa prod correction was released on July 24, 2025, and changes for the remaining Journal Event types were released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.

Re-Edit Red Slip Job Card Sales Amount Non-Taxable
ConsTax PO - UV Body Building Order
ConsTax PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned differing workshop and department values across JC, JCO, and JV. Investigation confirmed that the values followed existing logic based on the branch code of the user who created the Job Card and the user who customer-approved the quote. The case was classified as a rare Operation Miss; no system changes or recovery were performed, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Workshop Code in JC reflects the Branch Code of the user who created the Job Card; it was 23 in this case.
JCO Workshop Name reflects the Branch Code of the user who Customer Approved the Quote; it was 21 in this case.
JV Department Code (CSJS200) and Department Code (CSJS300) come from the JCO Site, which was 21.
JVs had already been sent to KB.
The observed behavior was confirmed as current logic rather than a defect requiring a change.
The case was considered a rare Operation Miss, so no changes were made.
investigation_report.root_cause: A rare Operation Miss caused different branch-derived values to be used: JC used the Job Card creator's Branch Code (23), while JCO and JV used the Customer Approved Quote user's/JCO Site Branch Code (21).
investigation_report.resolution: No corrective system change was made. The incident was closed after confirming the existing logic and classifying the case as a rare Operation Miss.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned Entity Transfer behavior for Sales Rep transfers, particularly transfers within special sales. Multiple UAT issues were identified, including unavailable target users due to organization and position configuration, duplicate Position Id values, and incorrect user filtering. The final implementation restricts Sales Rep Transfer to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position, and was deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.
important_findings: Entity Transfer initially displayed only configured position types; requested additional position types were added to the Entity Transfer logic on UAT1.
A transfer between D0X20852 and D0X20851 was blocked because their primary organizations differed: D0X20852 was in Default Organization, 000000000O, while D0X20851 was in Okayama East Branch, 10.
A transfer did not reflect because both users had the same Position Id; the Position Id issue was corrected.
Person selection was unavailable for one Sales Order because no user was assigned to the current Sales Rep's position; the position was assigned to users.
The final Entity Transfer rule allows Sales Rep Transfer only to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position.
The self-approval validation was separately identified as introduced to FDP through CR-0836 and was removed from NV Quote on UAT1 for testing.
investigation_report.root_cause: Entity Transfer user-selection and transfer behavior did not meet the required special-sales transfer criteria; additional issues were caused by different user organizations, duplicate Position Id values, and missing user assignments for the current Sales Rep position.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated Entity Transfer to allow Sales Rep Transfer only among users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position; corrected duplicate Position Id configuration and assigned missing positions to users. The changes were deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Bulk invoice data was not sent on 30 June because the existing logic determines the send schedule from the closing date of the original account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order. The relevant account had a closing date of 20, so the data was scheduled for 20 July rather than 30 June. The behavior was confirmed as consistent with the current logic, and a change is being addressed through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.
important_findings: Recovery was completed and the data was linked to KB again.
Bulk invoice data is fetched using "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, which represents the original Account.
The closing date used for bulk invoice processing is taken from the account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code".
The original Account closing date was 20; therefore, data was expected to be sent on 20 July, not 30 June.
Current logic does not fetch bulk invoice data using the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code".
A logic change is being tracked under project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.
investigation_report.root_cause: The bulk invoice workflow uses the closing date of the original Account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, rather than the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code". Because that account's closing date was 20, the data was not scheduled to send on 30 June.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the incident data by linking it to KB again. The required logic change is being handled through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.

important_findings: UV Purchase Quote status could be manually updated from the "My Branch" view.
A status change from "Approved" to "Order Intake" was permitted, while reverting from "Order Intake" to "Approved" was not possible.
The one-way status transition blocked the business process.
Recovery for the affected record was completed.
The selected fix was to make the Purchase Quote Status field read-only.
The fix was implemented in UAT and released to Production on July 24.
investigation_report.root_cause: The UV Purchase Quote Status field was manually editable from the "My Branch" view, allowing an "Approved" to "Order Intake" transition that could not be reversed.
investigation_report.resolution: Made the Purchase Quote Status field read-only, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it to Production in the July 24 FDP regular release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate Journal Vouchers were created for Body Building Orders in FDP Production, including Chugoku prod. Investigation found that the validation introduced under MFTBCFFR-3809 checked only for an existing Completed JV trigger, allowing a second trigger while the original trigger was still in progress. The validation was updated and tested in UAT1, then released to FDP Production on 27th August.
important_findings: Affected duplicate Journal Vouchers were recovered using reverse Journal Vouchers and linked to KB through the daily batch.
The MFTBCFFR-3809 validation prevented new JV triggers only when a Completed trigger existed for the Body Building Order.
A duplicate Journal Voucher was created two minutes after the original because the original JV trigger had not yet reached Completed status.
The corrected validation prevents creation of another JV trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of status.
UAT testing confirmed that multiple Shipment Details responses from IBOS send the Journal Voucher trigger only once.
The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 27th August planned release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The validation check added by MFTBCFFR-3809 searched only for existing Completed JV triggers. When another trigger was received before the original trigger completed, the validation did not detect the in-progress trigger and created a duplicate Journal Voucher.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the JV-trigger validation to block creation of a new trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of trigger status. The fix was implemented in UAT1 and released to FDP Production on 27th August.

This is a case of user mis operation, not a system defect. Hence, kindly allow us to reject this incident.

Subsequently, in Revision 2 of the quote, the user updated the tax value for the same line item to ¥9,700. As a result, the tax value reflected in the Registration Request remains ¥8,600.
 
To correct this, the appropriate action would have been for the user to generate a new invoice(has to cancel the existing invoice) after updating the tax value in Revision 2 of the quote.
 
Please let us know if any further clarification is needed.
 
Best regards,
Ujjwal Goel

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned three tax amounts finalized through the Tax Finalize button not being reflected in the Sales Order Tax and Expenses amounts. Investigation established that Tax Finalize did not trigger tax-amount synchronization; synchronization occurred only when the "Actual amount including Tax" field was manually changed. A change was implemented and tested in UAT/UAT-1 to synchronize taxation line-item prices on tax finalization, then released to Prod.
important_findings: The issue was not caused by Quote revision or Registration Request creation timing; the reported issue was Sales Order values not updating after tax confirmation.
Three tax amounts are finalized by clicking the Tax Finalize button.
Before the fix, clicking Tax Finalize performed validations and froze values but did not synchronize the Tax Amount to the Sales Order.
Tax Amount synchronized only when the "Actual amount including Tax" field was manually changed.
A UAT test identified that after a Quote revision changed the three tax amounts, clicking Tax Finalize did not update the Sales Order Tax and Expenses amount.
The synchronization change was tested successfully in UAT-1 and released to Prod.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Tax Finalize button did not trigger synchronization of finalized Tax Amount values to the Sales Order; synchronization was only triggered by manual changes to the "Actual amount including Tax" field.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented synchronization so the taxation line-item price/finalized Tax Amount is synchronized to the Sales Order/Registration Request when Tax Finalize is performed. The change was tested in UAT/UAT-1 and released to Prod.

This caused values such as 0.5 to round to 1 in the invoice file's SMDO067 column, differing from Siebel UI logic. important_findings: The Customer Pay Amount rounding was missing at a required step in the batch logic used to fetch monthly invoice data.
Missing batch rounding caused 0.5 to be rounded to 1 during calculation.
The incorrect calculated value was populated in the SMDO067 column of the invoice file.
The corrected Monthly Invoice logic in UAT8 calculates rounding consistently with Siebel UI.
Bulk invoice data for May 2025 was recreated using the revised logic and approved for Prod release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The batch logic calculating Customer Pay Amount did not apply rounding at the required calculation step, causing incorrect Delta amount values in monthly invoice data.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Monthly Invoice batch logic in UAT8 to apply correct rounding consistent with Siebel UI; the fix was approved for deployment to Prod in the June 26 release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An Assessment Request with Assessment Purpose set to "User Purchase" could be directly mapped to an NV Quote as a Trade-in Vehicle, allowing a UV Purchase Order to be mapped to an NV Sales Order. The issue was replicated in UAT1 and the affected record was recovered. Validation was implemented for both NV Quote Trade-in and UV Quote Trade-in processes, validated in UAT, and released to Prod on July 24, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT1 using NV SO# A001295706, PO# F001295707, and AR# H000047991.
AR# H000047991 had Assessment Purpose "User Purchase" and could be selected as a Trade-in Vehicle on an NV Quote.
The unrestricted assessment mapping allowed a UV Purchase Order to be mapped to an NV Sales Order.
The affected production record was recovered.
A validation message was added to prevent selection of irrelevant trade-in vehicles in NV Quote Trade-in and UV Quote Trade-in processes.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PO allocation failures occurred in FDP Shikoku, Okayama, Aomori, and Chugoku for Parts Purchase Orders received from D2S; the issue was also observed in the SC version. Investigation determined that D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger for parts that had not been registered in order line items. Affected orders were recovered in the relevant production environments, and preventing recurrence requires order-line-item registration before cancellation.
important_findings: Current logic registers parts in order line items only when the received part is Norm(ZFTN) or Bans(ZFTS).
D2S sent ZFTX triggers directly to cancel parts that were not present in the order line items.
Cancellation and PO allocation failed because the target parts did not exist in the order line items.
The issue affected FDP and was also observed in the SC version.
Affected orders were recovered in FDP - PROD, FDPC - PROD, FDPA - PROD, and FDPO - PROD.
investigation_report.root_cause: D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger before the relevant part had been registered in the order line items. Since only Norm(ZFTN) and Bans(ZFTS) parts are registered under the current logic, the cancelled parts did not exist in the line items and could not be cancelled or allocated.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected orders in the applicable FDP production environments. To prevent recurrence, order line item registration must occur before the ZFTX cancellation trigger is processed.

Mr. Tsunoda
We apologize for keeping you waiting.
Below, we will inform you of the results of the investigation and our future response policy.
What is the problem?
 → IBOS's estimate response is not reflected.
 What is the cause?
 → This issue is due to the operation setting in the existing data map (backend) being set to "update". Since this setting only allows modification of existing records, no new bodywork records were created to be included in the IBOS response.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: IBOS estimate responses were not reflected because new body specification/bodywork records in the IBOS response were not created. The backend data map operation was configured as "update", which only modified existing records. The operation was changed to "upsert" in UAT so that existing records are updated and new records can be created; IBOS response testing and demonstration remained pending.
important_findings: The issue affected reflection of IBOS estimate responses for NV Body quotes.
The existing backend data map operation was set to "update", preventing creation of new body specification/bodywork records received from IBOS.
The configuration issue was associated with changes made when the Body Building sub-quote was removed from FDP.
Changing the data map operation to "upsert" allows both updates to existing records and creation of new records from the IBOS response.
The fix was reported as implemented and tested on UAT/UAT1, but end-to-end IBOS response testing was still pending.
Requested verification was to submit an NV quote with a body using "Submit to IBOS" and confirm that the IBOS quote response updates the relevant records.
investigation_report.root_cause: The backend data map operation was set to "update", which only updated existing records and prevented creation of new body specification/bodywork records included in IBOS estimate responses.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the backend data map operation from "update" to "upsert" in UAT/UAT1, enabling IBOS responses to update existing records and create new body specification/bodywork records as needed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Stock records were visible in SIEBEL/Siebel DB but missing from the PBI 5-02 report because they were excluded by ODI filtering conditions. The affected Shikoku parts were corrected by changing their item category to LUMF and creating/executing the required Price Master; recovery completed and the records became visible in PBI 5-02. For part #101244115, the remaining root cause was identified as an inventory update timestamp outside the effective date range of its price-list item.
important_findings: Shikoku Branch 42 parts HB06MS2, HB511, HD72T, HD72U, HD72V, and MB05A were present in SIEBEL but absent from PBI 5-02.
These parts were excluded from the PBI datamart by ODI because they failed the condition S_PRI_LST.SUBTYPE_CD = 'Parts Price List'.
The affected parts were incorrectly categorized as NORM instead of LUMF, so the expected LUMF price lists with List price and D/N price set to 0 had not been created.
After the item category was manually changed to LUMF, Price Master was created and executed, and the affected parts appeared in PBI 5-02.

Part #101244115 failed the ODI condition S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD BETWEEN S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_START_DT AND NVL(S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_END_DT,'31-12-9999') because its LAST_UPD timestamps were later than the configured EFF_END_DT of 2025-04-26.
investigation_report.root_cause: Invalid or missing price-list master data caused ODI exclusions: the affected parts were categorized as NORM rather than LUMF and lacked a 'Parts Price List'; for part #101244115, S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD was outside the S_PRI_LST_ITEM effective-date range.
investigation_report.resolution: Manually changed the affected parts' item category to LUMF, created and executed the Price Master, and completed recovery so the parts became visible in the PBI 5-02 report.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Journal Voucher data for Liability Insurance Orders was not sent to KB because the department code was null. Investigation found that migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), which resulted in missing department code in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher. The impacted orders were patched, recovery JVs were created, and recovery data was added to Prod for transmission to KB in the nightly batch.
important_findings: On 22 May, a Journal Voucher was created after spreadsheet approval but was not sent to KB because its department code was not set.
Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id).
A null Primary Position Id caused the department code to be null in both the Insurance Order and the Liability Insurance Journal Voucher.
Liability Insurance Orders with status "Spreadsheet Approved" were excluded from the recovery.
PR_POSTN_ID was patched by mapping the Sales Rep's Primary Position for the impacted Insurance orders.
Recovery JVs were created and added to Prod for delivery to KB in the nightly batch.
investigation_report.root_cause: Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), causing the department code to be null in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher and preventing JV data from being sent to KB.
investigation_report.resolution: Patched PR_POSTN_ID for impacted Liability Insurance Orders using the Sales Rep's Primary Position, created recovery JVs, and added the recovery data to Prod for transmission to KB.

Dear Tsunoda-san,
 Thank you for your continued support.
We have completed our analysis regarding the reported issue in the JIRA ticket. We successfully replicated the issue in the UAT environment using the reference record NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3, and confirmed that this is a case of user misoperation.
 Here are the steps the user followed that led to the issue:
 1.) In NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2, the user added a trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001601.
 2.) While creating Rev-3, the user removed the AR# from the trade-in vehicle line item and then deleted the record.
 3.) Subsequently, the user added a new trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001602.
As a result of this sequence, the asset_id in the trade-in line item was cleared, leading to the display of a blank line item in the NV Quote.
 To avoid this issue, we suggest the user to delete the existing trade-in line item entirely and then, create a new line item with the desired trade-in vehicle information or to change the AR# directly without erasing it.
Please feel free to contact us if you have any questions or need further assistance.
Best regards,
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A blank trade-in line item could be created in an NV Quote when the AR# was removed and the line item was saved during a quote revision. Replication in UAT confirmed that clearing the AR# cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id, resulting in the blank line item. A validation was implemented and tested in UAT to prevent saving a trade-in line item with a blank assessment number, then released to PROD on June 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT using NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3.
In NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2, removing AR#: H000001601 from a trade-in vehicle while creating Rev-3 and then deleting the record cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id.
A new trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001602 could then be added while the cleared asset_id caused a blank line item to display in the NV Quote.
The implemented validation prevents users from saving a trade-in line item when the AR# / assessment number is blank.
Users can still update the AR# through the standard process or delete the trade-in line item.
The UAT test record was UAT1, NV Quote #: 1-6AFG8S; the validation error message was changed to “Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.”
investigation_report.root_cause: The trade-in line item process allowed the AR# to be removed and the line item saved, which cleared asset_id and created a blank trade-in line item in the NV Quote.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented validation in UAT and released it to PROD on June 26, 2025, preventing a trade-in line item from being saved with a blank AR# / assessment number.
technical_entities: Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.

Thank you for your support.
We have analyszed this issue thorughly and below are our findings:
 On 6th February, User changed the closing of the mentioned account from 20 to EOM. 
Since, Bulk Invoice logic includes only 30 days of data, this data was not sent in February EOM. 
 These orders were supposed to be sent to KB on 20th closing, but user changed the closing from 20 to EOM. Now in Feb EOM, this data is supposed to be sent to KB but since Bulk Invoice logic only includes data of last 30 days, 20th Jan to 28th Jan data was not sent to KB. 
This is not a system bug, during initial development of the Bulk Invoice functionality, only 30 days range was included. There is a ongoing CR where we will change this range from 30 days to 60 days. By this CR, such cases will be avoided. 
Kindly verify our analysis and please let us know if you have any query or need any additional information.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: SV & PT Orders with Customer Code "0000328018" were omitted from the February EOM Bulk Invoice transfer to KB after the account closing was changed from 20 to EOM on 6 February. Bulk Invoice processing was limited to the last 30 days, excluding data from 20 January to 28 January. Recovery Bulk Invoice data was sent to the MDIS team, completing the recovery.
important_findings: Affected SV & PT Orders were I000012952, I000020814, and M000015656.
The account closing was changed from 20 to EOM on 6 February.
The orders were expected to be sent to KB on the 20th closing, but were instead deferred to the February EOM run.
Bulk Invoice logic included only the previous 30 days, so data from 20 January to 28 January was not sent to KB.
An ongoing CR will extend the Bulk Invoice range from 30 days to 60 days to prevent similar omissions.
investigation_report.root_cause: Bulk Invoice logic was designed to process only the last 30 days of data. Changing the account closing from 20 to EOM caused 20 January to 28 January data to fall outside the February EOM processing window.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery Bulk Invoice data was sent to the MDIS team for delivery to KB; all recoveries were completed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Journal events of type "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM" could generate an incorrect Department Code. Investigation found that the Department Code was sourced from the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator instead of the relevant inventory name. The mapping was corrected, released to Prod on 2 June 2025, and recovery JVs were completed for Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku.
important_findings: For "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM", Department Code was fetched from the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator.
The corrected logic uses the Purchase Return Order inventory name as the Department Code and uses the inventory name for "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" JV lines.
The fix was deployed to UAT1 for testing before Prod release.
Recovery required reverse JV and correct JV data with the correct JV_Department_Code.
Recovery was completed in Prod for Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku and linked to KB through the daily batch.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect Department Code mapping: the system used the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator rather than the applicable inventory name for "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM" journal events.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Department Code mapping to use inventory name, released the fix to Prod on 2 June 2025, and created reverse and corrective recovery JVs for affected orders in Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A mismatch in workshop codes between the Quote header and JCO header also affected billing bank account processing. Investigation found that the workshop name was mapped to different codes in the two headers. The Affiliated Location and Company Codes were corrected in the Production environment, and the scenario was replicated in UAT-4 for validation.
important_findings: The JCO header mapped the workshop name to Affiliated Location Code 05 for user D8SIBATM.
The Quote header mapped the workshop name to Affiliated Company Code 50.
The differing mappings caused a workshop-code mismatch between the Quote header and JCO header.
The issue also occurred for billing bank accounts.
Job Cards created after 19th May 2025 were no longer affected after the Production correction.
The scenario was replicated in UAT-4 using Job Card I000035340 and UID D0X20864.
investigation_report.root_cause: The workshop name was mapped differently between the JCO header and Quote header: Affiliated Location Code 05 on the JCO header versus Affiliated Company Code 50 on the Quote header.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the Affiliated Location and Company Codes in the Production environment; recoveries were completed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Statistics were not collected for tables in the Wakayama environment because the Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked tables below its configured data-volume cutoff. The affected tables were unlocked and statistics were gathered, resolving the incident on 19 May 2025 at 13:45 JST. As a permanent measure, Wakayama will use monthly manual statistics collection through DBMS statistics instead of coe_Siebel_stats.sql.
important_findings: coe_Siebel_stats.sql locks tables with fewer rows, preventing statistics collection for those tables.
The Wakayama tables had insufficient data volume to exceed the script cutoff value.
The cutoff value is defined by the Oracle-provided and recommended script and cannot be changed by the support team.
A similar issue occurred in the FDP Hakodate environment in February 2025.
Unlocking statistics on the affected tables followed by gathering statistics restored collection.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Affected Vehicle records displayed the Fuso Reception Number as the Chassis Number instead of the combination of Stamped Model Code and C# number, while C# was present. Initial analysis attributed unprocessed D21G files to exhausted ODI database storage, but later analysis attributed the condition to SC-to-FDP Chugoku data migration; both explanations were challenged because affected chassis numbers were confirmed after transfer. Records were repeatedly recovered, including recurrence A050266885, but the timeline does not establish a validated root cause or confirmed permanent fix.
important_findings: The reported symptom was that the Chassis Number remained the Fuso Reception Number while C# was displayed; the expected Chassis Number format was Stamped Model Code plus C# number.
An initial finding stated that ODI database storage reached its limit, preventing D21G file execution and VIN updates; an incremental ODI storage expansion mechanism was reportedly implemented.
A later comparison of FDP Chugoku Vehicle Data with SC Production identified records where Fuso Reception Number was used as Chassis Number despite non-null Stamped Model Code and C# number.
The issue recurred for record A050266885 on 2025-08-06 and the record was manually recovered.

Support repeatedly classified the issue as SC-to-FDP Chugoku migrated data, but this was disputed because chassis-number confirmation occurs after transfer and affected May 2025 chassis were reported.
Affected Vehicle records were recovered, but the requester continued to request confirmation of the corrective action and completion date.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The March 31 Bulk Invoice file from Cubastion showed that all referenced JCs were successfully sent from Siebel to KB, so the Bulk Invoice process was operating normally. The investigation identified that the Account master linkage from Siebel to KB had been intentionally suspended for all accounts in Shikoku Production pending deployment of the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR. KB was performing manual recovery while the interface remained suspended, and the incident was closed as not being a system issue.
important_findings: All referenced JCs were included in the March EOM (March 31) Bulk Invoice file and were successfully sent to KB.
Siebel sends Bulk Invoice data to KB; no information was available regarding CSS Invoice processing.
MFTBCFFR-3040 addressed incorrect mapping in some Account master data columns sent to KB; the incident fix was deployed to all FDP environments.
A further CR requested after MFTBCFFR-3040 remained pending for Production deployment.
Under MFTBCFFR-3149, the complete Account master interface was stopped in Shikoku Production for all accounts, not only specific account codes.
Account code 1000007404, created in April, was not sent to KB because Account master bulk processing had been stopped before April.
investigation_report.root_cause: The complete Account master linkage from Siebel to KB was intentionally suspended in Shikoku Production at Miyauchi's request until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is deployed to Production.
investigation_report.resolution: KB performed manual recovery while the Account master linkage remained suspended pending CR development and Production deployment; the incident was closed as not being a system issue.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In a Payer Change Order, changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh the Closed Date from the newly selected payer. The retained old Closed Date prevented the change order from being processed at EOM (31 March), and the JC lines and change order lines were instead sent to KB on 20 April. The issue was identified as similar to MFTBCFFR-3672 and was tracked through that incident.
important_findings: Bill to Basic Account and Ship to basic account values are initially fetched from JCO when a Payer Change Order is created.
Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account should update Closed Date and Payment term based on the new payer.
Closed Date retained its previous value after the payer change and was not updated to EOM (31 March).
K000076384 was output in billing data on 20 April rather than at the end of March.
The issue was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3672.
investigation_report.root_cause: Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not update the Closed Date value in the Payer Change Order, leaving the previous date and preventing EOM processing.

important_findings: D8NOOSHI created Job Cards with a Branch CS Staff position, but the department code was not fetched correctly.
The Employee master had department code 0108 assigned to the Branch CS Staff position; 0108 is a Headquarter department code.
The incorrect Employee master department assignment caused the Branch CS Staff position to be created with an HQ department and caused the Journal Voucher to fail.
After correcting D8NOOSHI's Employee master department code, the correct department code was populated in Journal Vouchers.
Okinawa Prod Job Card I000035491, created by D8NOOSHI and closed on 2025/05/30 10:56:21 AM, confirmed the corrected Journal Voucher department code.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect Employee master data assigned Headquarter department code 0108 to employee D8NOOSHI's Branch CS Staff position.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the Employee master department code for D8NOOSHI; Journal Vouchers subsequently populated the correct department code.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned activity status changes in the UI and the relationship between Activity status and Job Card (JC) status. Investigation confirmed that users could manually perform all standard Activity status transitions. A fix was implemented so that closing a JC automatically sets the Activity status to "Work Completed" and makes it read-only; it was validated in UAT 1 and released to production on 26 May 2025.
important_findings: The standard Activity status flow is "Open" → "Request for Reservation" → "Reservation Confirmed" → "Work Completed" → "Closed".
Users were able to manually change Activity status through the UI, including all standard transitions.
When Job Card (JC) status is set to "Closed", the fix updates the Activity status to "Work Completed" regardless of its prior status.
After an Activity status is updated to "Work Completed", the status becomes read-only and cannot be manually modified.
The fix was implemented and validated in UAT 1 before release to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: The UI allowed users to manually modify Activity status, and Activity status was not automatically set to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) status was set to "Closed".
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented automatic Activity status update to "Work Completed" when JC status is set to "Closed", regardless of previous Activity status, and made the Activity status read-only after that update. The fix was validated in UAT 1 and released to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Profit values differed between Sales Quote, Sales Order, and Power BI in PROD. Investigation identified synchronization discrepancies between quote and order records, including mismatched product_id values between order_item and corresponding quote_item and line-item count mismatches. Manual data patching was completed in Siebel for affected production records, but a Power BI mismatch remained for AR# H000001001 and PBI-side validation was still in progress.
important_findings: Some production records had mismatched product_id values between order_item and the corresponding quote_item.
The affected records were attributed to synchronization discrepancies between quotes and orders.
Line-item count mismatches were identified for 91 records in Chugoku Prod and 1 record in Okayama Prod.
Manual data patching was completed in Siebel, and Sales Profit for UV Sales Orders was confirmed synchronized with the respective UV Sales Quotes.
Power BI still showed an unmatched value for AR# H000001001: Sales Quote and Sales Order were 1,105,936, while PBI was 1,107,086.
The Power BI display was also reported to be missing comma thousand separators.
investigation_report.root_cause: Synchronization discrepancies between quote and order records, including mismatched product_id values and line-item count mismatches.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Invoice CustomerName mapping was reviewed because it was selecting different customer sources based on the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header. An interim UAT-1 change mapped CustomerName to Prospect Account Name when the flag was Y, but the final validated requirement was to always use Ship To Customer Name. The final mapping was approved for PROD deployment, with release planned for 14 May.
important_findings: The original CustomerName logic used Vehicle Owner Name when Cash Receipt Flag was Y and Ship To Customer Name when it was N.
An interim FDP UAT-1 change mapped CustomerName to Prospect Account Name when Cash Receipt Flag was Y.
The final FDP UAT-1 mapping sets CustomerName from Ship To Customer Name regardless of the Cash Receipt Flag value.
Validation confirmed CustomerName uses the JC customer even when the Vehicle Owner in the vehicle master differs from the JC customer.
The final Xlms value was validated and approved for PROD deployment.
investigation_report.root_cause: CustomerName was mapped conditionally to Vehicle Owner Name or other sources based on the Cash Receipt Flag, instead of consistently using Ship To Customer Name.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the CustomerName tag mapping in FDP UAT-1 to use Ship To Customer Name regardless of Cash Receipt Flag, validated the results, and approved the change for PROD release on 14 May.

san,
Thank you for your support.
We have analysed this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
While creating Journal voucher line, system checks whether the amount is equal to zero or not. Since, we do not create zero amount JV, we have added a search specification which check if the tax amount is equal to zero or not. If the tax amount is equal to zero then JV line is not created. Hence, no JV line was created for "Job Card Sales CT" Journal event.

The same issue affected other FDPs and the release was planned for all FDPs.
UAT-1 validation confirmed that the error no longer occurred before production approval.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: JCO Payment Term values were affected when Payer Basic Account Code did not align with the Bill To account after account changes. Investigation confirmed that Payment Term and Payer Basic Account Code are populated from the Bill To Basic Account Code in the JC Header. The mapping was corrected so Payer and Sold To values synchronize with Bill To, validated in FDP UAT-1, and released to PROD.
important_findings: Payment Term and Payer Basic Account Code are populated based on the Bill To Basic Account Code selected in the JC Header.
JCOs with missing Payment Term had a different Payer Basic Account Code than JCOs without the issue.
If the Payer Account Code is invalid, Payment Term can be blank because the value cannot be referenced from Account Code (AR).
Payer Code and Name are sourced from Bill To Customer.
All Sold To values also needed to be mapped to Bill To because Sold To fields are hidden in the FDP version.
The fix could not be reproduced in UAT after deployment and was released to PROD on 26 June.
investigation_report.root_cause: Payer Basic Account Code and Sold To values were not consistently mapped/synchronized to the Bill To account in the JC, causing Payment Term lookup failures when the Payer Account Code differed from or was invalid for the Bill To account.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the FDP UAT-1 mapping so Payer To and Sold To values synchronize with Bill To of the JC; the validated fix was released to PROD on 26 June.
technical_entities: Payer Mapping Change(Bill To Customer Code).xlsx

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Individual invoice generation failed for JCO# I050019559 because the Branch Code used for issuance did not match the creator's Primary Branch Code. The behavior was confirmed as consistent with current functionality and similar to MFTBCFFR-3534. The incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
important_findings: JCO# I050019559 was created by user D8TKANEM.
The creator's Primary Branch Code was UG.
Individual invoice issuance used Branch Code 7331, mapped to UF, which did not match UG.
The Branch Code mismatch caused individual invoice generation to fail.
A blank Closed Date does not affect individual invoice issuance.
The behavior is consistent with current functionality and similar to MFTBCFFR-3534.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Branch Code used to generate the individual invoice (7331 → UF) did not match the JCO creator's Primary Branch Code (UG).
investigation_report.resolution: No system change was made; the incident was rejected because the behavior was working as per current functionality.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate journal vouchers (JVs) were created when IBOS returned duplicate responses for a single record. Affected JVs were recovered using reverse JVs, with daily monitoring in Chugoku until a permanent fix was deployed. The fix was deployed and tested in UAT-01, where JVs were created only once, and was released to PROD through an emergency release on May 19.
important_findings: Duplicate responses from the IBOS system for a single record caused duplicate journal vouchers (JVs) to be created.
Affected duplicate JVs were corrected by creating reverse JVs.
Daily monitoring was performed in the Chugoku environment, with duplicate JVs removed before the daily night batch when detected.
The fix was deployed to UAT-01 and testing showed that a JV was created only once.
The production fix was released through an emergency release completed on May 19.
investigation_report.root_cause: IBOS returned duplicate responses for a single record, resulting in duplicate JV creation.
investigation_report.resolution: A fix was deployed and validated in UAT-01, then released to PROD through an emergency release on May 19. Duplicate JV records were recovered using reverse JVs while daily monitoring continued until the permanent fix was deployed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: During migration to FDP-Chugoku, duplicate vehicle records with the same VIN/Fuso Reception Number caused the first matching vehicle to be mapped to Purchase Orders instead of the correct vehicle. The incorrect mapping to Chassis Orders prevented creation of Recycle Fee Orders and Pool Cost Orders. Recovery required correcting vehicle mappings, executing TOB files, restoring related Chassis, Sales, and Body Orders, and resolving a duplicate recycle fee order; final verification reported no further recovery required.
important_findings: SC data was confirmed correct; the issue occurred during migration to FDP-Chugoku.
Serial numbers were identified from Purchase Orders, and duplicate vehicle data caused the first vehicle with the same VIN to be selected regardless of SC data.
Incorrect vehicle-to-Chassis Order mapping resulted in missing Recycle Fee Orders and Pool Cost Orders.
Recovery initially updated only Chassis Orders; affected Sales Orders and Body Orders also required recovery.
A remaining record had conflicting model codes FK62FK4J, FQ62FU6B, and FK65FK4, with product code 012 identified as invalid/garbage data.
A duplicate recycle fee order was identified and recovered.
investigation_report.root_cause: A data-migration matching issue: duplicate vehicle records with the same VIN/Fuso Reception Number caused the first matching vehicle to be linked to Purchase Orders and Chassis Orders instead of the correct vehicle.
investigation_report.resolution: Correct vehicle records were re-linked to affected Chassis Orders, TOB files were executed, related Sales Orders and Body Orders were recovered, and the duplicate recycle fee order was recovered. The recovered records were subsequently verified and reported as requiring no further recovery.

Because the Journal Voucher Department Code is derived from the Branch Code, it was blank. Recovery was completed by setting Branch Code to 10, and the user was to update the employee master.
important_findings: User D8NOOSHI is part of the Headquarter division and did not have a Branch Code.
The Journal Voucher Department Code is populated from the Branch Code.

Recovery was performed by setting Branch Code to 10 for the affected records.
The issue was determined not to be a system issue; the employee master required updating.
investigation_report.root_cause: User D8NOOSHI's employee master did not contain a Branch Code because the user belongs to the Headquarter division, resulting in a blank Journal Voucher Department Code derived from that Branch Code.
investigation_report.resolution: Set Branch Code to 10 for the affected records and update the user's employee master.

Thank you for your continued support.
We have checked the issue and found the following:
RCA: The JV for Chassis Orders is created by a Siebel Job that filter orders based on Status and Batch RF Status.
The conditions used to filter the orders are:
Status = 'Shipment Instructed'
Batch RF Status in ("Send Shipment to RF", "Send Create to RF", "")
Since the orders migrated from SC to Chugoku had Batch RF Status 'Sent to Create RF', these orders were not picked up when the Siebel Job was executed.
We have attached the list of migrated Chassis Orders along with their current status in Chugoku Production.
We will recover all the listed orders. However, as per the current logic, JV will only be created for orders with Status = 'Shipment Instructed'.
For the others, the JV will be created automatically once their status is updated to 'Shipment Instructed'.
Best Regards,
Shivam

JV creation under the existing logic applies only to orders with Status = "Shipment Instructed".
investigation_report.root_cause: Migrated Chassis Orders from SC to Chugoku Production had Batch RF Status "Sent to Create RF", which did not match the Siebel Job filter values for JV creation.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders. Remaining orders will generate JVs automatically after their status is updated to "Shipment Instructed".

comments.author: Soham Modi
comments.text:
Thanks for your support.
Regarding this issue, when Siebel sends a request to the TOB system, we have observed scenarios where TOB does not return a response.
In the normal process flow, TOB does not accept triggers from the Siebel side after 5:00 PM JST. If a trigger is sent to TOB after 5:00 PM JST and not accepted by TOB then the corresponding records fail in the asynchronous transaction on the Siebel side. Subsequently, a Siebel batch job runs on the next day and reprocesses all failed records by resending them to TOB.
However, in this particular case, the request was accepted by TOB, and no response was received from the TOB side. As a result, the record was not identified as failed on the Siebel side and therefore was not retriggered by the batch job on the next morning as expected.
Kindly review the above and let us know the next action required from the Cubastion side.
Please let us know in case of any queries or if any additional information is required from our side.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

investigation_report.investigation_summary: TOB transmissions triggered after 5:00 PM JST could receive no TOB response, preventing Siebel from identifying the asynchronous transaction as failed and retrying it the following morning. The issue was observed across multiple FDP records and had a similar incident in SC. A countermeasure was developed in UAT1 to retrigger records with completed interfaces but no TOB response, but no completed UAT, production deployment, or final resolution was confirmed.
important_findings: Normally, TOB triggers sent after 5:00 PM JST are not accepted and result in a Siebel asynchronous-transaction failure.
For affected records, TOB did not return a response, so Siebel did not mark the record as failed and the next-day batch job did not retrigger it.
The behavior was observed across multiple records in all FDP environments and was also associated with an incident in SC: INC4990796.
The proposed countermeasure is to retrigger records for which the interface is completed but no TOB response is received.
The retrigger logic must avoid resubmission on days when TOB is not open, such as Sundays.
Development of the proposed fix was completed in UAT1, but UAT completion and deployment were not confirmed.
investigation_report.root_cause: TOB did not return a response for requests triggered after 5:00 PM JST. As a result, Siebel did not classify the asynchronous transaction as failed, so its next-day batch job did not resend the affected records.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved Journal Vector (JV) creating non-taxable line items when the related Sales Price was "0", including after Change Order processing. Initial UAT1 fixes addressed re-edit and Price Change scenarios, but validation found the issue persisted for Payer Change and Price and Payer Change scenarios. The additional fix was validated in UAT-1, and the incident was deployed to PROD on 12 June 2025.
important_findings: For taxable Account Codes, all line items are taxable, but Change Order (Price Change) could generate Non-Tax Line Items with a value of "Zero" in the Journal Vector.
The initial UAT1 correction passed JC Close, JC Close And Re-Edit, and JC Close And Change Order (Price Change) scenarios for both Tax and Non-Tax cases.
UAT-1 validation found [Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable] line items were still created when Sales Price was "0" for Payer Change and Price and Payer Change scenarios.
After the follow-up fix, Payer Change scenarios no longer created a JV line item when Sales Price was "0".
UAT was completed and the fix was released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: The zero-value line-item suppression did not cover Change Order workflows involving Payer Change or Price and Payer Change, allowing [Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable] JV line items to be created when Sales Price was "0".
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the UAT1/UAT-1 fix to suppress JV line-item creation for zero Sales Price in Payer Change scenarios; the correction was validated in UAT and deployed to PROD on 12 June 2025.

PO F000072028 was linked to item #1 and had reached the "Acceptance Verification Done" status, preventing creation of another PO. The incident was classified as user mis-operation and rejected.
important_findings: The "Create PO" button is intended to become active after sales are recorded for specified sales positions.
A PO already existed for item #1: F000072028.
The user manually corrected the bodywork unit price while processing PO F000072028.
PO F000072028 was linked to item #1 and had status "Acceptance Verification Done", which prevented creation of a new PO for that item.
The required corrective action was to cancel the existing PO before creating a new PO.
investigation_report.root_cause: User mis-operation: an existing PO, F000072028, was already linked to item #1 and was in "Acceptance Verification Done" status, preventing a new PO from being created.
investigation_report.resolution: Cancel existing PO F000072028 and then create a new PO for item #1.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Chassis Price was not displayed in Aomori Production while pricing was available in UAT2. Investigation confirmed that the affected Production pricing/master data was absent because the final Production model-code file did not include the required model code. The affected Production record was recovered and a file was executed to align Production pricing with UAT; subsequent UAT2 alignment with Production was identified as requiring a separate SR.
important_findings: The initial issue was caused by the absence of the Price Master for the affected Chassis in Aomori Prod.
The affected Production record was recovered; model code FED90K74S00H could not be found in the files previously executed on Aomori Prod.
The January 2024 UAT setup file included model code FED90G73S00H, but the final Production file shared in July 2024 did not include it.
The file executed in Aomori Production through SR MFTBCFFR-3780 contained updated model-code pricing, creating a pricing difference with UAT2.
Production setup files were agreed to be applied only to Production; applying them to UAT requires a separate service request.
investigation_report.root_cause: The final model-code file supplied for the Aomori Production setup did not include the required model code/pricing data, while the earlier UAT setup file did.
investigation_report.resolution: The affected Aomori Production record was recovered and the relevant file was executed, aligning Production model-code pricing with UAT. Any subsequent UAT2 update to match Production was to be requested through a separate SR.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Invoice CustomerName population was investigated for Job Cards where the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header is Y. The expected source was the Vehicle Owner Name, but the invoice mapping referenced a different field. The mapping was corrected in FDP UAT-1, approved for production, and released on April 24.
important_findings: For Cash Receipt Flag = Y on the JC Header, Invoice CustomerName must be populated from the Vehicle Owner Name.
For Cash Receipt Flag = N, Invoice CustomerName is populated from the Ship To Customer Name.
The existing mapping for Cash Receipt Flag = Y was mapped to a different field instead of Vehicle Owner Name.
The corrected mapping was validated in FDP UAT-1 using JC# I001293791.
The approved mapping change was released to the production environment on April 24.
investigation_report.root_cause: For Job Cards with Cash Receipt Flag = Y, the Invoice CustomerName mapping referenced an incorrect field rather than the Vehicle Owner Name.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the Invoice CustomerName mapping to use the correct Vehicle Owner Name field when the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header is Y, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to production on April 24.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Orders were created without line items when the Material master file from D2S contained an unusually high record count. Processing of the file was delayed, and the order-creation job executed before all parts had been released to siebel. The teams discussed a workaround with IT and D2S, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: The Material master file from D2S contained 82,876 records.
The increased Material master file volume caused the package execution to take longer.
The order-creation job ran before all parts were released to siebel.
The issue occurs when a high number of Material master records are sent from D2S.
investigation_report.root_cause: A high-volume Material master file from D2S delayed package processing, allowing the order-creation job to run before all parts were released to siebel, resulting in orders without line items.
investigation_report.resolution: A workaround was discussed with the IT team and D2S team; no specific corrective action was documented.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Commission fee and tax calculations were triggered when "Create Spreadsheet" was selected for a Liability Order. The button could be enabled through the Clerical Error workflow before "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" had a valid value, creating incorrect commission details. The enablement logic was updated in UAT, recovery JVs were processed and linked to KB, and the fix was released to production on April 24.
important_findings: Commission calculation occurs when the "Create Spreadsheet" button is clicked within an order.
"Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" is populated when "Liability Insurance Policy #" is entered on the order.
The issue was reproduced on UAT8 using liability order Q050023214 by setting the order to "Liability Clerical Error", clearing the Clerical error flag, and then creating a Liability Spreadsheet.
The "Create Spreadsheet" button was enabled without requiring a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date".
Recovery required creation of Reverse JV and Correctr JV with the posting date set to the current date; the JVs were linked to KB through the nightly batch.
"Create Spreadsheet" is visible only in the My Branch and All Insurance Orders views under Liability Order, and testing used user D0X20922.
investigation_report.root_cause: The "Create Spreadsheet" button could be enabled through the "Liability Clerical Error" workflow while "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" was not valid, allowing commission calculation to run with incomplete order data.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the "Create Spreadsheet" enablement condition to require a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date". The fix was validated in UAT, recovery Reverse JV and Correctr JV entries were linked to KB, and the change was deployed to production in the April 24 scheduled release.
technical_entities: Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date

Dear Shiromoto San,
Thank you for your support.
*RCA*: 
In the Power BI report, the field X_REPAIR_COST has a null value in both the Warehouse DB and Siebel DB for AR# H000109757.
Since X_REPAIR_COST is aggregated using SUM, Power BI automatically ignores null values instead of treating them as zero. As a result, AR# H000109757 does not contribute to the total sum and does not appear in visuals that display only aggregated results.
Additionally, there are multiple ARs where X_REPAIR_COST is null.
*Fix*: To address this issue, we have two possible solutions:
1. Modify the logic in ODI to convert null values of X_REPAIR_COST to 0 before loading the data.
2. Modify the logic in Power BI to handle null values appropriately.
We will finalize and implement the appropriate solution, and in the meantime, we will manually recover these records after business hours today.
Regards,
Sheetal

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Profit values in the UV Report (2-06 - Used car details (profit and loss)) did not consistently match Siebel. The investigation identified an inconsistency in the profit calculation formula, and corrected logic was deployed to UAT and then all FDP Prod environments. A remaining discrepancy in FDP Iwate showed that PBI 2-06 Report Profit still differed from Siebel Sales Quote and Order Profit due to rounding/overall-profit logic requiring further change.
important_findings: The profit calculation formula contained an inconsistency that caused UV Report profit values to differ from Siebel.
Corrected profit logic was deployed to UAT Okayama and verified against Siebel UAT1, except for identified garbage-data orders E001192564, E001261152, and E001187324.
FDP UAT1 SO# E001294027 was reported as an additional profit mismatch after the initial UAT release.
The corrected logic was released to all FDP Prod environments, but FDP Iwate AR# H000003201 still showed PBI 2-06 Report Profit 1020811.90 versus Siebel Sales Quote and Order Profit 1,020,813.
Logic similar to the SC Power BI 2-06 report was implemented, but additional logic changes were required to round the overall profit and align all profit values.
Further corrective work was requested through an AMS CR; the timeline does not confirm that the remaining discrepancies were resolved.
investigation_report.root_cause: An inconsistency in the profit calculation formula, with remaining mismatches requiring additional overall-profit rounding logic.

important_findings: Some JVs were not created, causing an amount gap.
The issue occurred for Color records and affected records on multiple FDPs.
The defect specifically prevented JV creation for line type "4".
Target recovery data was prepared to create JVs that had not been created earlier.
Sample January TOB Invoice data from Shikoku and March TOB Invoice data from Chugoku were used for UAT8 verification.
JV creation was confirmed on UAT8 before release to Production.
investigation_report.root_cause: A defect affecting Color records prevented Journal Voucher (JV) creation for line type "4".

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A sales report associated with sales order A000023860 was reported as not sent to TOB after recycling, causing sales-result discrepancies. Investigation confirmed that the DJ2L transaction from Siebel on 28/March/2025 had a TOB error response and that the record existed in both JMS logs and the TOB Request/Response Screen; the unresolved concern was why it was not displayed when filtering by Interface ID DJ2L.
important_findings: Sales order A000023860 sent DJ2L from Siebel on 28/March/2025 and received an error response from TOB.
The displayed error response was identified as an error during recycling send/receive processing.
The sales report sent after recycling was reported as not TOB-sent, causing sales results not to match.
The relevant record was confirmed in both JMS logs and the TOB Request/Response Screen.
The record was reported as visible in the UI when checked using Interface ID DJ2L, although the user reported it was not displayed using only that Interface ID filter.
IT and business teams planned further discussion, but no confirmed final finding or corrective action was documented.

investigation_report.root_cause: The order-derived Shop Code "10V1" was used as the credit and debit Department Code but did not exist in KB Department Code Mapping, preventing the JV from being linked and sent to KB.
investigation_report.resolution: Added the required Department Code/shop-code mappings in Prod, mapped the remaining attached shop codes to 0001, and reprocessed and sent the "10V1" recovery JV to KB.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A job card of type "51: Complaint" could become linked to a new vehicle order by first creating it as "22: New car modification (movement)", linking the order, and then changing the JC Type before completion. The investigation confirmed that the relevant internal-order fields were retained when the JC Type changed. A Service Job Card fix was implemented in FDP UAT1, validated, and released to Production on 13 September.
important_findings: "51: Complaint" job cards cannot be directly linked to a new car order by design.

New vehicle order A000121450 was linked by creating a "22: New car modification (movement)" job card, setting the new car order in the internal order field, and changing the JC Type to "51: Claim" before completion.
The system allowed the linkage because internal-order values persisted after the JC Type was changed.
The fix resets "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type is changed.
UAT-1 validation confirmed that changing JC Type from "22" to another type, including "26", correctly resets the values.
The fix was released to Production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.
investigation_report.root_cause: Service Job Card did not reset the internal-order fields when the JC Type was changed, allowing a new car order linked under JC Type "22: New car modification (movement)" to remain linked after changing the job card to "51: Claim".
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented a Service Job Card change to reset "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type changes; validated in FDP UAT1/UAT-1 and deployed to Production on 13 September.

Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
When user creates a Payer Change Order, values in Bill to Basic Account and Ship to basic account is fetched from JCO. Then user changes the payer in Bill to Basic Account and values in Closed Date and Payment term should be reflected according to new Payer entered. But when user enters the value in Bill to basic account, the closed date field value is not updated and old value remains in the change order. Because of this, closed date was not changed to 25 in the change order and hence not sent to KB. Since the date was EOM, all the JC lines and change order lines were sent to KB on EOM(31st March).
Fix Plan: We will fix this issue where closed date will be updated when user enters the new payer in Bill to basic account. We will share the fix on UAT1 by 24th April. 
Meanwhile, please let us know if you have any query or need any additional information.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

宮内さん、
いつもお世話になっております。
問題概要：
ユーザーが支払者変更オーダーを作成する際、「Bill to Basic Account（請求先基本アカウント）」および「Ship to Basic Account（出荷先基本アカウント）」の値はJCOから取得されます。その後、ユーザーが「Bill to Basic Account」に別の支払者を入力した場合、「Closed Date（締日）」および「Payment Term（支払条件）」は、新しく入力された支払者に基づいて更新される必要があります。
しかし現状では、ユーザーが「Bill to Basic Account」に新しい支払者を入力しても「Closed Date」の値が更新されず、変更オーダーには以前の値が残ったままになります。

Problem summary:
When a user creates a payer change order, the "Bill to Basic Account" and "Ship to Basic Account" values are retrieved from the JCO. If the user subsequently enters a different payer in the Bill to Basic Account, the Closed Date and Payment Term must be updated based on the newly entered payer.

This fix will be released to the UAT1 environment by April 24th.
If you have any questions or require additional information, please feel free to contact us.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Payer Change Order retained the previous Closed Date after the user changed the Bill to Basic Account, causing bulk invoice data to be excluded from the expected closing-date processing and sent to KB at EOM instead. The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1, where Closed Date and Payment Term now update based on the newly selected payer. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
important_findings: For Account 0000205096, Change Order K000065493 retained an EOM closing date although the account closing date was 25.
In a Payer Change Order, Bill to Basic Account and Ship to Basic Account are initially retrieved from JCO.
Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh Closed Date or Payment Term; the prior values remained on the change order.
Because Closed Date remained EOM rather than 25, the change order was not sent to KB with the expected bulk invoice data; JC lines and change order lines were sent on 31 March.
The corrected behavior was verified in UAT-1 for Payer Change and Payer and Price Change scenarios.
investigation_report.root_cause: When the payer was changed in Bill to Basic Account on a Payer Change Order, the system did not update Closed Date and Payment Term from the newly selected payer, leaving the previous EOM Closed Date on the change order.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated FDP so that changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account on a Service Change Order refreshes Closed Date and Payment Term according to the new payer. The fix was deployed to FDP UAT-1, validated, and released to PROD on 12 June 2025; recovery bulk invoice data was also shared with MDIS after approval.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect Credit and Debit Department Code assignment in PO GR JV for Trade-In purchase orders. The existing logic used the NV Sales Order Last Approver, but the required logic for NV Trade-In is to derive the Branch Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep. The fix was validated in UAT1, affected JVs were recovered, and the change was released to Production on April 24.
important_findings: The original PO GR JV logic assigned Credit and Debit Department Code based on the NV Sales Order Last Approver/PO creator.
For NV Trade-In, both Credit and Debit Department Code must be set from the Branch Code of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep.
The fix was implemented in UAT1 and UAT passed with AR#H000046387 and PO# F001294580.
Alternate approver D0X20883 received the NV Sales Order approval request for Sales Rep D0X20897; approving the order created the Trade-In PO with D0X20883 as creator.
UV Trade-In does not require this fix because the department code on the JV Trade-In line is derived from the Assessment request, not the UV Sales Order final approval.
Affected JVs were recovered before the Production release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The NV Trade-In PO GR JV department-code logic incorrectly derived Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Last Approver instead of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the NV Trade-In PO GR JV logic to set Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code, validated the change in UAT1, recovered affected JVs, and released the fix to Production on April 24.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A recycle fee order could not be sent to TOB because the TOB response received in the JMS queue was not reflected in Siebel. The order was recovered, allowing the user to resend it to TOB. Investigation could not reproduce the issue in UAT, and later code-level verification reported expected functionality with no observed recurrence. No confirmed root cause or preventive fix was documented.
important_findings: The recycle fee order was recovered so it could be resent to TOB.
A TOB response was received in the JMS queue but did not update the status in Siebel, with no error reported in the scenario.
An initial finding stated that Siebel could not read half-width katakana in the TOB response; this was challenged because half-width kana is standard for TOB error messages.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT.
Code-level verification reported that the implementation and functionality were working as expected.
No recurrence was observed during subsequent monitoring in Siebel.
investigation_report.resolution: The recycle fee order was recovered, enabling the user to resend it to TOB. No permanent corrective change or preventive fix plan was documented.

comments.author: Ujjwal Goel
comments.text:
Dear Tsunoda-san,
After analyzing the issue, we have determined that RCA of this jira is same as MFTBCFFR 3641 that there is no city code in the address associated with the account used in the Sales Order.
We have replicated the issue on UAT 6 (Sales Order: A000026083). Below are the steps to replicate the issue:
Step 1: Create an Opportunity with Account code: 0000032930.
Step 2: Create and approve the quote.
Step 3: Create a Sales Order for the respective quote and approve the Sales Order.
Step 4: During the approval process for the Sales Posting of the Sales Order, when you attempt to approve the second approval from the Inbox, you will encounter a pop-up error. As a result, you will not be able to change the status to "Approved."
Step 5: Despite the inability to approve the Inbox, the Sales Order’s approval status in the approval history will show as "Approved," a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order will be created, and the status of your Order will change to "Sales Posting Completed."
Step 6: In the Inbox, when you reject the approval, the order status will change to "Rejected." You can then generate approvals again. If you repeat the process from Step 4, you will notice multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders being generated.
Error Message in error logs : 次のフィールドは必須です：口座、勘定コード、勘定コード、勘定コード、勘定コード、勘定コード、郵便番号、主要郵便番号日(SBL-BPR-00131)
Proposed Fix: To address this issue, we will ensure that the pop-up error currently encountered during the inbox approval process will be triggered when clicking "Generate Approval."
Please let us know if you need further clarification or assistance.
Best regards,
Ujjwal Goel

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Sales Posting approval failed for Sales Orders whose associated account address lacked a city code, causing Falcon-side validation errors. The failure could leave approval history marked "Approved" and create a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order even though the final Inbox approval was not completed. Recovery removed the existing shipment order and required completion of customer address data; the MFTBCFFR-3641-equivalent fix was deployed to UAT and production on April 14.
important_findings: The root cause matched MFTBCFFR-3641: the account used by the Sales Order had no city code in its address.
Error logs reported: "The following fields are required: Account, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Postal Code, Primary Postal Code Date (SBL-BPR-00131)".

During second Sales Posting approval in Inbox, a pop-up error prevented the Inbox item from becoming "Approved," while approval history could show "Approved" and the order could move to "Sales Posting Completed."
Rejecting and regenerating approval after the failure could create duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders.
Orders with null account address information error on the Falcon side; mandatory customer address fields, including "City County Name" and "OOAZA Name", must be populated before processing.
The existing Pool Cost Shipment was removed during recovery, and a reverse JV was created.
investigation_report.root_cause: Missing city code/address information in the customer account associated with the Sales Order caused Falcon-side mandatory-field validation errors during Sales Posting approval.
investigation_report.resolution: Applied the MFTBCFFR-3641-equivalent fix in UAT and deployed it to production on April 14. The recovery removed the existing Pool Cost Shipment, created a reverse JV, and required the customer account address details to be completed before regenerating and approving Sales Posting.

Dear Tsunoda-san,
After analyzing the issue, we have determined that the problem arises because there is no city code in the address associated with the account used in the Sales Order.
We have replicated the issue on UAT 6 (Sales Order: A000026083). Below are the steps to replicate the issue:
Step 1: Create an Opportunity with Account code: 0000032930.
 Step 2: Create and approve the quote.
 Step 3: Create a Sales Order for the respective quote and approve the Sales Order.
 Step 4: During the approval process for the Sales Posting of the Sales Order, when you attempt to approve the second approval from the Inbox, you will encounter a pop-up error. As a result, you will not be able to change the status to "Approved."
 Step 5: Despite the inability to approve the Inbox, the Sales Order’s approval status in the approval history will show as "Approved," a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order will be created, and the status of your Order will change to "Sales Posting Completed."
 Step 6: In the Inbox, when you reject the approval, the order status will change to "Rejected." You can then generate approvals again. If you repeat the process from Step 4, you will notice multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders being generated.
Proposed Fix: To address this issue, we will ensure that the pop-up error currently encountered during the inbox approval process will be triggered when clicking "Generate Approval."

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Incomplete address data on the account used by the NV Quote/Sales Order caused an approval-processing error while downstream processing still marked approval as completed and generated duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and JVs. The affected account address is the account selected in the Contractor Name field, whose address is sent to Falcon. Duplicate JVs and Falcon records were recovered, and validation was implemented in NV Quote to prevent approval generation when the selected contractor account has incomplete address data. The validated fix was released to PROD on April 14.
important_findings: The original failure was reproduced on UAT 6 with Sales Order A000026083 and customer code 0000032930.

During the second Sales Posting approval from Inbox, an error prevented Inbox approval, but approval history showed Approved, the order moved to Sales Posting Completed, and a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order was created.
Rejecting the Inbox approval and regenerating approvals could create multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and duplicate JVs.
The account address data used by the Sales Order was incomplete; missing city code/address fields, including Oaza/Common Name for account 0000029653, triggered the issue.
Validation checks only the address of the account selected in the Contractor Name field because Falcon sends that account's address data.

Recovery included unmapping Pool Cost Shipment orders, creating reverse JVs for duplicate JVs, resolving a Data set separator-related JV error for KB transmission, and completing Falcon recovery after customer master updates.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incomplete or null address fields on the account selected in the Contractor Name field for the NV Quote/Sales Order, including missing city code and Oaza/Common Name, caused the approval-processing error.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented NV Quote validation on the Request Approval/Generate Approval action to block processing when the Contractor Name account has incomplete address information, with the message: "Please check the business partner master of the user selected in the business partner name. The customer address in the business partner master is a required field." The fix was validated in UAT and released to PROD on April 14; duplicate JVs were reversed and Falcon recovery was completed.
technical_entities: Last name of primary shipping destination
