investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate JVs were created for a JC linked to Sales Order#: Q050057080 because a spreadsheet could be approved, later manually changed to "Cancelled", and replaced with another approved spreadsheet. JV creation is triggered when "Spreadsheet Status" changes to "Spreadsheet Approved". A reverse JV was created for the JV generated from the cancelled spreadsheet, and the UI validation was deployed to production on April 14.
important_findings: A JV for Liability Orders is created when "Spreadsheet Status" changes to "Spreadsheet Approved".
The "Spreadsheet Status" field remained editable after approval, allowing an approved spreadsheet to be manually changed to "Cancelled".
Spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01 was approved and later cancelled; its approval had already created a JV.
Spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-02 was subsequently created and approved for the same JC, creating another JV.
A reverse JV was created for the JV generated by spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01.
The fix restricts editing of "Spreadsheet Status" to records whose status is "Spreadsheet Created".
investigation_report.root_cause: The "Spreadsheet Status" field was editable after "Spreadsheet Approved", allowing an approved spreadsheet to be cancelled and replaced with another approved spreadsheet, which triggered duplicate JV creation.
investigation_report.resolution: Created a reverse JV for the JV generated by cancelled spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01 and changed the UI so "Spreadsheet Status" is editable only when its value is "Spreadsheet Created". The fix was validated in UAT and deployed to the production environment on April 14.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Body Building Order could be manually transitioned without required vendor information, resulting in a blank Vendor Finance Account Code on the Journal Voucher (JV). Initial UAT1 validation covered the "Pending" to "Ordered" transition, but testing identified that "Order changed" could still be selected without a bodybuilder/Vendor Name. Validation for both required vendor details was corrected, verified, and deployed to production in the April 14 urgent release.
important_findings: The affected Body Building Order had a blank Vendor Finance Account Code, which caused the corresponding Journal Voucher (JV) value to be blank.
The issue was reproduced in UAT by manually changing a Body Building Order status from "Pending" to "Ordered" while "Vendor Finance Account Code" was null.
The initial UAT1 fix added a pop-up validation when changing status from "Pending" to "Ordered" with a blank "Vendor Finance Account Code".
Validation testing found that status "Order changed" could still be selected without a bodybuilder/Vendor Name for both Non-IBOS and IBOS workflows.
The final fix added Vendor Name validation equivalent to the validation used when executing "Generate Approvals" without Vendor Code.
investigation_report.root_cause: Manual status changes for Body Building Orders lacked validation for required vendor information, allowing transitions with blank Vendor Finance Account Code and, in the "Order changed" path, missing Vendor Name.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected order and deployed validation preventing status changes when required Vendor Finance Account Code or Vendor Name is missing. The corrected validation was verified and applied to production in the April 14 urgent release.

ML351609 required an after-hours price update due to its effective start date, and all part prices were updated after the price revision activity.
important_findings: The affected parts were not present in the D2S files received on 19/03/2025, so they were not updated in FDP environments.
ML351609 had an effective start date of 01/04/2024 and was scheduled for an after-hours price update on all FDPs.
After the price revision activity, all affected part prices were updated in FDP-PROD.
investigation_report.root_cause: The affected part records were missing from the D2S files received on 19/03/2025.
investigation_report.resolution: D2S resent the missing parts, and the prices were updated in FDP environments; ML351609 was updated through an after-hours price revision activity. All part prices were confirmed updated.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Parts Internal Order list prices became null when parts were added through Sub Quote in NV Quote. Investigation reproduced the issue on UAT1 and established that the related NV Sales Order Start Price was set to null during Sub Quote completion. A fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.
important_findings: Parts Internal Order list price is fetched from NV Sales Order.
Adding a part through Sub Quote in NV Quote caused the NV Sales Order Start Price to be set to null.
The issue was reproduced on UAT1 with NV Sales Order A001293389, part ###600SILVER, resulting in null list price on Parts Internal Order M001293390.
When parts are added through Parts and Intenal Work in an NV Quote line item, the list price is displayed; the issue occurred when creating the part order through Sub Quote.
The fix was verified on UAT1 using NV Sales Order A001293480 with parts ###600BLACK-5K and ###1003, creating Parts Internal Order M001293481.
The fix was applied to PROD in the April 14 release.
investigation_report.root_cause: During Sub Quote completion in NV Quote, the Start Price for the added part in NV Sales Order was set to null. Since Parts Internal Order list price is sourced from NV Sales Order, its list price also became null.
investigation_report.resolution: Fixed the Sub Quote processing issue that set NV Sales Order Start Price to null; the fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A JV was created for Sales Order # Q050020683 but was not linked to KB because its Credit Department Code was set to "INTERNAL" from the Insurance Order. Investigation found that the Ejibai-created order inherited incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details from its linked existing order because it was created before Sales Rep recovery for migrated orders completed. Recovery JVs were created with Credit and Debit Department Code 3011 and sent to KB, and the affected order was recovered.
important_findings: The JV was not linked to KB because its Credit Department Code was "INTERNAL", sourced from the Insurance Order.
Sales Rep recovery for all migrated orders was completed on February 17, 2025.
Sales Order # Q050020683 was created through Ejibai on February 13, 2025, before the Sales Rep recovery completed.
Ejibai order-creation logic retrieves Sales Rep details from the linked existing order, causing incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details to be inherited.
Recovery JV processing used Credit Department Code 3011 and Debit Department Code 3011.
investigation_report.root_cause: Sales Order # Q050020683 was created through Ejibai before Sales Rep recovery for migrated orders completed, so it inherited incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details from its linked existing order; the resulting JV had Credit Department Code "INTERNAL" from the Insurance Order and could not link to KB.
investigation_report.resolution: Created recovery JVs using Credit Department Code 3011 and Debit Department Code 3011, sent them to KB, and recovered the affected order.

Dear Tsunoda-san,
 
Thank you for your continued support.
 
After analyzing the issue, we have determined the root cause as follows:
 
Typically, when an invoice is created, the "Billing Status Code" field in the sales order items related to the invoice is updated to "Invoiced." However, in this case, this update did not occur, which is preventing the Registration Request from being completed.
 
As this problem is rare and difficult to replicate, we have considered a preventive measure.
 
The preventive measure we propose involves updating the order line items where the billing code status should have been invoiced but was not processed correctly. To address this, we will trigger a workflow when the "Create Registration Request" button is clicked. The workflow will check the sales order line items whose status should have been invoiced but is not, and will update their billing code status to "Invoiced."
 
Please let us know if you have any feedback or concerns regarding this approach.
 
Best regards,
Ujjwal Goel

通常、請求書が作成されると、それに関連する受注明細の「請求ステータスコード」フィールドが「請求済み」に更新されます。しかし、今回のケースではこの更新が行われず、追加の請求書が作成されてしまいました。
この問題は発生頻度が低く、再現が困難であるため、防止策を検討しました。
提案する防止策として、本来「請求済み」に更新されるべき受注明細のステータスが処理されていない場合に、それを更新する仕組みを導入します。具体的には、「自動請求」ボタンをクリックした際にワークフローを起動し、「請求済み」に更新されるべき受注明細の請求ステータスコードをチェックし、未処理のものを「請求済み」に更新するようにします。

どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。

Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
After analyzing this issue, we identified the root cause as follows:
Typically, when an invoice is created, the Billing Status Code field on its associated order line is updated to "Invoiced." However, in this case, this update was not made and an additional invoice was created.
Because this issue occurs infrequently and is difficult to reproduce, we looked into ways to prevent it.
As a proposed preventive measure, we will introduce a mechanism to update the status of an order item that should have been updated to "Invoiced" if it has not been processed. Specifically, when the "Automatic Billing" button is clicked, a workflow is started, the billing status code of the order details that should be updated to "Invoiced" is checked, and the unprocessed ones are updated to "Invoiced".
If you have any comments or concerns regarding this policy, please let us know.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The affected record was recovered, but the incident was rare and could not be reproduced in UAT. Investigation identified that the Billing Status Code on sales order items associated with an invoice was not updated to "Invoiced," preventing Registration Request completion. A preventive workflow-based correction was deployed to Production on 24 April 2025, with increased logging and ongoing monitoring.
important_findings: When an invoice is created, the associated sales order items are normally updated with Billing Status Code "Invoiced."
For the incident, the Billing Status Code update did not occur, which blocked completion of the Registration Request.
The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, so error handling was added to the invoice creation workflow and monitored.
The preventive correction checks order line items associated with completed invoices and updates unprocessed Billing Status Code values to "Invoiced" during Registration Request completion.

The intended business flow remains that a Registration Request can be completed only after invoice completion; canceled invoices and subsequently created replacement invoices are handled based on invoice status.
The correction was implemented in Production on 24 April 2025, with log levels increased for continued monitoring.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Billing Status Code on sales order items associated with an invoice was not updated to "Invoiced," preventing the Registration Request from being completed.
investigation_report.resolution: A temporary preventive workflow-based correction was deployed to Production to identify order line items linked to completed invoices whose Billing Status Code was not updated and set the status to "Invoiced" during Registration Request completion. Error logging and monitoring were also increased.

To address this, we will trigger a workflow when the "Auto Invoice" button is clicked. The workflow will check the sales order line items whose status should have been invoiced but is not, and will update their billing code status to "Invoiced."

Typically, when an invoice is created, the Billing Status Code field on its associated order line is updated to "Invoiced." However, in this case, this update was not made and an additional invoice was created.
Because this issue occurs infrequently and is difficult to reproduce, we looked into ways to prevent it.
As a proposed preventive measure, we will introduce a mechanism to update the status of an order item that should have been updated to "Invoiced" if it has not been processed. Specifically, when the "Automatic Billing" button is clicked, a workflow is started, the billing status code of the order details that should be updated to "Invoiced" is checked, and the unprocessed ones are updated to "Invoiced".

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An additional invoice could be created because the Billing Status Code on the associated sales order item/order line was not updated to "Invoiced" after invoice completion. The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, and the underlying reason for the missing status update remained under investigation with error logging. A temporary preventive workflow was planned for Production, with ongoing monitoring transferred to MFTBCFFR-3616.
important_findings: Invoice completion normally updates the Billing Status Code of associated sales order items to "Invoiced".
In the affected case, the Billing Status Code update did not occur and remained "Blank", allowing an additional invoice to be created.
The issue was not reproducible in UAT, and error logging was added to capture recurrence details.
The proposed preventive measure triggers a workflow from the "Automatic Billing" button to identify order lines that should be "Invoiced" and update their Billing Status Code.
The temporary fix was scheduled for implementation in the Production environment on 24 April 2025; subsequent monitoring was to continue under MFTBCFFR-3616.

D2S price master must be processed using the same file across all FDPs; using different files causes values to differ between FDPs.
Recovery was completed on all PROD environments.
Data-loading procedures will be improved to verify that price updates are correct and consistent across all FDP Prod environments.
investigation_report.root_cause: The D2S Price master file had duplicate records for Part Number MK658033, and manual deletion of one record caused inconsistent results across FDP environments.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed on all PROD environments. The data-loading procedure will be improved to ensure price updates are correctly applied and verified across all FDP Prod environments.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Vehicles from the common TOB TCB-01 file were synchronized to SC and all FDP environments, causing vehicles outside the intended dealer scope to be registered in the China region. Investigation confirmed that TCB-01 processing has no dealer-code-based filtering in either SC or FDP. The incident was closed as an IT issue after discussion with the business; no implementation change was recorded.
important_findings: TOB sends the same TCB01 file, containing all TOB-managed vehicles, to SC and all FDP environments.
Vehicles with dealer codes other than 7306 were registered as China-region vehicles, although dealer code 7306 was the intended update scope.
TCB-01 processing in SC and FDP has no record filter based on dealer code; all file data is synchronized.
No dealer-code filter was configured during FDP initial setup, and no related business change request had been received.
Applying a filter to TCB-01 processing requires a change request (CR).
The case was considered a rare occurrence and closed following discussion with the business.
investigation_report.root_cause: TCB-01 processing in both SC and FDP environments was configured without dealer-code-based record filtering, so all vehicles in the common TOB file were synchronized to all environments.

*RCA:* The issue occurs due to data migration and editable Sales Order # field in UV Inventory screen.
In FDP a new flag “Previous Assessment Flag” was created which is set to Y for all the UV Pool Cost-Procurement, Job Card Order and UV Body Building Orders if the parent UV Sales Order is Sales Posting Completed. This flag ensures that purchase orders associated with old UV Sales Order are not visible on UI if the vehicle is stocked in again.
During data migration, this flag was not set to “Y” so user was able to see all the previous purchase orders on UI and was able to change the Sales Order #.
*Preventive Measures:* We will perform recovery for all the migrated order tonight so that they are not visible under UV Inventory screen after restock in.
Also, we suggest to make this field read only on UI because user can change the Sales Order # for any purchase order that is associated with stocked in vehicle and KB Map/Unmap trigger is not created in this user operation.
Please let us know if you have any further query.
Best Regards,
Shivam

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Purchase orders were incorrectly visible in UV Inventory after vehicle restock, allowing users to change the associated Sales Order # and disrupting the sales process. Data migration had not set the FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" to Y for qualifying orders, and the editable "Sales Order #" field permitted the change without creating a KB Map/Unmap trigger. Recovery was completed for migrated orders, the field was changed to read-only, and the fix was released to production on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: The affected PO was unmapped from UV Sales Order# E050064869 and mapped to Sales Order# E020841755 as recovery.
In FDP, "Previous Assessment Flag" must be set to Y when the parent UV Sales Order is Sales Posting Completed, preventing prior purchase orders from appearing after vehicle restock.
During data migration, "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y, so previous purchase orders remained visible in UV Inventory.
"MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" was editable for 10 responsibilities, allowing authorized users to edit the UI "Sales Order #" field.
Editing "Sales Order #" for a purchase order associated with a stocked-in vehicle does not create a KB Map/Unmap trigger.
Recovery was completed for migrated orders, and no similar issue was found in NV.
investigation_report.root_cause: During data migration, FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y for qualifying orders, leaving prior purchase orders visible in UV Inventory. Users with access to the editable "MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" could then change the editable "Sales Order #" field without generating a KB Map/Unmap trigger.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered migrated orders so prior purchase orders no longer appear in UV Inventory after restock, and changed the "Sales Order #" field to read-only in UV Inventory. The change passed UAT and was released to PROD on March 26, 2025.

Investigation confirmed that the Self-Approval Restriction CR exists in the SC version but is not implemented in FDP. The approval flow rules were reviewed and were functioning as expected; no system change was required.
important_findings: In the SC version, the Self-Approval Restriction CR displays an error and prevents the approval email when the requester and approver are the same.
In the FDP version, approval email is expected to be sent to the approver even when the requester and approver are the same.
The FDP version does not implement the Self-Approval Restriction CR, so no self-approval error message is displayed.
The "JC Close Low Profit" (Manager) approval flow contains rules determined by "Quote Profit Ratio After Discount".
Reviewed approval flow rules were confirmed to be working as expected, and no additional modifications were required.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Self-Approval Restriction CR functionality implemented in the SC version is not implemented in the FDP version.
investigation_report.resolution: No corrective system change was required; the approval flow rules were verified as functioning correctly and the incident was requested to be dismissed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In FDP, Sales Posting was possible when no JCO existed because the Service Quote had not been progressed to "Customer Approved". The investigation confirmed that FDP had no Sales Posting validation for missing JCOs, while JCO creation after "Customer Approved" already required the corresponding Job Card to be closed before Sales Posting. A validation was implemented in UAT, approved for production, and released on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced on UAT1: a Sales Order could be completed while the JCO activity was not completed.
In FDP, Sales Posting was allowed when no JCO was created because the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved".
Changing the Service Quote to "Customer Approved" creates a JCO; after that, Sales Posting is blocked until the corresponding Job Card is closed.
The existing FDP behavior resulted from a missing validation check, potentially triggered when the user did not progress the Service Quote to "Customer Approved".
SC includes a validation message when changing a Delivery Request status to "Completed" in the equivalent missing-JCO scenario.
A similar validation was implemented in FDP, validated in UAT, approved for Prod, and released on March 26, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: FDP did not validate the presence of a JCO during Sales Posting when the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved", allowing Sales Posting without JCO creation or Job Card closure.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented a validation in FDP to prevent the missing-JCO Sales Posting scenario; the change was deployed to UAT, approved for Prod, and released to production on March 26, 2025.

comments.text:
Dear Tsunoda San, 
Thanks for your support. 
Please find below the analysis details for incident *MFTBCFFR: 3546* regarding the issue where the recycle order was not displayed in the Chugoku Production environment.
*Root Cause Analysis (RCA):*
The *D21F* file was received and processed before the *D21A* file. Since the chassis record had not yet been created during the D21A file execution, the recycle fee order could not be created during the D21F execution.
*Recovery Action:*
As part of the recovery, the *D21F* process was re-executed after the successful completion of the *D21A* process. This resulted in the successful creation of the recycle fee order.
*Countermeasure:*
As this issue was caused by the sequence of *TOB* file processing and is *not related to the Siebel system*, we are unable to provide a Siebel-side countermeasure for this scenario.
*Monitoring:*
To avoid such errors, Cubastion has configured email notifications to alert the team whenever any file execution fails. This enables us to promptly identify unprocessed or failed files and take timely recovery actions whenever required.
Since this issue was caused by the TOB file processing sequence and is not related to the Siebel system, we would like to proceed with closing this Jira ticket.
Best Regards,
Deepika Raheja

■ 再発防止策
 
本事象は、TOBファイルの処理順序に起因するものであり、Siebelシステムの不具合ではないため、Siebel側で対応可能なシステム改修はございません。

Dear Tsunoda San,
 
Thank you for your continued support.
 
We would like to report the results of our investigation regarding **incident MFTBCFFR-3546 (recycling fee order not displayed on chassis order in production environment in China)**.
 
■ Cause (RCA)
 
After investigation, we confirmed that the D21F file was received and processed before the D21A file.
 
At the time of D21F processing, a recycling fee order could not be created because the chassis order (vehicle information) by D21A had not yet been created.
 
■ Recovery support
 
We have confirmed that re-running the D21F process after completing the D21A process will successfully create a recycling fee order.
 
■ Measures to prevent recurrence
 
This event is caused by the TOB file processing order and is not a problem with the Siebel system, so there is no system modification that can be done on the Siebel side.
 
Additionally, in order to detect similar events at an early stage, Cubastion has introduced a monitoring function that sends email notifications when file processing fails.
 
This allows us to quickly detect processing failures and unprocessed files, and promptly implement recovery measures if necessary.
 
We have confirmed that this issue is caused by the TOB file processing order and is not a problem with the Siebel system, so we would like to close this JIRA.
 
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In the Chugoku Production environment, recycle fee orders were not created because the TOB D21F file was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file. D21A creates the chassis order, which is a prerequisite for D21F to create the recycle fee order. The initially reported D21E dependency was corrected: the relevant sequence is D21A and D21F. Affected records were recovered by re-executing D21F after D21A processing; monitoring was implemented to identify similar cases for recovery.
important_findings: The root sequence issue was TOB processing D21F before the corresponding D21A file for the same order.
D21A creates the chassis order, while D21F creates the recycle fee order; without the chassis order, D21F cannot create the recycle fee order.
The initial reference to D21E in March 2025 was incorrect; the correct prerequisite file is D21A.
Re-executing D21F after successful D21A processing created the missing recycle fee orders.
The issue was identified as a TOB file sequencing issue rather than a Cubastion Siebel system defect.
Monitoring and email notifications were implemented to identify failed, unprocessed, or sequencing-related cases and enable recovery.
investigation_report.root_cause: The corresponding TOB D21F file was received and processed before the D21A file. Because D21A had not yet created the prerequisite chassis order, D21F could not create the recycle fee order.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered affected records by re-executing D21F after the corresponding D21A process completed, creating the recycle fee orders. Monitoring was implemented to detect similar cases and trigger recovery actions.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An intermittent Siebel issue caused Trade-in Consumption Tax not to be correctly reflected in the NV Quote header after entering a Trade-in Amount. Impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered. The code was corrected in UAT and released to production on March 26, 2025, with continued monitoring planned.
important_findings: The issue occurred intermittently and had no specific reproducible steps.
The affected behavior occurred when entering a Trade-in Amount: Trade-in Consumption Tax should populate in both the Trade-in subtab and the Quote Header.
All impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered; no recovery was required for other FDP environments.
The code did not follow Siebel best practices because Link Specification was not set to TRUE.
The UAT validation was intended to confirm that NV quotation and trade-in functionality continued to operate normally after the code change.
The production release of the fix was completed on March 26, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: Link Specification was not set to TRUE in the Siebel code, contrary to Oracle-recommended Siebel best practices, causing intermittent failure to reflect Trade-in Consumption Tax in the NV Quote Header.
investigation_report.resolution: Set Link Specification to TRUE in UAT, validated that existing NV quotation and trade-in functionality was not impacted, released the fix to production on March 26, 2025, and recovered affected records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments.

RCA: The events in this case are as follows.
A user creates an order from a quote that includes two parts items.

The user has revised the quote.

As a result, when users synced quotes and orders, they were synced with existing part items and no new items were created. Additionally, the parts order was already created for the old item, which caused the operation to stop.
As this is a very rare occurrence, we ask that you please monitor your systems for similar occurrences in the future and check with our business team to find a better and more efficient solution to control this issue.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A user revised a quote after creating an order, a Parts Internal Order, and Return order records for two part items. When the old part items were deleted and replacement part items were added, the replacement items received the same line numbers and synchronized to the existing part items instead of being created as new items. Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the affected part line items, allowing purchase-order creation to proceed.
important_findings: The order was created from a quote containing two part items, followed by creation of a Parts Internal Order and Return order records for both items.
After the quote was revised, the original two part items were deleted and two new part items were added with the same line numbers.
Quote-to-order synchronization matched the new part items to existing part items rather than creating new items.
Existing part orders for the old items caused the operation to stop and prevented purchase-order creation.
The incident was identified as a rare scenario and future occurrences should be monitored.
investigation_report.root_cause: After quote revision, replacement part items were assigned the same line numbers as deleted part items. During quote and order synchronization, they matched existing part items that already had Parts Internal Order and Return order records, leaving the parent order ID unchanged and causing the operation to stop.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the line items associated with the parts; the user was then instructed to create the purchase order.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: During the January 14, 2025 data migration from SC Prod to FDP Chugoku, address values for some records were corrected after AR account creation because of validation mismatches. The corrected records were not resent to KB after patching. Updating the records' "Last Update Date" triggered transmission in the nightly batch, and all affected records were recovered.
important_findings: The issue affected only some records migrated from SC Prod to FDP Chugoku on January 14, 2025.
Address information was updated after AR account creation due to validation mismatches.
Records updated after patching were not submitted to KB again.
All customer interface files sent to KB were reviewed and affected customers were identified.
Changing the "Last Update Date" caused the affected records to be sent to KB in the nightly batch.
All records were recovered on March 5, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: During the January 14, 2025 migration, address corrections made after AR account creation were not resent to KB after patching.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the affected records' "Last Update Date" so they were transmitted to KB in the nightly batch; all records were recovered.

Thank you for your support.
For this issue the probable fixes are as follows:
*Issue:* In D21Z file the date which is received from the TOB side does is in the format of *MMDD*  and not having the Year.
*Fix Plan-1*: Considering the Shipment date will be older than the  D21Z file execution data. We will compare the Shipment date received in the file to the file execution date and if the Shipment date is greater than the file execution date in the format of *MMDD* then we will take the previous year. Otherwise the current year. 
This change needs to be handled at the ODI side. So a project CR will be required for this.
*Fix Plan 2:* As the Shipment date is already updated by the D21N file. So, the Shipment date updating process from D21Z file will be stopped. This can be done by AMS-CR
*Fix Plan 3*: If TOB can send the year in the D21Z file then we can update the same in the Siebel system.
These are the probable fix plans to handle these types of issues.
In case a detailed discussion is required, we can also schedule a call for the same.
Regards
Ashutosh Dogra

角田さん、
いつもお世話になっております。
本件の問題について、以下のような対応案を考えております。
■ 問題点
D21Zファイルにおいて、TOB側から受領する日付がMMDD形式となっており、Year（年）の情報が含まれていません。
■ 対応案 
① 修正案1
Shipment DateはD21Zファイルの実行日より過去の日付であることを前提とし、以下のルールで処理を行います。 
Shipment Date（MMDD形式）がファイル実行日より大きい場合：前年を適用
それ以外の場合：当年を適用
この変更はODI側での対応が必要となるため、プロジェクトCRの申請が必要です。
② 修正案2
Shipment DateはすでにD21Nファイルにより更新されているため、D21ZファイルからのShipment Date更新処理を停止する対応です。
この場合、AMS-CRにて対応可能です。
③ 修正案3
TOB側でD21ZファイルにYear(年)の情報を含めていただける場合、それをSiebelシステムに反映する形で対応可能です。
以上が今回の問題に対する対応案となります。
ご不明点や詳細なご相談が必要な場合は、別途お打ち合わせを設定することも可能ですので、必要でしたら、ご連絡ください。
comments.text_enu:
Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
Regarding this issue, we are considering the following solutions.
■ Problems
In the D21Z file, the date received from the TOB side is in MMDD format and does not include Year information.
■ Countermeasure plan
① Amendment 1
It is assumed that the Shipment Date is a date in the past than the execution date of the D21Z file, and processing is performed according to the following rules. 
If the Shipment Date (MMDD format) is greater than the file execution date: apply the previous year
Otherwise: apply current year
Since this change requires action on the ODI side, a project CR application is required.
② Amendment 2
Since the Shipment Date has already been updated by the D21N file, this will stop the Shipment Date update process from the D21Z file.
In this case, AMS-CR can be used.
③ Amendment 3
If the TOB side can include Year information in the D21Z file, we can reflect it in the Siebel system.
The above is a solution to this problem.
If you have any questions or need detailed consultation, we can set up a separate meeting, so please contact us if necessary.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned incorrect chassis date display and an initial analysis attributed it to D21Z processing of MMDD date values without a year. The documented logic added the current year and converted MMDD to YYYYMMDD, resulting in incorrect dates for records requiring a prior year. Later comments disputed that D21Z contained the relevant actual shipping date, and the issue was not reproducible; only a temporary workaround was reported, with no permanent fix confirmed.
important_findings: Initial analysis identified D21Z_03032025113216 as containing Chassis Shipment Date and Actual Assembly Date in MMDD format without a year.
The configured D21Z processing logic adds the current year and converts MMDD values to YYYYMMDD; this caused an affected date to be updated as 04/12/2025.
Recovery was completed for the initially affected record.

Proposed corrective options included ODI logic to select the prior year when the MMDD date is greater than the file execution date, stopping Shipment Date updates from D21Z because D21N already updates it, or having TOB provide the year.
Later feedback stated that D21Z has no actual shipping date and that the issue was not D21Z-related, leaving the original source attribution unresolved.
As of 2026-04-07, IT reported that only a temporary workaround had been implemented and a permanent solution had not been applied; subsequent updates stated the issue could not be reproduced.

investigation_report.root_cause: During the Import process, line items with missing part numbers in the master failed and were reprocessed after the master was corrected, causing prices not to be populated for some Accessories sales order line items.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In FDP UAT1, accepting UOE Quote 1-6FH10R failed when the Customer code was blank, despite External ID 0000212580 being set for UID MHATA91. The behavior differed from the SC version, where the function worked correctly. The FDP issue was corrected in UAT1, validated by the requester, and released to production on August 27 in the regular release.
important_findings: The issue occurred when the Customer code was blank during the Accept action.
For UOE Quote 1-6FH10R, External ID 0000212580 was set for UID MHATA91, but accepting the quote did not set the Customer code and displayed an error.
The corresponding function worked correctly in the SC version, indicating a difference between FDP and SC behavior.
The corrected behavior was validated in FDP UAT1 before production approval.
The fix was released to the production environment in the regular release on August 27.
investigation_report.root_cause: In the FDP version, the logic to set the External ID for the latest UID did not work when the Customer code was blank, causing the Accept action to fail.
investigation_report.resolution: The FDP logic was corrected in FDP UAT1, validated as working, and released to production in the August 27 regular release.

comments.text:
Dear Shiromoto-san
Thank you for your continued support.
This is to inform you that the incident INC4015844 raised in the SC environment, which involved a fix related to wrong UV Sales Order Status, has been addressed. The fix has been successfully implemented in the FDP UAT-1 environment.
With this update, users will no longer be able to click 'Generate Approval' button when UV Sales Order status is 'Rejected' but the Delivery Request has been Completed. The 'Generate Approval' button will now be disabled for UV Orders whose Delivery Request is completed but Sales Order status is 'Rejected'.
Kindly find the reference record on UAT-1 environment:
 AR#: H000051489, UV SO#: E001300162
Kindly verify the changes in the FDP UAT-1 environment and approve the fix for production deployment.
Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or require further information.
Best regards,
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report.investigation_summary: INC4015844 addressed an incorrect UV Sales Order status behavior in the SC environment. A fix was implemented in FDP UAT-1 to prevent approval generation for rejected UV Sales Orders when the associated Delivery Request is completed. The change requires verification and approval before production deployment.
important_findings: Users could click the 'Generate Approval' button when a UV Sales Order status was 'Rejected' and the Delivery Request was Completed.
The fix disables the 'Generate Approval' button for UV Orders with a completed Delivery Request and a 'Rejected' Sales Order status.
The fix was implemented in the FDP UAT-1 environment.
Reference validation record: AR# H000051489, UV SO# E001300162.
investigation_report.root_cause: The 'Generate Approval' button was enabled for UV Sales Orders in 'Rejected' status when their associated Delivery Request was completed.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented a fix in FDP UAT-1 to disable the 'Generate Approval' button when the UV Sales Order status is 'Rejected' and the Delivery Request is completed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Customer-related fields were becoming null on UV Sales Order when users could manually clear the Customer Name field. The issue was fixed in the FDP UAT environment by making Customer Name read-only, preventing users from removing it. The fix was released to production in the regular release on July 24.
important_findings: The Customer Name field on the UV Sales Order screen was not read-only.
Users could remove Customer Name manually on a UV Sales Order.
Clearing Customer Name also nullified Customer Name, Bill To Account, and Payer Account.
Making Customer Name read-only prevented customer-related fields from becoming null.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Vehicle-to-business-object migration data in FDP was inconsistent because SC Prod vehicle identifiers did not reliably align. The investigation found duplicate VIN vehicles and mismatches between X_KEY and ASSET_NUM in SC Prod; migration used ASSET_NUM as the unique/user key. Recovery was completed in FDP according to the provided file, updating affected Chassis# (Key#) references.
important_findings: Vehicle records in SC Prod contain X_KEY, SERIAL_NUM, and ASSET_NUM; these values should ideally match.
For ASSET_NUM "FK62F-605267", X_KEY and SERIAL_NUM were "FU74HZ-510966".
Migration used ASSET_NUM as the unique/user key, causing mismatches when X_KEY and ASSET_NUM differed.
When multiple SC Prod vehicles had the same VIN, the correct vehicle ID was not updated during migration.
Recovery scope included Chassis# (Key#) references for JC, WO, Quote, PO, JCO, Expense, and Change Order.
There was no Registration# gap; Power BI had no SC Version and no gap, so no Power BI recovery was required.
investigation_report.root_cause: SC Prod vehicle master data contained duplicate VIN records and mismatched X_KEY, SERIAL_NUM, and ASSET_NUM values; using ASSET_NUM as the unique key during migration prevented the correct vehicle ID from being updated.
investigation_report.resolution: Completed FDP recovery based on the provided file by correcting affected Chassis# (Key#) references across JC, WO, Quote, PO, JCO, Expense, and Change Order.

Dear Shiromoto-San,
Thank you for your support.
*RCA:*
Currently, our logic retrieves Profit (Sales Price - Cost Price) based on the formula: *Cost Price = Cost * Quantity*, regardless of the DELETE_FLG status in the Datamart database.
However, line items deleted from the Siebel side still exist in the Datamart DB, marked with *DELETE_FLG = 'Y'*, while active line items in Siebel are marked as *DELETE_FLG = 'N'* in Datamart.
Since the PBI report doesn't have a filter to separate deleted line items, causing the difference in Profit values between the PBI report and Siebel. 
*Fix Plan:* 
We are actively working on resolving this issue and expect to implement the fix by *14/03/2025* on UAT.In the meantime, we will proceed with the recovery of impacted records.
Regards,
Sheetal

RCA:

しかし、Siebel 側で削除された明細は Datamart DB に DELETE_FLG = 'Y' として残り、一方で Siebel 上で有効な明細は Datamart 上で DELETE_FLG = 'N' として管理されています。

よろしくお願いいたします。

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PBI profit values differed from Siebel because deleted Siebel line items remained in the Datamart database and were included in profit calculations. The fix added DELETE_FLG handling in ODI and filtered Power BI reports to display only active line items. The changes were validated in UAT and deployed to prod across all environments.
important_findings: Deleted Siebel line items remain in the Datamart DB with DELETE_FLG = 'Y', while active line items use DELETE_FLG = 'N'.
The existing profit logic included records regardless of DELETE_FLG, causing PBI report profit discrepancies versus Siebel.
Impacted records for Iwate SO#: E000003241 and Chugoku SO#: E050024154 were recovered while the permanent fix was being developed.
DELETE_FLG was added to WC_UV_SALES_F and ODI processing was updated to set DELETE_FLG = 'Y' for inactive records.
Power BI UV reports 2_05 and 2_06 were updated with DELETE_FLG = 'N' filtering and verified by deleting a Siebel line item.
investigation_report.root_cause: PBI reports did not exclude Datamart line items marked DELETE_FLG = 'Y', so deleted Siebel line items were included in profit calculations.
investigation_report.resolution: Added DELETE_FLG to WC_UV_SALES_F, updated ODI to set DELETE_FLG = 'Y' for inactive records, and applied DELETE_FLG = 'N' filtering in Power BI UV reports 2_05 and 2_06. The changes were validated in UAT and deployed to prod across all environments.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue occurs after a price change because Siebel continues to use cached price data instead of querying the database for the updated value. New prices are retrieved correctly because no corresponding cache record exists. A custom solution to clear the cache after price changes was being investigated.
important_findings: Siebel stores price data in cache to improve performance.
After a price change, cached price data can prevent retrieval of the updated database price.
New prices are retrieved from the database because no cache record exists for them.
Clearing the Siebel price cache after a price change is required to force a new database query.
A custom solution for cache clearing was under investigation.
investigation_report.root_cause: Siebel retained outdated price data in cache after a price change, preventing a new query to the database for the updated price.

以下の手順で問題を再現しました。
**再現手順:**

4. 架装発注の発注書を承認し、その後、見積を修正する。修正後、架装発注オーダーに見積アイテムが同期される。

Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
After a detailed analysis of this issue, we have identified the root cause. It turns out that when a bodywork order has a negative cost and list price, the sales order's Quote ID is saved, which is causing the issue.
I reproduced the problem using the steps below.
**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Add a bodywork order item to the quote and enter both the list price and cost as negative values.
2. Approve the quote and create an order based on the quote.
3. Approve the order and click the "Create Purchase Order" button to create a purchase order for the bodywork order.
4. Approve the purchase order for the bodywork order and then revise the estimate. After modification, the quoted item is synchronized to the bodywork purchase order.
**Root Cause Analysis (RCA):**
Creating a purchase order for a bodywork order using the Create Purchase Order button triggers a workflow. However, negative price validation breaks this workflow. As a result, the sales order's Quote ID is saved in the bodywork purchase order.
Later, when you amend the quote, it will find all sales orders with the same Quote ID and sync the line items. As a result, bodywork purchase order line items with Quote IDs will also be synchronized with the sales order.
**Reproduction on UAT:**
 - **Bodywork order:** B001292881 (UAT 1)
 - **Sales Order:** A001292880 (UAT 1)
The expected fix date for this issue in the UAT environment is **March 7**.
If you have any questions or need additional support, please let us know.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A bodywork purchase order incorrectly received synchronized quote line items after the related quote was amended. Investigation reproduced the issue when a bodywork order item had negative list price and cost: negative-price validation interrupted the Create Purchase Order workflow, leaving the sales order Quote ID on the bodywork purchase order. A fix was deployed to all FDP UAT environments and released to production on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced by creating a bodywork order item with negative list price and cost, approving the quote and order, and using Create Purchase Order.
Negative-price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by Create Purchase Order.
The interrupted workflow caused the sales order Quote ID to be saved on the bodywork purchase order.
When the quote was amended, synchronization selected all sales orders with the same Quote ID, including the bodywork purchase order.
The issue was reproduced in UAT 1 with bodywork order B001292881 and Sales Order A001292880.
The fix was validated across all FDP UAT environments and deployed to production on March 12, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: Negative-price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by Create Purchase Order, causing the sales order Quote ID to remain saved on the bodywork purchase order. Quote amendment synchronization then updated that bodywork purchase order because it shared the Quote ID.
investigation_report.resolution: A fix was applied across all FDP UAT environments and released to the production environment on March 12, 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Tax Finalization in Registration request failed when creating expense items after a UV Sales Quote was revised and synchronized with its UV Sales Order. The issue was reproduced in UAT-01 for reference order E001292965 and attributed to user changes that interchanged Additional Body and Liability insurance line-item product types before invoice creation. Recovery for the affected record was completed.
important_findings: The user created a UV Sales Order from a UV Sales Quote.
The product type was changed from Additional Body to Liability insurance and then mistakenly changed back to Additional Body, interchanging the line items.
An Expense invoice was created from the Sales Order while the line items were interchanged.
Revising and syncing the UV Sales Quote restored the Additional Body and Liability Insurance line items to their original positions.
Because the invoice had been created from the interchanged line items, Tax Finalization in Registration request returned an error to create the expense for the items.
The issue was replicated in UAT-01 using reference order E001292965.
investigation_report.root_cause: User mis-operation caused Additional Body and Liability insurance line-item product types to be interchanged before Expense invoice creation; a subsequent UV Sales Quote revision and synchronization restored the original line-item positions, creating a mismatch that caused the Tax Finalization expense-creation error.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Incorrect product IDs were assigned to migrated quote line items containing specific option codes, affecting NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders in the Chugoku environment. Investigation identified duplicate product-name records in the product master with different product types. All identified impacted records were recovered after business hours, and the issue was reported not to recur when processing migrated data or copying migrated NV Quotes.
important_findings: Product master contained duplicate records for product names "AE", "AD", "AF", "4A", "FD", and "BB".
For each duplicate product name, one record had product type "Parts" and the other had product type "Options".
Migrated quote line items containing the affected option codes received incorrect product IDs.
The issue could also occur when a user copied a migrated NV Sales Quote and created a new record in Chugoku.
A list of impacted NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders was identified, and recovery for all impacted records was completed.
investigation_report.root_cause: Duplicate product-name records in the product master for "AE", "AD", "AF", "4A", "FD", and "BB", with conflicting product types "Parts" and "Options", caused incorrect product IDs to be populated on migrated quote line items containing those option codes.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed for all identified impacted NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders. The issue was confirmed not to recur when users process migrated data or copy from migrated NV Quotes.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned FDP behavior for parts internal orders, including an error when creating a parts order and incorrect inventory name field editability. Investigation confirmed that FDP logic differed from SC. The corrected logic was validated in FDP UAT-1 and released to production on March 26, 2025.
important_findings: FDP logic differed from SC for parts internal order inventory name field editability.
The inventory name field must be non-editable when Already Issued, Already Reserved, or Processed Qty is not 0.
The inventory name field must be editable only when Already Issued, Already Reserved, and Processed Qty are all 0.
Initial FDP UAT-1 fixes did not pass confirmation; additional feedback was addressed before the final UAT fix.
The final fix was applied to FDP UAT-1, approved for PROD deployment, and released to production on March 26, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: FDP logic for parts internal order inventory name field editability was not aligned with SC specifications based on Already Issued, Already Reserved, and Processed Qty values.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the FDP logic in FDP UAT-1 to match SC behavior and released the approved fix to production on March 26, 2025.

本件について詳細に分析した結果、根本原因を特定しました。架装発注に負のコストおよびリスト価格が設定されている場合、販売オーダーのQuote IDが保存され、それが問題を引き起こしていることが判明しました。 
 
以下の手順で問題を再現しました。 
 
**再現手順:** 
1. 見積に架装発注アイテムを追加し、リスト価格とコストの両方を負の値で入力する。 
2. 見積を承認し、その見積を基にオーダーを作成する。 
3. オーダーを承認し、「Create Purchase Order」ボタンをクリックして架装発注の発注書を作成する。 
4. 架装発注の発注書を承認し、その後、見積を修正する。修正後、架装発注オーダーに見積アイテムが同期される。 
 
**根本原因分析 (RCA):** 
「Create Purchase Order」ボタンを使用して架装発注の発注書を作成すると、ワークフローがトリガーされます。しかし、負の価格のバリデーションによってこのワークフローが中断されます。その結果、架装発注オーダーに販売オーダーのQuote IDが保存されます。 
その後、見積を修正すると、同じQuote IDを持つすべての販売オーダーを検索し、行アイテムを同期します。このため、Quote IDを持つ架装発注オーダーの行アイテムも、販売オーダーと一緒に同期されてしまいます。

- **販売オーダー:** A001292880 (UAT 1)

Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support. 
 
After a detailed analysis of this issue, we have identified the root cause. It turns out that when a bodywork order has a negative cost and list price, the sales order's Quote ID is saved, which is causing the issue. 
 
I reproduced the problem using the steps below. 
 
**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Add a bodywork order item to the quote and enter both the list price and cost as negative values. 
2. Approve the quote and create an order based on the quote. 
3. Approve the order and click the "Create Purchase Order" button to create a purchase order for the bodywork order. 
4. Approve the purchase order for the bodywork order and then revise the estimate. After modification, the quoted item is synchronized to the bodywork purchase order. 
 
**Root Cause Analysis (RCA):**
Creating a purchase order for a bodywork order using the Create Purchase Order button triggers a workflow. However, negative price validation breaks this workflow. As a result, the sales order's Quote ID is saved in the bodywork purchase order. 
Later, when you amend the quote, it will find all sales orders with the same Quote ID and sync the line items. As a result, bodywork purchase order line items with Quote IDs will also be synchronized with the sales order. 
 
**Reproduction on UAT:**
- **Bodywork order:** B001292881 (UAT 1)
- **Sales Order:** A001292880 (UAT 1)
 
The expected fix date for this issue in the UAT environment is **March 7**. 
 
If you have any questions or need additional support, please let us know.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A bodywork purchase order incorrectly retained the originating sales order's Quote ID when created from a quote containing negative list price and cost. Negative price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order", causing later quote amendments to synchronize sales-order line items to the bodywork purchase order. A fix was validated across FDP UAT environments and deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT1 with Bodywork order B001292881 and Sales Order A001292880.
A bodywork order item with both negative list price and negative cost triggered the failure path.
The "Create Purchase Order" workflow was interrupted by negative price validation.
The interrupted workflow saved the sales order's Quote ID on the bodywork purchase order.
When the quote was amended, line-item synchronization selected all sales orders sharing the Quote ID, including the bodywork purchase order.
The fix was applied to all FDP UAT environments and released to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: Negative price validation broke the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order" for a bodywork order with negative cost and list price, causing the sales order's Quote ID to be saved on the bodywork purchase order. Subsequent quote amendments synchronized line items to that bodywork purchase order because it shared the Quote ID.
investigation_report.resolution: A fix was deployed across all FDP UAT environments and then applied to the production environment in the March 12, 2025 release.

**■ 問題の概要** 
本件はデータ移行に起因して発生しました。

請求書ステータスが **「完了」** の場合、本来であれば請求書の **行番号**（中国環境）が **「税金」** タイプの注文明細に紐づくはずでした。

該当レコードを修正し、中国環境の **新しい行番号** に紐づける対応を実施しました。
**■ 再発防止策** 
本件はデータ移行時の設定ミスによるものであり、今後同様の問題が発生しないよう注意を払います。

Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your help.
Sorry for the late reply.
**■ Problem summary**
This issue occurred due to data migration.
**■ Root cause**
When the invoice status is **Completed**, the invoice **line number** (in China environment) should have been associated with the **``Tax"** type of PO line. 
However, at the time of migration, the invoices were registered with a status of ``Completed'', but the **old line number in the SC environment** was still associated with the **``Tax''** type of PO line.
**■ Countermeasures**
We have corrected the record and linked it to the **new line number** in the Chinese environment.
**■ Recurrence prevention measures**
This issue is due to a configuration error during data migration, and we will take precautions to prevent similar issues from occurring in the future.
Thank you very much for your support.
Hirsch

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Tax confirmation could not be completed for an affected order after data migration. Investigation found that completed invoices retained an old SC environment line number on PO lines of type "Tax" instead of the new China environment line number. The affected record was corrected, enabling the user to proceed with tax confirmation; no additional impacted records were found.
important_findings: The issue affected tax confirmation for order code 0000U05007, with customer payment method Transfer and customer payment date 2025/02/14.
For invoices with status "Completed", the invoice line number in the China environment must be associated with the "Tax" type PO line.
Migrated invoices were registered as "Completed", but "Tax" type PO lines remained associated with the old line number from the SC environment.
The affected record was recovered by linking the "Tax" type PO line to the new China environment line number.
A review found no other records impacted; no additional recovery was required.
investigation_report.root_cause: A data-migration configuration error left the old SC environment invoice line number associated with "Tax" type PO lines for invoices registered as "Completed", rather than associating the new China environment line number.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the affected record by linking its "Tax" type PO line to the new China environment line number, allowing tax confirmation to proceed.

The fix is independent of Consumption Tax Rounding configured in Administration – Sales – Consumption Tax Master.

investigation_report.root_cause: UV Quote used different rounding and additional cost price calculation logic than UV Sales Order when calculating Sales Profit, causing inconsistent Profit Amount values.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate Premium Payment records with blank PPR# were identified for multiple orders in FDP and also in SC. Investigation found that SonpoWeb triggers IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) during daily settlement processing, and Siebel creates records from the decoded interface payload when the received Policy Number exists. The behavior was confirmed as functioning as expected; duplicate records were cancelled and the ticket was dismissed.
important_findings: Duplicate Premium Payment records with blank PPR# were found for orders Q019496832, Q034399511, and Q036345352.
The duplicate records were created through SonpoWeb calls to IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation).
Daily settlement processing triggers IFIN010 (Daily Settlement) from Siebel to SonpoWeb and IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) from SonpoWeb to Siebel.
Siebel decodes the IFIN011 payload, extracts settlement and premium values, and creates a record when the received Policy Number exists.
SC has the same functionality and contained 18 duplicate records; Chugoku had no new duplicate records since March 3, 2025.
The functionality was determined to be working as expected, with no interface-process change identified.
investigation_report.root_cause: SonpoWeb triggered IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) with additional clearance-data details, and Siebel created Premium Payment records from the decoded payload when the received Policy Number existed.
investigation_report.resolution: Duplicate Premium Payment records were updated to "Cancelled". No functional change was made; the behavior was accepted as expected and the ticket was dismissed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate Recycle Fee Orders were created for vehicles and affected delivery approval processing. Investigation identified duplicated D21F file processing and confirmed that users entering recycling confirmation in VOW triggered the issue. All affected duplicate orders were recovered across FDP environments; prevention requires users to stop entering recycling confirmation in VOW or a Change Request affecting Siebel and ODI.
important_findings: Two D21F files were received for the same VIN, creating duplicate records: D21F_08012025113917 and D21F_10022025113525.
Under the current specification, receipt of a D21F file creates a Recycle Fee Order for the respective vehicle.
The issue was determined to occur when users entered recycling confirmation from VOW.
Duplicate Recycle Fee Orders were recovered in all FDP environments.
If VOW recycling confirmation cannot be discontinued, a Change Request is required for changes to both Siebel and ODI.
investigation_report.root_cause: Users entered recycling confirmation in VOW, resulting in duplicated D21F file processing and duplicate Recycle Fee Orders mapped to the Sales order.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered all affected duplicate Recycle Fee Orders in all FDP environments. Users were to be instructed to stop entering recycling confirmation in VOW; otherwise, a Change Request is required for Siebel and ODI changes.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: During data migration, an unpopulated backend column on the Siebel side caused missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report. All records affected by the migration issue were recovered. Two Sales Orders, A003403571 and A017304950, had a separate trade-in amount issue caused by FDP ODI logic; the code fix was applied in all UAT environments and production release was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3470.
important_findings: A backend column on the Siebel side was not populated during data migration, causing missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report.
Multiple impacted Sales Orders were recovered for the data-migration issue.
Sales Orders A003403571 and A017304950 remained at Trade-in Price Total 0 because they did not meet ODI logic conditions.

The issue can be reproduced when an NV Sales Order with a trade-in is posted, the related UV Purchase Order is stocked in, and the stocked-in UV Purchase Order is used for a new UV Sales Order; the NV sales order trade-in amount becomes 0 in PBI report NV_3-06.
The ODI behavior was common across FDPs and had been resolved in SC through Incident INC4242736.
Required FDP ODI code changes were applied across all UAT environments and UAT was approved.
investigation_report.root_cause: A backend column on the Siebel side was not populated during data migration, resulting in missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report.
investigation_report.resolution: All records impacted by the data-migration issue were recovered. The separate FDP ODI logic fix was applied in all UAT environments, approved for release to PROD, and tracked under MFTBCFFR-3470.

comments.text:
Thank you for your ongoing support.
Please check the RCA for this issue below and Let us know if you have any query.
1.First user created External WO :- 1-E6M77 on 2025/01/29 03:54:31 PM and respective SPO :- J000188523
For this WO Work Start Date/Time is 2025/01/30 06:46:06 PM and Work completion date/time :- 2025/01/30 06:46:08 PM
 
Please note that in SPO Work Start Date/Time and Work completion date/time populated from JC Header.
For JC Header Work Start Date/Time is the Start time of WO in which work is started first (in this case 1-E6M77) and Work completion date/time is Completion time of the Last WO (in this case 1-E4SST, Work completion date/time :- 2025/01/30 06:46:45 PM).
As SPO status set to Completion of Acceptance Inspection JV is created and Posting date in JV has the value of Work completion date/time field of the SPO. 
posting date set to 30/01/2025 for JV of SPO J000188523.
 
2. Now, User created another External WO :- 1-F9HQT on 2025/02/19 01:57:28 PM and respective SPO :- J000192078 in Re-edit mode.
For this WO Work Start Date/Time is 2025/02/19 02:05:03 PM and Work completion date/time :- 2025/02/19 02:05:04 PM.
 
For JC Header Work Start Date/Time is the Start time of first WO (same as before 1-E6M77) and Work completion date/time is Completion time of the Last WO (in this case 1-F9HQT, Work completion date/time :- 2025/02/19 02:05:04 PM).
As SPO status set to Completion of Acceptance Inspection JV is created and Posting date in JV has the value of Work completion date/time field of the SPO. 
posting date still set to 30/01/2025 for JV of SPO J000192078 because Work completion date/time of last WO 1-F9HQT is not set to the JC Header.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A re-edited External WO caused the JV Posting Date for SPO J000192078 to remain at 2025/01/30 while the related work completed on 2025/02/19. Investigation confirmed that the work completion date/time for External WO 1-F9HQT was not updated in the JC Header before JV creation; the JC Header was only updated after Generate Approval was clicked in the MF Job Card Detail Applet. A fix was validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to PROD on March 12.
important_findings: SPO work start date/time and work completion date/time are sourced from the JC Header.
A JV is created when an SPO reaches "Completion of Acceptance Inspection", and its Posting Date is based on the SPO work completion date/time.
For re-edited External WO 1-F9HQT, the JC Header retained the previous completion date, causing the JV for SPO J000192078 to use Posting Date 2025/01/30.
The JC Header work completion date/time was updated to 2025/02/19 14:05:04 only after Generate Approval was clicked in the MF Job Card Detail Applet.
Updating the JC Header after JV creation caused a date/time mismatch between the JV and the SPO screen.
The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1 before production deployment.
investigation_report.root_cause: The work completion date/time of re-edited External WO 1-F9HQT was not correctly set in the JC Header before the JV was created, so the JV used the prior JC Header/SPO completion date of 2025/01/30.
investigation_report.resolution: A fix was implemented and validated in FDP UAT-1, then deployed to PROD in the March 12 release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The SPO JV Posting Date was derived from the Job Card Work Completion Date. For Service Purchase Orders, the JV was created before the Work Completion Date was changed, causing the SPO JV to retain the old date. The shared fix for MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348 was completed in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to production on March 12.
important_findings: JV Posting Date is sourced from the Job Card field Work Completion Date.
For Service Purchase Orders, the JV is created before the Job Card Work Completion Date is changed.
The sequence caused the SPO JV Posting Date to use the previous Work Completion Date.
MFTBCFFR-3337, MFTBCFFR-3347, and MFTBCFFR-3348 required the same fix and were tracked under MFTBCFFR-3348.
The fix was completed in FDP UAT-1 and applied to production in the March 12 release.
investigation_report.root_cause: For Service Purchase Orders, the JV was created before the Job Card Work Completion Date was updated, so the SPO JV Posting Date retained the old Work Completion Date.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented the shared fix in FDP UAT-1 and deployed it to the production environment in the March 12 release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved missing chassis and option asking prices and costs on the NV Quote. Initial investigation could not reproduce the one-time Production occurrence in UAT, but later testing in RT2 identified pricing issues when the RWD date was removed and re-entered while updating chassis and options. A validation requiring the Desired shipping date before chassis selection was implemented, the error-message wording was corrected, and the fix was released to Production on 12 August 2025.
important_findings: The original Production occurrence was recovered, including the actual cost of options, but could not initially be reproduced in UAT.
When the RWD date was null, the selected chassis price was not displayed on the NV Quote.
In RT2, removing the RWD date and updating the chassis, then re-adding the date and updating the chassis, resulted in chassis pricing being displayed while option pricing became null.
The reported issue concerned missing asking price and cost for both chassis and option prices, not only blank chassis pricing.
Backend investigation attributed the zero-cost issue to the selected line options.
The validation message was corrected to use "Desired shipping date" rather than "scheduled shipping date".
investigation_report.root_cause: A null RWD date caused selected chassis pricing not to display; the zero-cost condition was attributed to the selected line options.
investigation_report.resolution: Added validation requiring users to enter the Desired shipping date before selecting a chassis, corrected the validation-message wording, and released the changes to Production on 12 August 2025.

During Customer AR data updates, module flags were not updated when one NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department code was blank and the others were "9999".
If a module's responsible department is "9999", its corresponding module open flag must be removed; this applies to NV and the other modules.
Recovery was completed in UAT8 before being performed in Chugoku Production.
Recovery was completed in Chugoku Production.
investigation_report.root_cause: During Customer AR data updates, module flags were not updated when one of the NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department codes was blank and the remaining codes were "9999".
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the affected Customer AR module open flags through recovery in UAT8 and subsequently in Chugoku Production, removing each module's open flag when its responsible department was "9999".

The JMS connection pool was increased from 60 to 90 to accommodate requests from all FDPs.
The change was released to production on 26/02/2025 and required no Siebel changes.
investigation_report.root_cause: JMS connections were disconnected during TOB response processing, preventing TOB responses from being reflected in the UI.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Okinawa experienced spreadsheet creation failures caused by duplicate spreadsheet serial numbers, despite having only one agency. Investigation found that serial numbers were generated from 0001 for each Ejibai ID, which could collide with an existing spreadsheet having the same insurance company code, year, and serial number in Completed or Approved status. Tokyo Marine was requested to add codes individually so each branch can create spreadsheets separately.
important_findings: The suspected extra-zero issue in the ID was ruled out; the Siebel configuration matched the provided Excel configuration.
Unlike Shikoku and Wakayama, where multiple agency codes caused serial-number overlap, Okinawa had one agency but received multiple requests with the same serial number.
For each Ejibai ID, the spreadsheet serial number was generated starting from 0001.
A new spreadsheet creation fails when a spreadsheet with the same insurance company code, year, and serial number already exists in Completed or Approved status.
The E column in the E-JiBAI Web ID Master file was blank for Okinawa; confirmation was requested regarding bulk-settlement authorization for registered users.
investigation_report.root_cause: Spreadsheet serial numbers were generated from 0001 per Ejibai ID, resulting in duplicate serial-number collisions with existing spreadsheets for the same insurance company code and year.
investigation_report.resolution: Tokyo Marine was requested to add codes individually so that each branch can create spreadsheets separately.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Report data was missing after the IKM was changed in ODI under MFTBCFFR-3269. The initial full load behavior deleted records from the DataMart table. The DataMart backup was used to recover affected data across environments, and reports now display the recovered records; Aomori remains empty because it has no records with qualifying report statuses.
important_findings: The IKM in ODI was changed from IKM Insert Global to IKM Incremental Update under MFTBCFFR-3269.
After the IKM change, the IKM initially ran as a full load rather than an incremental load.
The full load deleted records from the DataMart table, causing missing report data.
A backup of the DataMart table containing the old records was available during recovery.
Recovery was completed for all environments and data became visible in reports.
The Aomori report has no records because it only includes records with status code "Internal Posted" or "Expired", and no Aomori records meet those conditions.
investigation_report.root_cause: Changing the ODI IKM from IKM Insert Global to IKM Incremental Update caused the IKM to initially run as a full load, deleting records from the DataMart table.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the DataMart table records from the available backup and completed recovery across all environments.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An ODI package IKM issue caused updated records to be inserted into the fact table rather than updated, resulting in duplicate Security No.# values and incorrect commission fees. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to PROD in all environments, after which duplicates were removed and commission fees were corrected. A separate 6_10 report issue was traced to an ODI X_INS_TYPE filter that excluded records from insertion into the DataMart table.
important_findings: The ODI package IKM processed record updates as inserts into the fact table.
This behavior created duplicate Security No.# records and affected commission fee values.
The ODI fix was validated in FDP UAT, where duplicate Security No.# records were no longer present.
Changes were deployed to PROD in all environments, correcting duplicate Security No.# records and commission fees.
Data was visible in the 6_02 report.
The 6_10 report omitted records because the ODI X_INS_TYPE filter only included 'Voluntary Automobile', 'Voluntary Other', 'Voluntary Fire', and 'Life Insurance' values.
investigation_report.root_cause: The ODI package IKM inserted updated records into the fact table instead of updating existing records. Separately, the ODI X_INS_TYPE filter excluded non-matching records from the DataMart table, preventing them from appearing in the 6_10 report.
investigation_report.resolution: The ODI changes were validated in FDP UAT and deployed to PROD in all environments, eliminating duplicate Security No.# records and correcting commission fees.

Multiple UV Purchase Orders with the same assessment number can also be valid when an NV quote contains multiple quantities or when an NV order is canceled.

The quote-revision duplicate-PO fix passed UAT using the flow: create Trade-In Quote and SO, approve SO, create revised quote, approve revised quote, and verify no duplicate UV Purchase Order is created.
The fix was deployed to UAT1 and UAT8 before release to the FDP production environment.
The multiple-quantity scenario required separate process changes and was not included in the completed quote-revision fix.
The SC version required a separate release planned for February 25, 2025 and SNOW incident tracking.
investigation_report.root_cause: A defect in the Trade-in quote-revision flow created an additional UV Purchase Order after approval of a revised NV quote, reusing the same assessment number.
investigation_report.resolution: Canceled confirmed duplicate UV Purchase Orders and deployed a fix preventing duplicate UV Purchase Order creation after revised quote approval to the FDP production environment on February 18, 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The recycle-fee submission issue to TOB was caused by duplicate vehicle records with the same recycle fee ticket number. The duplication was reproduced in UAT and traced to a VIN# change occurring after the vehicle had already been migrated, causing the vehicle delta-data import program to create a new record because VIN# is its user key. All identified affected records were recovered under MFTBCFFR-3168.
important_findings: The issue occurs when a vehicle is duplicated with the same recycle fee ticket number, preventing correct recycle-fee processing to TOB.
Vehicle "BE740G-400580" was initially created in SC Prod from a TCB01 file with both Fuso reception # and VIN# set to "046754".
The vehicle was migrated to FDP Chugoku before D21A from TOB updated its VIN# to "BE740G-400580".
During vehicle delta-data migration, the import program treated the updated VIN# as a user key and created a new vehicle record.
The user submitted the recycle fee to TOB before the duplicate-vehicle recovery was completed.
All impacted records, not only the reported order, were recovered as part of MFTBCFFR-3168.
investigation_report.root_cause: A vehicle was migrated while its VIN# was "046754", then D21A updated the VIN# to "BE740G-400580". During subsequent vehicle delta-data migration, the import program used VIN# as its user key and created a duplicate vehicle record.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered all identified impacted duplicate-vehicle records under MFTBCFFR-3168, including the reported order.
