comments.author: Abhishek Singh.
comments.text:
We have analyzed this issue and we found that while performing recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, we had checked that duplicate recycle fee orders were existing for the attached vehicles.
 * When performing recovery for duplicate recycle fee orders, we check which recycle fee order is mapped to the chassis order and is visible on UI under the chassis order screen. 
 * Furthermore, we check if the TOB status and message is present in the recycle fee order and if so, we consider the one with TOB status and message as the final one and unmap the one that has null value for TOB status and message.
 * All the duplicate recycle fee orders were in 'Pending' status and their TOB status and message was null.
 * Only difference in the duplicate recycle fee orders was their 'Created' date.
 * So we unmapped the recycle fee orders with older 'Created' date and kept the latest 'Created' recycle fee orders that were mapped to the chassis order. 
 * While doing so, we missed the fact that the older 'Created' recycle fee order could be mapped to a sales order.
 * As a result, we updated the status of the latest 'Created' recycle fee order which was visible on UI and was visible under the chassis order screen and unmapped the older 'Created' recycle fee order from the vehicle, due to which it was also unmapped from the Sales order causing this issue.
As a precautionary measure to avoid such occurrence in the future, we will add one more step in our SOP while checking for duplicate recycle fee orders to check if they are mapped to any Sales order.
Kindly let us know if you have any further queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

角田さん、
いつもお世話になっております。
本件について調査を行った結果、Jira MFTBCFFR-3159 のリカバリーを実施する際に、対象車両に対して重複したリサイクル料金オーダーが存在していることを確認しました。
重複したリサイクル料金オーダーのリカバリーを行う際、どのオーダーがシャシーオーダーにマッピングされ、UI 上のシャシーオーダー画面で表示されているかを確認します。
さらに、リサイクル料金オーダーに TOB ステータスおよびメッセージが存在するかを確認し、存在する場合はそのオーダーを最終的なものとし、TOB ステータスおよびメッセージが null のオーダーをアンマップします。
確認したところ、すべての重複したリサイクル料金オーダーは「Pending」ステータスであり、TOB ステータスおよびメッセージは null でした。
これらのオーダーの唯一の違いは「作成日（Created）」だったため、作成日が古いオーダーをアンマップし、最新の作成日のオーダーをシャシーオーダーにマッピングした状態で保持しました。
しかし、この作業の際に、古い作成日のリサイクル料金オーダーが受注（Sales Order）にマッピングされている可能性を見落としていました。
その結果、UI 上で表示され、シャシーオーダー画面に表示されていた最新の作成日のリサイクル料金オーダーのステータスを更新し、古い作成日のリサイクル料金オーダーを車両からアンマップしました。
これにより、受注からもアンマップされてしまい、本件の問題が発生しました。
今後、同様の問題を防ぐため、重複したリサイクル料金オーダーを確認する際には、それらが受注にマッピングされているかどうかを追加で確認する手順を SOP に追加いたします。
ご不明点がございましたら、お知らせください。
よろしくお願いいたします。

Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
As a result of investigating this issue, we have confirmed that when performing the recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, there was a duplicate recycling fee order for the target vehicle.
When recovering duplicate recycle fee orders, check which orders are mapped to chassis orders and displayed on the chassis orders screen on the UI.
Additionally, it checks if the TOB status and message exist on the recycling fee order, makes it final if it exists, and unmaps orders with null TOB status and message.
I checked and found that all duplicate recycling fee orders were in a "Pending" status with a null TOB status and message.
The only difference between these orders was the "Created" date, so we unmapped the orders with the older creation dates and kept the orders with the latest creation dates mapped to the chassis orders.
However, during this process, they overlooked the possibility that recycling fee orders with old creation dates were mapped to Sales Orders.
As a result, we updated the status of recycle fee orders with the most recent creation date displayed on the UI and displayed on the Chassis Order screen, and unmapped recycle fee orders with older creation dates from the vehicle.
As a result, it was also unmapped from the order, causing this issue.
To prevent similar issues in the future, we will add a step to our SOPs when reviewing duplicate recycling fee orders to ensure they are mapped to a sales order.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: During recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicles. important_findings: Duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicles during recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159.
All duplicate recycle fee orders were in Pending status and had null TOB status and message.
The only observed difference between duplicate orders was the Created date; older orders were unmapped and latest orders retained for the chassis order.
The older recycle fee order was mapped to a Sales Order, which was overlooked during recovery.
Unmapping the older recycle fee order from the vehicle also unmapped it from the Sales Order.
investigation_report.root_cause: During duplicate recycle fee order recovery, an older order mapped to a Sales Order was unmapped based solely on its older Created date, causing it to be unmapped from the Sales Order.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the records attached to this Jira and added a planned SOP check to verify whether duplicate recycle fee orders are mapped to any Sales Order before unmapping them.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Invoice C050006192 did not trigger the approval flow because it inherited a Dummy primary position from sales order A030793563. The sales order primary position was Dummy because position mapping for the primary position in the order's SC was not provided. The required corrective action is to change the missing position mapping through a service request.
important_findings: Sales order A030793563 had a Dummy primary position.
Position mapping was not provided for the primary position in the sales order's SC.
Invoice C050006192 copies its primary position from the sales order.
Invoice C050006192 had position type Dummy, which prevented the approval flow from being triggered.
The position mapping must be changed through a service request.
investigation_report.root_cause: Missing business-provided position mapping for the primary position in the sales order's SC caused sales order A030793563 to use a Dummy primary position, which was copied to invoice C050006192 and prevented approval-flow triggering.
investigation_report.resolution: Raise a service request to change the missing position mapping.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident affected Planned Expenses with "Open" and "Pending Approval" statuses. Investigation identified 647 affected records, all of which were recovered. The issue occurred when users processed or copied a Planned Invoice of a Job Card migrated from SC Prod because its "BranchId" had not been updated.
important_findings: Chugoku's Approval Matrix handles approval requests from "Branch-Assistant-Staff" in the same way as SC.
The requested Planned Expense status changes included "Pending Approval" to "Cancelled" for I036763022/2-432343562 and I036678507/2-433752822(Add).
A total of 647 records with "Open" and "Pending Approval" status had the same issue.
The issue was reproduced/investigated in the UAT environment.
The "BranchId" was not updated on Planned Invoices of Job Cards migrated from SC Prod.
Processing or copying a migrated Planned Invoice triggered the issue.
investigation_report.root_cause: "BranchId" was not updated in the Planned Invoice of a Job Card migrated from SC Prod; processing or copying that migrated Planned Invoice caused the issue.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered all 647 affected records, including changing the requested Planned Expense statuses from "Pending Approval" to "Cancelled".

comments.text:
We have analyzed this issue and we found that while performing recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, we had checked that duplicate recycle fee orders were existing for the attached vehicles.
 * When performing recovery for duplicate recycle fee orders, we check which recycle fee order is mapped to the chassis order and is visible on UI under the chassis order screen. 
 * Furthermore, we check if the TOB status and message is present in the recycle fee order and if so, we consider the one with TOB status and message as the final one and unmap the one that has null value for TOB status and message.
 * All the duplicate recycle fee orders were in 'Pending' status and their TOB status and message was null.
 * Only difference in the duplicate recycle fee orders was their 'Created' date.
 * So we unmapped the recycle fee orders with older 'Created' date and kept the latest 'Created' recycle fee orders that were mapped to the chassis order. 
 * While doing so, we missed the fact that the older 'Created' recycle fee order could be mapped to a sales order.
 * As a result, we updated the status of the latest 'Created' recycle fee order which was visible on UI and was visible under the chassis order screen and unmapped the older 'Created' recycle fee order from the vehicle, due to which it was also unmapped from the Sales order causing this issue.
As a precautionary measure to avoid such occurrence in the future, we will add one more step in our SOP while checking for duplicate recycle fee orders to check if they are mapped to any Sales order.
Kindly let us know if you have any further queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

本件について調査を行った結果、Jira MFTBCFFR-3159 のリカバリーを実施する際に、対象車両に対して重複したリサイクル料金オーダーが存在していることを確認しました。
重複したリサイクル料金オーダーのリカバリーを行う際、どのオーダーがシャシーオーダーにマッピングされ、UI 上のシャシーオーダー画面で表示されているかを確認します。
さらに、リサイクル料金オーダーに TOB ステータスおよびメッセージが存在するかを確認し、存在する場合はそのオーダーを最終的なものとし、TOB ステータスおよびメッセージが null のオーダーをアンマップします。
確認したところ、すべての重複したリサイクル料金オーダーは「Pending」ステータスであり、TOB ステータスおよびメッセージは null でした。
これらのオーダーの唯一の違いは「作成日（Created）」だったため、作成日が古いオーダーをアンマップし、最新の作成日のオーダーをシャシーオーダーにマッピングした状態で保持しました。
しかし、この作業の際に、古い作成日のリサイクル料金オーダーが受注（Sales Order）にマッピングされている可能性を見落としていました。
その結果、UI 上で表示され、シャシーオーダー画面に表示されていた最新の作成日のリサイクル料金オーダーのステータスを更新し、古い作成日のリサイクル料金オーダーを車両からアンマップしました。
これにより、受注からもアンマップされてしまい、本件の問題が発生しました。
今後、同様の問題を防ぐため、重複したリサイクル料金オーダーを確認する際には、それらが受注にマッピングされているかどうかを追加で確認する手順を SOP に追加いたします。

よろしくお願いいたします。

Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
After investigating this issue, we found that when performing the recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, there was a duplicate recycling fee order for the target vehicle.
When recovering duplicate recycle fee orders, check which orders are mapped to chassis orders and displayed on the chassis orders screen on the UI.
Additionally, it checks if the TOB status and message exist on the recycling fee order, makes it final if it exists, and unmaps orders with null TOB status and message.
I checked and found that all duplicate recycling fee orders were in a "Pending" status with a null TOB status and message.
The only difference between these orders was the "Created" date, so we unmapped the orders with the older creation dates and kept the orders with the latest creation dates mapped to the chassis orders.
However, during this process, they overlooked the possibility that recycling fee orders with old creation dates were mapped to Sales Orders.
As a result, we updated the status of recycle fee orders with the most recent creation date displayed on the UI and displayed on the Chassis Order screen, and unmapped recycle fee orders with older creation dates from the vehicle.
As a result, it was also unmapped from the order, causing this issue.
To prevent similar issues in the future, we will add a step to our SOPs when reviewing duplicate recycling fee orders to ensure they are mapped to a sales order.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Thank you for your support.

The PO Allocation received on 2025/01/31 had a D2S timestamp earlier than the latest allocation received on 2025/01/29.
The D2S team was requested to investigate why the allocation was sent to Siebel on 2025/01/31.

This issue is caused by concurrent loading of transactional data in FDP Chugoku, resulting in high database memory usage and processing halts.
After getting IT approval, we adjusted the database parameters to resolve memory-related issues (same as 3184 for analysis).

investigation_report.investigation_summary: D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing stopped because of a database-related error, making the Chassis order unavailable on FDP-Aomori. Database parameters were adjusted with IT approval, and the production fix was applied through MFTBCFFR-3174; no recurrence was reported.
important_findings: D21N, D21R, and D21F files were not executed on the morning of the 24th.
Log analysis identified a database-related error that stopped file processing.
Concurrent transactional-data loading in FDP Chugoku caused high database memory usage and processing halts.
Database parameters were adjusted to address the memory-related issue, using the same analysis approach as 3184.
An alert function was added to notify the AMS team if an ODI package fails.
The fix was deployed to prod through JIRA MFTBCFFR-3174.
investigation_report.root_cause: Concurrent loading of transactional data in FDP Chugoku increased database memory usage, causing a database-related error and halting D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing.
investigation_report.resolution: Database parameters were adjusted with IT approval to resolve the memory-related issue, and the fix was applied to prod through MFTBCFFR-3174. An alert function was added to notify the AMS team when an ODI package fails.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Sales Order approval failed when the associated Recycle Fee Order had the status "Recycle Order Changed", which occurs after using "Change Order" in the Recycle Fee Order Applet. The approval logic was updated and verified in UAT1 using a designated chassis order. The fix was deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
important_findings: Using "Change Order" in the Recycle Fee Order Applet changes the Recycle Fee Order status to "Recycle Order Changed".
Sales Orders could not be approved while the associated Recycle Fee Order was in "Recycle Order Changed" status.
CR-0697 was reported as deployed to SC on December 19, 2022; its availability in FDP/Okayama Fuso was disputed during the investigation.
The updated UAT logic allowed approval of Sales Orders with Recycle Fee Order status "Recycle Order Changed".
UAT1 chassis order B001249837 was provided for validation, with associated Recycle Fee Order B001249897.
The fix was applied to PROD in the March 12 production release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Sales Order approval logic did not support approval when the associated Recycle Fee Order status was "Recycle Order Changed".
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the approval logic to allow Sales Order approval for Recycle Fee Orders in "Recycle Order Changed" status, validated it in UAT1, and deployed it to PROD on March 12, 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Sales Price mismatch between Siebel and FDP PBI reports was traced to ODI logic handling Billing Rate Type values. The logic did not correctly recognize the labor product 'FDP Rate' for FDP Shikoku order I00006001, causing the Sales Price to differ between Siebel and PBI. The ODI logic was corrected, validated in FDP UAT5 using order I000035271, and released to production in the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
important_findings: The incident involved mismatched Sales Price values between Siebel and the FDP PBI report.
For FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001, line item 1-1A8DK0 had labor product 'FDP Rate', which did not satisfy the ODI Sales Price logic.
The ODI logic was expected to include 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', but incorrect values such as 'FDP???' and '?????????' were observed.
Recovery was completed for the affected mismatched values, after which Siebel sales prices matched the PBI report.
The corrected logic was verified in FDP UAT5 with ORDER_NUM I000035271 and labor product 'FDP Rate'; values populated correctly in FDP PBI reports.
The ODI change was released to production with the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: ODI Sales Price logic did not correctly match the Billing Rate Type value 'FDP Rate' due to incorrect expected values, so the labor product on FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001 was excluded from Sales Price processing.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified the ODI logic in FDP UAT to correctly handle 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', validated the fix in FDP UAT5, recovered the affected mismatched data, and deployed the change to production on February 8, 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident covered three BIP printing issues: D21A blank output, D21N wrapped multi-line fields, and incorrect D21L-related output. D21A blank output occurred when a schedule package created a record but no file existed to generate a BIP report. All three issues were corrected on UAT1 and released to PROD across all FDP environments on 2025-02-12.
important_findings: D21A prints blank when the schedule package creates a record but no corresponding file exists, so no BIP report is generated.
The original D21N explanation that its format matched all environments, including Shikoku, was rejected; a corrected BIP report was later attached after the issue was resolved.
No D21L file existed; the BIP was being printed from the Reports Tab instead of the "Print" button.
The D21L countermeasure was to remove the report from the Reports Tab.
The fixes applied to all FDP environments, not only Shikoku.
UAT confirmation could not be performed because UAT had not received the TOB batch.
investigation_report.resolution: All three issues were resolved on UAT1 and deployed to PROD on 2025-02-12 as part of the planned FDP release.

important_findings: The issue was reproduced in UAT-1 for JC I001290325.
JC Create Branch Code was 10 (Okayama East Branch) and Location Branch Code was 50 (Okayama West Branch).
The Journal Voucher Department Code was set to 10 (Okayama East Branch), while the expected Department Code or Branch Code required investigation was 50.
The initial KB functionality sets the Journal Voucher Department code to the Branch Code only for this Order Type.
The requirement to set the Department code from the Location code was not implemented since the first FDP and requires an AMS-CR/new CR.
investigation_report.root_cause: The existing KB functionality was designed to populate the Journal Voucher Department code from the Branch Code only; mapping it to the Location code was not implemented.

Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
 Expense charge to in Parts Expense Order and Parts expense order is set by Department code of the order creator. In the record mentioned above (Parts Expense Order : M000004280 and Parts Expense Return Order: M000004307), user D8MAEKAT created these records who have Department code 8030.

Fix Plan: Either we can change the Expense Charge to field mapping in Expense return order where we will show value of the return order rather than parent order expense charge value or we can change the mapping in JV where we will set Parent Order's expense charge to field value in Department Code(CSJS300) of Expense Return Order JV line. 
Kindly validate our analysis and let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
 Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Parts Expense Return Orders displayed the parent order's "Expense Charge To" value in the UI while the return order backend value was based on the return creator's department. The agreed fix copies the original Parts Expense Order's "Expense Charge To" into the expense return order header and updates the UI to display the return order's own stored value. The fix was validated in UAT1 and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
important_findings: For Parts Expense Order M000004280, creator D8MAEKAT had department code 8030, but "Expense Charge To" was manually changed to 8040.
Parts Expense Return Order M000004307 retained 8030 as its backend "Expense Charge To" based on the return-order creator, while the UI displayed 8040 from the parent order.
The same parent-order UI mapping existed in SC.
JV mapping used the Expense Return Order's "Expense Charge To" value in Department Code (CSJS300), creating a mismatch with the UI display.
In UAT1, Expense Order M001290336 was changed from department 1020 to 1030 before creating Expense Return Order M001290337; the return order and its Journal Voucher used 1030.
JV recovery was confirmed as not required.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Parts Expense Return Order UI mapped "Expense Charge To" from the parent order, while the return order header/backend value was independently set from the return creator's department, causing UI and Journal Voucher department-code inconsistency.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified expense-return creation to copy the original expense order's "Expense Charge To" into the expense return order header and changed the Parts Expense Return Order UI to display the return order's own "Expense Charge To" value. The change was tested in UAT1, approved, and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was reproduced on UAT-02 when a Sales Order was cancelled at specified workflow statuses, causing the Vehicle status and sub-status to change to "Sold", "Sold". The behavior originated from logic implemented under FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented. The logic was corrected for UV so that a Vehicle is set to "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete; the change was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
important_findings: On UAT-02, cancelling a Sales Order in Registration Completed, Sales Posting Completed, Delivery Completed, or Delivery Pending Approval updated the Vehicle status and sub-status to "Sold", "Sold".
The behavior was introduced after FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented.
The agreed rule for UV is that Vehicle status becomes "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete.
A Sales Order cancelled before Sales Posting must retain its current Vehicle status.
The initial change was applied to both NV and UV tracks, but NV changes were reverted because NV has different requirements.
The UV fix passed UAT and was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: Cancellation logic introduced after FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented incorrectly updated the Vehicle status and sub-status to "Sold", "Sold" when a UV Sales Order was cancelled before Sales Posting was complete.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the UV cancellation process so that Vehicle status is changed to "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete; cancellations before Sales Posting retain the current Vehicle status. The NV change was reverted, and the UV fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
technical_entities: FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In UV Purchase Quote, the List Applet fetched Assessment number from Vehicle while the Form Applet fetched it from Assessment Request (AR). When a new Assessment Request was created for the same VIN#, the Vehicle Assessment number was updated and older Purchase Quotes displayed the newer number in the List Applet. The fix aligned both applets to fetch Assessment # from AR, was validated in UAT01, and released to production on February 12, 2025.
important_findings: UV Purchase Quotes created from different Assessment numbers but linked to the same VIN# could display an updated Assessment number in the List Applet.
The List Applet sourced Assessment number from Vehicle, whereas the Form Applet sourced it from Assessment Request (AR).
Creating a new Assessment Request for the same Vehicle updated the Vehicle Assessment number, affecting older Purchase Quotes linked to that Vehicle.
The reported behavior initially matched the SC version existing functionality.
The fix was tested on UAT01 using UV Purchase Quote 1-5WJ1LD and UAT passed.
The change was released to production on February 12, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: Inconsistent Assessment number sourcing between the UV Purchase Quote List Applet (Vehicle) and Form Applet (Assessment Request); Vehicle Assessment number updates for the same VIN# changed the value shown for older Purchase Quotes.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the List Applet to fetch Assessment # from AR, matching the Form Applet; validated in UAT01 and deployed to production.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident was recovered successfully. Investigation determined that the user created multiple SRs without completing existing SRs and completed them in a non-chronological order, which led to a rare validation gap where a Module flag could be selected without entering the module's responsible shop code. No further corrective action was implemented under this Jira.
important_findings: The user created multiple SRs before completing the existing SRs and completed the SRs in random order.
The SR created at 2025/01/20 06:39:44 PM was completed at 2025/01/21 09:22:17 AM, after the SR created at 2025/01/20 07:45:08 PM was completed at 2025/01/20 08:07:48 PM.
An existing SR creation validation requires responsible code details when a Module flag is selected.
In this rare completion-order scenario, the user was able to select the Module flag without entering the module's responsible shop code.
A potential future AMS-CR would add validation on the Update AP button requiring existing SRs to be completed or rejected before creating another Update AP SR.
investigation_report.root_cause: User mis-operation: multiple SRs were created without completing existing SRs and then completed in a random, non-chronological order, exposing a rare validation gap.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed. No additional action was taken in this Jira; a future AMS-CR may add Update AP button validation.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: An invoice upsert failed in Siebel with an EAI Siebel Adapter error, and no invoice number was generated. The reported error indicated that no user key could be used for the "MF Ejibai Invoice" Integration Component instance. Subsequent checks found the operation working normally with no further irregularities; the issue remained under production monitoring.
important_findings: The failure occurred at the "Upsert - Invoice" step when invoking the "EAI Siebel Adapter" service using the "Upsert" method.
The reported errors were "SBL-BPR-00162" and "SBL-EAI-04397": "No user key can be used for the Integration Component instance 'MF Ejibai Invoice'."
No Invoice number was generated for the failed transaction.
Invoice number generation uses EAILookupSiebel("MF_EJIBAI_SC_IDENTIFIER", ...).
The team requested the request XML sent by Ejibai to Siebel for further analysis.
Later validation found the operation functioning normally, with no additional user escalations or irregularities observed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Address field in Service Quote BIP was not updated when the corresponding AR address was updated because the two components used different backend Siebel field mappings. The required BIP mapping changes, previously implemented in Wave 1 and Wave 2 production under MFTBCFFR-2575, were applied to FDP UAT-5 and then released to Wave 3 production on January 24. Branch verification was completed and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Service Quote BIP and AR used different backend Siebel field mappings for the Address field.
Because of the mapping discrepancy, Address in Quote BIP was not updated when AR was updated.
The same BIP mapping changes had already been deployed to Wave 1 and Wave 2 production through MFTBCFFR-2575.
The MFTBCFFR-2575 BIP changes were applied on FDP UAT-5 and deployed to Wave 3 production on January 24.
Branch verification was completed after the production release.
investigation_report.root_cause: Different backend Siebel field mappings for the Address field between Service Quote BIP and AR prevented Quote BIP Address updates when AR was updated.
investigation_report.resolution: Applied the BIP mapping changes from MFTBCFFR-2575 to FDP UAT-5 and deployed them to Wave 3 production on January 24.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned a Bank Info/account-name value described as "For business testing". Review of the Siebel response found that this value was not sent by SIEBEL. The issue was confirmed to originate from KB settings, and the incident was rejected as not being a SIEBEL issue.
important_findings: The Siebel response did not contain the account-name value "For business testing".
Bank Info was not an interface value received from SIEBEL.
SIEBEL was sending the correct response.
The affected Branch was asked to check the settings in KB.
The incident was confirmed as a KB-side issue rather than a SIEBEL issue.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect or problematic settings in KB caused the Bank Info/account-name value; the value was not supplied by SIEBEL.
investigation_report.resolution: Branch was requested to check and correct the relevant KB settings; the incident was rejected as not a SIEBEL issue.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Duplicate Recycle fee order records caused TOB responses to update a duplicate order rather than the original, leaving the correct recycling order/TOB status unupdated. The incident was initially attributed to duplicate D21F files, but CIH server logs showed no evidence that the file was sent twice and the reason duplicate files existed on the ODI server remained unknown. A VOW-related explanation was later confirmed to apply to a separate Iwate incident, not this Okinawa incident. Affected records were recovered, and the ticket was ultimately closed as a rare case without a confirmed recurrence-prevention change.
important_findings: Duplicate recycling fee orders caused TOB response data to be reflected on duplicate records instead of the original submitted order.
The same D21F file was observed twice in the system, resulting in duplicate Recycle fee order records.
CIH server logs did not show a history of the D21F file being sent twice.
The cause of two identical files being created on the ODI server was not determined.
The VOW recycling-confirmation input cause applied to a separate Iwate incident and was not applicable to this incident.
Recovery was completed for affected VINs, including updating affected recycling order statuses to Completed.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected recycling order records, including updating their status to Completed. The ticket was placed on HOLD pending recurrence and later closed as a rare case; no preventive system change was documented.

important_findings: Initial investigation identified a possible user misoperation involving an incorrect Ejibai Location code; this code is entered on the Ejibai screen and is not visible in the Siebel UI.

The logged error was "No user key can be used for the Integration Component instance 'MF Ejibai Invoice'.(SBL-EAI-04397)" with parent error "SBL-BPR-00162".
No Invoice number was generated for the failed transaction.
Further analysis required the request XML sent by Ejibai and revalidation of the supplied Ejibai Codes.
The incident was tracked through MFTBCFFR-3045 because it was identified as the same issue.

comments.text:
-San,
As per current logic, Tax is calculated as sum of "Net Price" in Tax & Expenses tab and "Total Selling Price" but if "License Plate Number Fee" and "Illuminated License Plate Number Fee" has price then these prices are subtracted from the Total amount.
Total Amount: 65000
License Plate Number Fee: 6000
Fee License Plate Number Fee: 7000
Consumption Tax Rate: 10
Taxable Amount = 65000 - (6000 + 7000) = 52000
Tax Amount = 5200
This logic is present on all FDPs that  "License Plate Number Fee" and "Illuminated License Plate Number Fee" is subtracted from net taxable amount.
Kindly let us know in case of any queries.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Sales Posting JV amounts and creation behavior for outsourcing orders were inconsistent with the required IBOS and Non-IBOS pricing logic. The existing logic depended on Net Price, causing JV creation to fail when Net Price was absent despite bodywork and other billing amounts being present. The UAT1 fix changed Sales Posting JV creation to evaluate Net Price and Total Selling Price, with the Base Amount set to their sum; the change was validated and released to Prod on 14 May 2025.
important_findings: Initially, JV contained Agency Fee, PO, and CT pricing, while the invoice sent Agency Price plus Total Selling and did not send PO price, causing a JV-to-invoice price difference.
For Non-IBOS cases, Total Selling Price was mapped to JV in UAT1; subsequent changes addressed both IBOS and Non-IBOS logic.
Outsourcing Order A001292536 did not create a Sales Posting JV because Net Price was not set in Taxes & Expenses and the existing creation condition required Net Price to be non-zero.
The required behavior was to create a JV when bodywork and other billing amounts were present, regardless of whether Net Price was set.
The corrected Sales Posting JV Base Amount is Net Price plus Total Selling Price.

JV tax calculation subtracts License Plate Number Fee and Illuminated License Plate Number Fee from the taxable amount; the validated example calculated tax of 5200 from a taxable amount of 52000 at a 10% Consumption Tax Rate.
investigation_report.root_cause: Sales Posting JV creation and Base Amount logic relied on Net Price being non-zero, so no JV was created when Net Price was absent even when Total Selling Price or bodywork and other billing amounts required a JV.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Sales Posting JV condition to check Net Price and Total Selling Price, and set the JV Base Amount to the sum of Net Price and Total Selling Price. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Prod in the 14 May 2025 release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A mismatch between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was reproduced on UAT-4 using two browser sessions. Completing the Shaken Expense in one browser created a Journal Voucher using the original Actual Amount, while a stale second browser session could subsequently overwrite the Actual Expense amount. The fix prevents updates to Actual Amount after the Actual Expense is Completed, and the Journal Voucher difference was recovered.
important_findings: The issue was reproduced on UAT-4 with JC# I000031108 and Expense ID 1-JCL44.
Clicking Done in Browser 1 marked the Shaken Expense as Completed and created a Journal Voucher with Actual Amount 17,400.
Without refreshing Browser 2, changing Weight Tax Actual Amount to 16,800 overwrote the Actual Expense but did not update the existing Journal Voucher.
The resulting discrepancy between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was ▲600.
After the fix, users cannot update Actual Amount from another browser once the Actual Expense is Completed.
investigation_report.root_cause: A stale multi-browser session allowed the Actual Expense Actual Amount to be updated after the record was marked Completed and its Journal Voucher had already been created, causing the Journal Voucher and Actual Expense amounts to diverge.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented a UAT-4 restriction preventing Actual Amount updates in multi-browser sessions after Actual Expense status is Completed, and added the ▲600 difference to the Journal Voucher.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In the Map/Unmap process for UV Purchase Orders, Journal Vouchers were created when Net Price was zero because the required zero-price condition was missing from the DataMap search specification. The condition was added and validated in UATs, preventing JV creation for zero-price Map/Unmap cases while retaining JV creation when Cost fields contain a non-zero value. The fix was released to FDP on 23 January 2025.
important_findings: MAP/UNMAP scenarios in UV Purchase Orders lacked a DataMap search specification condition for Net Price equal to zero.
The missing condition caused Journal Vouchers to be created for zero-price cases.
After the fix, zero-amount Journal Vouchers are not created for Map/Unmap cases.
A Journal Voucher is still created when any Cost field contains a value other than zero, even if the total amount is not zero yen.
The fix was deployed to UATs, passed UAT, and was released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The DataMap search specification for MAP/UNMAP scenarios in UV Purchase Orders did not handle cases where Net Price equals zero.
investigation_report.resolution: Added a Net Price equals zero condition to the DataMap search specification for MAP/UNMAP scenarios, preventing Journal Voucher creation for zero-price cases; released to FDP on 23 January 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In the Okinawa production environment, the Self-Contract flag was read-only for Quote# 1-8KE7V because its Contractant Code, 0000001163, was not included in the configured Own-Company codes. The required Own-Company codes were provided for multiple FDPs and configured in production, including Okinawa code 0000001163. An Own-Company code for Chugoku Fuso remained requested but was not provided in the discussion.
important_findings: The Self-Contract flag can be checked only when the Contractant Code is configured as an Own-Company code.
Quote# 1-8KE7V used Contractant Code 0000001163, which was initially not among the configured codes and therefore showed the Self-Contract flag as read-only.
The existing configuration listed 0000H00031 and 0000GZ6000 for SC use, and 0000108561 for Okayama use.
Production configuration was updated with Own-Company codes for Aomori, Hakodate, Iwate, Wakayama, Shikoku, and Okinawa, including 0000001163 for Okinawa.
The Own-Company code for Chugoku Fuso was still requested after the production configuration update.
investigation_report.root_cause: Contractant Code 0000001163 for Okinawa was not configured as an Own-Company code, causing the Self-Contract flag to remain read-only.
investigation_report.resolution: Configured the provided Own-Company codes in production, including Okinawa Contractant Code 0000001163.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Parts Sales return creation failed when the editable Already Returned Qty field in the shipment screen was set to a value equal to the ordered quantity. The failure was reproduced in UAT-5 and caused the Parts Sales Order screen to update its Already Returned Qty with the shipment-screen value, resulting in the validation "Please enter Return Qty." The field was changed to read-only in the shipment screen, verified in FDP UAT-1, and released to production in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: For SO M000034005 in UAT-5, setting Already Returned Qty in the shipment screen equal to the ordered quantity caused return-order creation to fail.
The displayed validation was "Please enter Return Qty."
After the validation, the Already Returned Qty on the Parts Sales Order screen was updated with the value entered in the shipment screen.
The issue was also reproduced for M000031415 in UAT5, while testing with several other orders did not reproduce it.
Previously affected shipment-line Already Returned Qty values were reset to 0 for SO M000003330 and M000007642 to allow Parts Sales return recreation.
The corrective change made Already Returned Qty read-only in the shipment screen.
investigation_report.root_cause: Already Returned Qty was editable in the shipment screen; entering a value equal to the ordered quantity propagated that value to the Parts Sales Order screen and prevented Parts Sales return creation.
investigation_report.resolution: Made the Already Returned Qty field read-only in the shipment screen, verified the fix in FDP UAT-1, and released it in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: FDP users in Shikoku and Wakayama could not create Liability Insurance policies or select the 11SC Agency code because the Production Pick Applet search specification did not include 11SC. UAT was configured for "= 26SC OR =11SC", while Production was configured only for "=26SC" after CR-820 changes had been migrated in FDP but not yet to Production. The Production configuration was released on 9 January 2025, and a subsequent Pick Applet search-spec data issue was corrected so both agency options became available.
important_findings: UAT search spec was "= 26SC OR =11SC", while Production search spec was "=26SC".
The configuration difference resulted from CR-820 changes being migrated in FDP while the CR had not yet been migrated to Production.
The issue affected FDPs using the 11SC agency, specifically Shikoku and Wakayama.
Users could not select the 11SC Agency code on the Insurance order screen.
A data issue in the Pick Applet search spec was corrected, after which both agency options were available.
investigation_report.root_cause: Production Pick Applet search-spec configuration/data restricted agency selection to 26SC and did not include 11SC. The discrepancy existed because CR-820 changes were present in FDP but had not yet been migrated to Production.
investigation_report.resolution: Released the required search-spec configuration to Production for Shikoku and Wakayama on 9 January 2025, then corrected the Pick Applet search-spec data so users could select both 26SC and 11SC.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Delivery Request Approval failed because vehicle information was inconsistent between related orders. The inconsistency was traced to recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834, where the Sales Order vehicle was updated but the corresponding Body Building Order was not updated for Trailer and Forklift cases. Recovery procedures were updated, and a later validation confirmed consistent Vehicle IDs across associated orders in all production environments.
important_findings: The incident occurred during Delivery Request Approval.
The Body Building Order and Sales Order had different vehicle information for Trailer and Forklift cases.
During recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834, the vehicle was updated in the Sales Order but not in the Body Building Order.
The issue was identified as a manual recovery error rather than a system defect.
Validation across all production environments confirmed that Sales Order, Chassis Order, NV Pool Cost Order, Recycle Fee Order, and NV Body Building Order had the same Vehicle ID.
The Recovery Manual was updated to require vehicle-information updates for all related orders during recovery.
investigation_report.root_cause: Manual recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834 updated vehicle information in the Sales Order but omitted the related Body Building Order, causing inconsistent vehicle information and the Delivery Request Approval error.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Recovery Manual so vehicle information is updated for all related orders during recovery; associated orders were subsequently validated to have consistent Vehicle IDs across all production environments.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect accounting configuration for Trade-In Loss transactions in NV and UV Trade In processes. The configuration was corrected in UAT1, but UAT8 initially failed for SO# E050016909 and Trade-In PO# F050016910, requiring additional changes. After validation, the fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
important_findings: For NV and UV Trade In processes, the Trade in Loss Fuso account code must be configured as the debit account code.
For NV and UV Trade In processes, the Bill to account code must be configured as the credit account code.
The initial UAT1 fix passed UAT approval, but UAT8 failed for SO# E050016909 and Trade-In PO# F050016910.
Additional changes were applied in UAT8 before the PROD release.
The incident was released to PROD on 23 January 2025 through the FDP release.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect debit and credit account-code configuration for Trade-In Loss in NV and UV Trade In processes.
investigation_report.resolution: Configured the Trade in Loss Fuso account code as the debit account code and the Bill to account code as the credit account code, applied additional UAT8 changes, and released the fix to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
technical_entities: Trade in Loss Fuso account code

comments.text:
Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this issue and this is a bug in this functionality. When the user tries to complete the 'Delivery Request', the system checks if their Purchase Orders are mapped to that sales order(UV Purchase Order and UV Pool Cost - Procurement). And we have checked the record that you have provided and in that assessment, the Assessment purpose is 'FUSO Owned Vehicle'. In case of 'FUSO Owned Vehicle', after user approves the assessment request and status changes to 'Assessment Completed', 'Create Verification Request' button is activated and user directly creates the Stock-In Verification request, without creating the UV Purchase Order. Since while completing the delivery request, the system checks for  'UV Purchase Order' and 'UV Pool Cost - Procurement' and in this case, UV Purchase order is not created, the error popped up to map all the key components.
Along with 'FUSO Owned Vehicle', 'Create Verification Request' is active after approving the Assessment request for all the assessments with below listed 'Assessment Purpose':
 * FUSO Owned Vehicle
 * Buyback
 * Monitor Vehicle
 * Cancelled Vehicle
 * Caravan (less than a year)
 * Caravan (more than a year)
We will fix this issue on UAT environment. We can perform recovery for this record, but since Prod release in FDP is halted, we will not be able to release this incident to Prod environments until the next planned Prod release.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

「FUSO Owned Vehicle」の場合、上記の「Assessment Purpose」に該当するすべての査定において、「Create Verification Request」は査定依頼を承認した後にアクティブになります。
FUSO Owned Vehicle
Buyback
Monitor Vehicle

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A functionality defect prevented completion of a Delivery Request for assessments using workflows that allow Stock-In Verification request creation without a UV Purchase Order. The issue was corrected in UAT1, validated successfully with SO# E001290027, and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
important_findings: Delivery Request completion checks that both UV Purchase Order and UV Pool Cost - Procurement are mapped to the corresponding sales order.
For FUSO Owned Vehicle assessments, users can create a Stock-In Verification request after the Assessment request reaches Assessment Completed without creating a UV Purchase Order.
The same Create Verification Request behavior applies to Buyback, Monitor Vehicle, Cancelled Vehicle, Caravan (less than a year), and Caravan (more than a year) assessment purposes.
The missing UV Purchase Order caused the system to display an error requesting all key components to be mapped.
The corrected implementation passed UAT1 validation using SO# E001290027.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Delivery Request completion validation incorrectly required a UV Purchase Order for assessment-purpose workflows that permit Stock-In Verification request creation without a UV Purchase Order.
investigation_report.resolution: The functionality was corrected in UAT1, validated successfully, and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.

Thank you for your ongoing support. We have investigated the issue and found that it is due to a user mis-operation. This is related to FDP UAT-1, Reference JC# I001287533.
Here are the steps we followed to replicate the issue:
1.The user created a Work Order (WO), then created and got approval for a quote. After entering the Arrival Date/Time in the Job Card (JC) header, the JC status changed to "Vehicle Arrived."
2.The user drilled down into the WO, started and stopped the work, then clicked on the "Set Acceptance Inspection" button. The WO status changed to "Acceptance Inspection."
3.Since all WOs are now in "Acceptance Inspection" status, the work completion date/time of the last WO was set to the JC's work completion date/time.
4.The user created a new WO with a template, and the customer approved the quote.
5.The user then drilled down into the new WO, started and stopped the work, and tried to click the "Set Acceptance Inspection" button.
However, this action is not allowed in the SC, as the "Set Acceptance Inspection" button is not active in this case. You can refer to SC JC# I026301176 for more details.
Please let me know if you need any further clarification or assistance.
Regards,
Akash

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A newly added Work Order (WO) was not included when updating the Job Card (JC) Work completion date/time because the WO was added after the JC reached "Maintenance Completed" status. Returning the JC to "Maintenance Started" and changing it back to "Maintenance Completed" updated the last WO date, including the added WO. The system was changed in FDP UAT1 so the JC header [Approval Request] action updates the last WO date, and the verified change was released to PROD on February 26, 2025.
important_findings: The issue occurred when a WO was added after the JC status was "Maintenance Completed".
The "Set Acceptance Inspection" action is not active for a newly added WO when all existing WOs are already in "Acceptance Inspection" status.
Changing the JC from "Maintenance Completed" to "Maintenance Started" and back to "Maintenance Completed" updates the date of the last WO, including an added WO.
The corrective change updates the last WO date, including added WOs, when the [Approval Request] button is clicked in the JC header.
The change was implemented in FDP UAT1, verified in UAT-1 at JC Close, and released to PROD on February 26, 2025.
investigation_report.root_cause: A WO was added when the JC status was "Maintenance Completed", so the added WO was not included in the last WO date update.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified the JC header [Approval Request] action to update the date of the last WO including added WOs; the change was verified in UAT-1 and deployed to PROD on February 26, 2025.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Required records were recovered in Hakodate Prod by running the D21A file, which created the associated Planned Pool Cost Procurement orders and Recycle fee orders. The incident was traced to a defect in an ODI package processing TOB files; an ODI patch was applied on 2025-01-19, and automated ODI email monitoring for unprocessed files was implemented. important_findings: All attached records were recovered in Hakodate Prod, including their Planned Pool Cost Procurement orders and Recycle fee orders.
The incident was caused by an issue in the ODI package responsible for TOB file processing.
An ODI patch addressing the package issue was applied on 2025-01-19.
Automated monitoring now sends email notifications from the ODI system when TOB files remain unprocessed.
MFTBCFFR-3152 was caused by data loading to FDP Chugoku, and MFTBCFFR-3350 was caused by a missing D21A file; neither was caused by the ODI failure.
investigation_report.root_cause: A defect in the ODI package used to process TOB files.
investigation_report.resolution: Applied an ODI patch on 2025-01-19 and implemented automated email monitoring for unprocessed TOB files.

Mr. Tsunoda,
 
Thank you for your continued support.
 
As discussed in the meeting, the current feature details and fix plans are as follows:
 
user steps
1. Estimate revision 1 is created.
2. A sales order is created and remains in "Approving" status.
3. Estimate revision 2 is created.
4. Once quotation revision 2 is approved, if the sales order associated with quotation revision 1 remains in the Approving status, the sales order will be canceled and will not be synchronized with quotation revision 2.
 
Current function of the "Revise" button
1. This button currently picks up the status of the canceled sales order (associated with quote revision 1).
2. The "Modify" button is disabled because the status is "Cancelled".
 
correction plan
1. Check if there are any canceled sales orders in the current quote.
2. If a canceled sales order is associated with the current quote, the "Revise" button will be disabled.
3. In this particular case, there are no sales orders associated with the current quote (Quote Revision 2), so the Revise button remains enabled.
 
Please approve the proposed modification plan in order to proceed with development on UAT1.
 
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us.
 
Thank you for your support.
Laxminarayan Meena

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Revise button was disabled for Quote Revision 2 after the Sales Order associated with Quote Revision 1 was cancelled. Investigation confirmed that the button logic incorrectly picked up the cancelled Sales Order status from the prior quote revision, although no Sales Order was associated with the current quote. The logic was corrected in UAT1 and released to PROD in the 14 January FDP release.
important_findings: Quote Revision 1 had a Sales Order in "Approving" status; when Quote Revision 2 was approved, the prior Sales Order was cancelled and was not synchronized with Quote Revision 2.
The existing Revise button logic evaluated the status of the cancelled Sales Order associated with Quote Revision 1.
Because the evaluated Sales Order status was "Cancelled", the Revise button was disabled for Quote Revision 2.
The intended behavior is to disable the Revise button only when a cancelled Sales Order is associated with the current quote.
UAT1 testing confirmed that the Revise button was active for quotation 1-5SCFIB, revision 2, after the fix.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Revise button logic incorrectly used the cancelled Sales Order associated with the previous quote revision rather than checking for a cancelled Sales Order associated with the current quote.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Revise button logic to check whether a cancelled Sales Order is associated with the current quote and keep the button enabled when no Sales Order is associated with the current quote. The fix was deployed to UAT1 and released to PROD in the 14 January FDP release.
technical_entities: FDP CR NV 14 Sales Revision without Change Order to be implemented

investigation_report.resolution: The old validation issue was fixed in FDP-UAT1, approved for production release, deployed in the 14th January FDP release, and affected Hakodate Production environment records were recovered.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: UV quotation details were linked to the wrong sales order when two sales orders existed for assessment H000014910. The quotation approval process selected cancelled sales order E000262435 instead of approved sales order E000268545. Functionality was updated and validated in UAT1, then released to Production on 16 December.
important_findings: Assessment H000014910 had two sales orders: E000262435 in "Cancelled" status and E000268545 in "Approved" status.
When the quotation was approved, its details were incorrectly linked to cancelled sales order E000262435.
The corrective change ensures quotation details are linked only to a sales order not in "Cancelled" status.
The fix was tested in UAT1 using UV SO# E001282425.
The fix was released to Production in the 16 December release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The quotation approval functionality did not exclude sales orders in "Cancelled" status, causing quotation details to link to E000262435 rather than approved sales order E000268545.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the functionality to link quotation details only to sales orders that are not in "Cancelled" status; validated in UAT1 and released to Production on 16 December.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Changing a quote to customer approved failed because the customer code used in the Job card had a null tax exempt flag. The tax exempt flag is non-nullable in Service order BC, causing the error during the quote status change. Recovery was performed to allow the user to proceed, and a fix to default null tax exempt flag values to 'N' was validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on December 16.
important_findings: The failure occurred when setting the quote status to customer approved.
The customer code used in the Job card had a null tax exempt flag value.
Tax exempt flag is a non-nullable column in Service order BC.
The corrective logic updates the tax exempt flag to 'N' when it is null for a customer.
The fix was validated in UAT-1 for JC# I001286847 and Quote# 1-5O8YM8.
The approved fix was released to Production in the December 16 release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The customer code associated with the Job card had a null tax exempt flag, which violated the non-nullable tax exempt flag column requirement in Service order BC during quote approval.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the tax exempt flag to 'N' when it is null for a customer; the fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on December 16.

Thank you for your continued support of the Japanese version of the comment above.
RCA (root cause analysis)
After investigating this issue, we found that SMDO001 of the Bulk Invoice was mapped to the last updated date in the Service Change Order.
The normal process is that once a service change order's status is set to "Approved," the order becomes "read-only." In this case, the Last Updated Date will be the same as the Posting Date.
However, for this order, the Last Modified Date was changed to November 6, 2024, and unlike the Posting date, the backend process set SMDO001 to 20241106.
Please check the attached screenshots.
modification plan
Create a new field to store the approval date and map that date field to SMDO001 in the Service Change Order Consolidated Invoice.
Please check it out and let us know if you have any questions.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: For Service Change Orders, Bulk Invoice field SMDO001 was mapped to Last Updated Date. A backend process changed the Last Updated Date after approval, causing SMDO001 to differ from the Posting Date. The mapping was changed to Change Order Completion Date, tested in Okayama UAT-1 with sample order K001287931, and deployed to production on April 14.
important_findings: When a Service Change Order is set to Approved, it becomes read-only and its Last Updated Date normally matches the Posting Date.
For the affected order, a backend process changed the Last Updated Date to November 6, 2024, setting SMDO001 to 20241106.
SMDO001 in Bulk Invoice was originally mapped to Last Updated Date for Service Change Orders.
The corrective mapping uses Change Order Completion Date for SMDO001 instead of Last Updated Date.
Posting Date mapping in Journal Voucher was changed in the same manner.
The change was implemented and tested in Okayama UAT-1, then applied to production on April 14.
investigation_report.root_cause: SMDO001 in Bulk Invoice for Service Change Orders was mapped to Last Updated Date, which could be changed by a backend process after approval.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the SMDO001 mapping from Last Updated Date to Change Order Completion Date for Service Change Orders, made the same change for Posting Date in Journal Voucher, and deployed the fix to production.

Dear Shiromoto-san,
Thank you for your continued support.
We have analyzed the issue and identified the following:
1. When the 'Job Card No' field has a value in the order activity, the 'Job Card Type' field becomes read-only:-
2. When the 'Job Card No' field is null in the order activity, the 'Job Card Type' field remains editable:-
Root Cause:-
 During the creation of an 'Order Activity', the 'Job Card Type' field is set to null, while the 'Job Card No' field is assigned a value (e.g., JC#). This results in the 'Job Card Type' field remaining null and read-only, restricting the user from entering a value.
Fix Plan:
 We propose modifying the process so that during the creation of an 'Order Activity,' the system will populate the 'Job Card Type' field in 'Order Activity' using the "JC Type" value from the 'Job Card.'
Please approve this fix plan so that we can proceed with development in the UAT environment.
Kindly let us know in case of any queries.
Thanks and regards,
 Laxminarayan Meena.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: For Order Activities created from quotes where SV staff had already created a Job Card, Job Card Type was blank and read-only. Investigation confirmed that Job Card No was populated while Job Card Type was set to null during Order Activity creation. The fix populated Job Card Type from the Job Card's JC Type; it was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on 16 December.
important_findings: Job Card Type becomes read-only when Job Card No has a value in the Order Activity.
For Direct Input SV Quote cases without a Job Card, Job Card No remains null and Job Card Type is editable, so no fix was required.
For SV staff created Quote cases, the Order Activity received a Job Card No but Job Card Type was set to null, preventing users from entering the required value.
The fix was deployed to UAT1, tested using Order number E001181418, approved for Production, and released on 16 December.
investigation_report.root_cause: During Order Activity creation for activities with an existing Job Card, the system populated Job Card No but set Job Card Type to null. Because Job Card Type is read-only when Job Card No is populated, users could not enter or correct the value.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified Order Activity creation to populate Job Card Type using the JC Type value from the Job Card. The change was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on 16 December.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A mismatch in sorting/order amounts was traced to differing Journal Voucher values when a BB PO line contained quantity greater than 1. Investigation identified calculation errors in Base Amount (CSJS213) and Base Amount (CSJS313) for PO- Body Building Order in Journal Voucher on the KB Side. The code fix was validated in UAT-Okayama and released to Production on 16 December.
important_findings: The issue reproduced in UAT1 (Okayama version) B001284361.
JV values differed when a BB PO line item had quantity greater than 1.
The affected Journal Voucher fields were Base Amount (CSJS213) and Base Amount (CSJS313) for PO- Body Building Order.
The calculation issue was identified on the KB Side.
The fix was completed in UAT-Okayama before Production deployment.
investigation_report.root_cause: Calculation errors in Base Amount (CSJS213) and Base Amount (CSJS313) for PO- Body Building Order in Journal Voucher on the KB Side, affecting BB PO lines with quantity greater than 1.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the code in UAT-Okayama, obtained approval, and released the fix to Production in the 16 December release.

Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this issue and we have found that the user 'D8HITASH' has a position type as 'Branch-Sales-Staff'. We checked the view role matrix for Aomori environment and as per that document, this view is read-only for users with responsibility 'MF Branch-Sales-Staff'. Hence, for this user, you are not able to make any changes on UI.
And for other 'Sales-Staff' users, they have position type as 'Branch NV/UV Sales Staff', for which, as per the view role matrix, this view is editable.
If business requires, we can change the position type for this user to 'Branch NV/UV Sales Staff'. You will need to raise an SR to update the Employee master, with corresponding position for this user in the employee master file.
Since this is working correctly as per the existing functionality and is not a bug, kindly allow us to reject this Jira.
Thanks,
Abhishek Singh.

comments.author: Abhishek Singh.
comments.text:
Thank you for your support.
As discussed, we received an employee master file in SR MFTBCFFR-2703, according to which the user was assigned 'Branch-Sales-Staff' position. This happened because the position string that was mentioned in the file referred to 'Branch-Sales-Staff' and not 'Branch NV/UV Sales Staff'.
Fix plan is as follows:
 * You need to raise an SR to change the JPN string for 'Branch NV/UV Sales Staff'.
 * And another SR to implement the changes in employee master, so that the user 'D8HITASH' is assigned the correct position(Branch NV/UV Sales Staff).
Since the current functionality is working correctly and the user was assigned the position as provided in the latest employee master to us, kindly allow us to reject this incident.
Kindly let us know if you have any further queries.
Thanks,
Abhishek Singh.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: User D8HITASH could not edit the UI because the assigned position type, Branch-Sales-Staff, grants read-only access in the Aomori view role matrix for responsibility MF Branch-Sales-Staff. The position was assigned from the employee master file received under SR MFTBCFFR-2703, where the provided position string mapped to Branch-Sales-Staff rather than Branch NV/UV Sales Staff. The behavior was determined to be correct per the configured role matrix, not a product defect.
important_findings: User D8HITASH was assigned the Branch-Sales-Staff position type.
In the Aomori view role matrix, the view is read-only for the MF Branch-Sales-Staff responsibility.
Users with the Branch NV/UV Sales Staff position type have editable access to the view.
The employee master file received in SR MFTBCFFR-2703 contained a position string that referred to Branch-Sales-Staff.
The proposed correction requires updating the JPN string for Branch NV/UV Sales Staff and updating the employee master assignment for D8HITASH.
investigation_report.root_cause: The employee master file assigned D8HITASH the Branch-Sales-Staff position because its position string referred to Branch-Sales-Staff instead of Branch NV/UV Sales Staff; this position has read-only access under the Aomori view role matrix.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: TOB files were not processed because of an issue in the ODI package, preventing downstream processing such as chassis-order creation when expected D21 files were not received. An ODI patch was applied to FDP Production environments on 2025-01-19, after which the issue no longer recurred. Automated monitoring was also implemented to notify the AMS team of unprocessed or failed TOB files.
important_findings: No D21 file was received in Siebel for the provided Fuso Reception numbers; therefore, no chassis order was created.
The issue was identified as an ODI package failure affecting TOB file processing.
Patch validation succeeded in FDP UAT when the D21A file was executed on UAT5, and ODI batch executions completed successfully after the Production patch upgrade.
Automated monitoring sends the AMS team daily email notifications when a TOB file is unprocessed or fails ODI processing.
MFTBCFFR-3152 and MFTBCFFR-3350 were confirmed to be unrelated: MFTBCFFR-3152 involved data loading to FDP Chugoku, and MFTBCFFR-3350 involved D21A file unavailability.
investigation_report.root_cause: A problem in the ODI package caused TOB files to remain unprocessed.
investigation_report.resolution: An ODI patch was applied to FDP Production environments on 2025-01-19, and automated email monitoring for unprocessed or failed TOB files was implemented. Subsequent monitoring confirmed no further discrepancies caused by the ODI failure.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved sales-order cancellation behavior for revised UV Quotes. Analysis of Assessment# H000037359 confirmed that the existing sales order is cancelled when the revised UV Quote status becomes Approved or Initial Approval Completed. The fix plan was validated in UAT1 after an initial UAT failure and released to Production in the 21st Nov FDP Release.
important_findings: For Assessment# H000037359, approving the revised UV Quote after selecting Generate Approval set Rev. 2 Quote status to "Initial Approval Completed".
When a revised UV Quote reaches Approved or Initial Approval Completed status, the existing sales order is cancelled.
Existing sales order E001281788 was cancelled after Rev. 2 Quote reached "Initial Approval Completed".
After cancellation of the existing sales order, the "Create Order" button became active on the Rev. 2 Quote.
The fix plan was applied in UAT1 and released to Production in the 21st Nov FDP Release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The existing sales order was not being cancelled as required when the revised UV Quote reached Approved or Initial Approval Completed status.
investigation_report.resolution: Applied the fix plan in UAT1 and released it to Production in the 21st Nov FDP Release.

important_findings: The affected Labors were linked to an External Work Order and therefore generated a Service PO under Outsourcing(External).
Line Item Type -External is mapped to Credit Account Code 271-20.
FDP has special vendors that are not considered external, but users create External Work Orders for them.
Siebel sends the correct account code; the required FDP-specific handling was not introduced during initial JV development.
Implementing the requested FDP functionality was considered difficult development at the time.
investigation_report.root_cause: FDP lacks functionality to apply Internal work order account codes for special FDP vendors when users create an External Work Order, causing the External Work Order account-code mapping to be used.
investigation_report.resolution: Users create an Internal work order when the desired Internal work order account code is required; the incident was closed without a development change.

comments.author: Laxminarayan Meena.
comments.text:
Dear Miyauchi San,
Thank you for your support.
Here is the explanation of your queries:-
Question:1 Why is consumption tax is present in Body Building Order even with zero order amount?
Answer: We have checked the 'Consumption Tax' field on Body Building Orders. It is a column based field which stores the total tax of line items when amount is entered in line items. Since, it is column based field, tax is not updated when line item is cancelled.
 
Question:2 Can Acceptance verification be done for Body building order when the line item is cancelled?
Answer: Yes, 'Acceptance Verification Done' status is possible for Body Building Orders with cancelled line items.
Please let us know in case of any other queries.
Thanks and regards,
Laxminarayan Meena.

Dear Miyauchi San,
Thank you for your support.

Please allow us to close the Jira.
Thanks
Amit

investigation_report.investigation_summary: For Body Building Order B000160867, Journal Voucher Lines for PO and Consumption Tax were not created because the order amount was 0 after the line item was cancelled. The Consumption Tax field retained tax calculated before cancellation because it is a column-based field and is not updated when a line item is cancelled. This behavior was confirmed as expected, and the incident was closed without a corrective change.
important_findings: Body Building Order B000160867 had an order amount of 0 because its line item was cancelled.
Journal Voucher Lines for PO and its Consumption Tax were not created when the order amount was 0.
The Consumption Tax field stores the total tax from line-item amounts when amounts are entered.
Consumption Tax is not updated when a line item is cancelled because it is a column-based field.
Body Building Orders with cancelled line items can still have the status 'Acceptance Verification Done'.
investigation_report.root_cause: The line item for Body Building Order B000160867 was cancelled, causing the order amount to become 0; therefore, Journal Voucher Lines for PO and Consumption Tax were not created.
investigation_report.resolution: No system correction was required; the behavior was explained as expected and the Jira was closed.

Post-release monitoring found no newly created Job Cards with a null rounding value in all three environments.
investigation_report.root_cause: A rounding issue resulted in null rounding values for Job Cards with the "Field Fix Flag" set to "Y", causing the "There is an open field fix" error during Job Card creation.

Investigation found that Service Quote BIP and AR used different backend Siebel field mappings, and the synchronization behavior available in FDP was not present in the SC version. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to PROD in the 21st Nov FDP Release.
important_findings: Updating an address through the Customer Update/Update Customer function did not update the AR address in the SC version.
For Quote BIP address updates, users were initially instructed to use the Update AR button.
Service Quote BIP and AR address fields had different backend Siebel mappings.
The FDP implementation updates the AR address when the Customer Address is updated; this functionality originated from FDP-AAC-01 Merge AR/ AP into one Finance Account.
In UAT-1, changes to the address in Basic Info were reflected in AR/AP and synchronized to BIP.
The fix was deployed to PROD in the 21st Nov FDP Release.
investigation_report.root_cause: Service Quote BIP and AR had different backend Siebel field mappings, and the FDP address-synchronization functionality was not present in the SC version.
investigation_report.resolution: The address synchronization issue was fixed in UAT-1, validated by testing, and deployed to PROD in the 21st Nov FDP Release.
technical_entities: FDP-AAC-01 Merge AR/ AP into one Finance Account

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Approval generation for an Assessment Request did not trigger the expected rule because the requesting user’s primary position was set incorrectly. important_findings: Approval processing evaluates the requesting user’s primary position.
User D8KOUSTA had both Branch-CS-Staff and Branch NV/UV Sales Staff Position.
Branch-CS-Staff was configured as D8KOUSTA’s primary position, preventing the expected approval rule from triggering.
Changing the primary position to Branch NV/UV Sales Staff allows the approval rule to trigger correctly.
The Assessment Request status was changed back to "In Progress" to enable recovery and approval regeneration.
The incident was identified as user mis-operation rather than a system issue.
investigation_report.root_cause: User D8KOUSTA had Branch-CS-Staff configured as the primary position instead of Branch NV/UV Sales Staff, while approval rules use the requester’s primary position.
investigation_report.resolution: Reverted the Assessment Request to "In Progress" and instructed the user to set Branch NV/UV Sales Staff as the primary position before selecting "Generate Approval".

いつもお世話になっております。
この問題について詳細に分析した結果、以下のことが分かりました：
青森本番におけるこの問題は、ContactテーブルのPR_HELD_POSTN_IDに不正な値が存在したために発生しました。このカラムには「SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff」のIDが含まれており、シャーシの発注データに必要です。

investigation_report.root_cause: A garbage LOV blocked TCB01 status updates, and an incorrect ID in Aomori caused incomplete D21E processing.

Thank you for your support.
We have found rca of this issue and are describing below step by step:-
For NV Case:
1.The user created an NV Quote with a Trade-In and used the auto-order button to generate an NV Sales Order, which initially had a status of 'Pending'.
2.The user then clicked the 'Generate Approval' button for the NV Sales Order but rejected the approval, resulting in the NV Sales Order status being updated to 'Rejected'.
3.The user revised the NV Quote (Revision 1) to NV Quote (Revision 2) and approved NV Quote (Revision 2).
4.NV Quote (Revision 2) synchronized with the NV Sales Order, triggering the creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In.
5.Since the Auto Order button is enabled in NV Quote (Revision 2), the user can generate a new NV Sales Order by clicking it.
Even though the NV Sales Order is in a 'Rejected' status, a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In will created.
For UV Case:
1.The user created a UV Quote with a Trade-In and used the auto-order button to generate a UV Sales Order with a 'Pending' status.
2.Revise UV Quote(Revision 1) to UV Quote(Revision 2) and approved UV Quote(Revision 2)
3.UV Quote (Revision 2) synchronized with the UV Sales Order, triggering the creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In.
Even though the UV Sales Order is in 'Pending' status, a UV Purchase Order for Trade In will create.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Trade-In synchronization created UV Purchase Orders when revised and approved quotes synchronized to sales orders that were not in an appropriate status. In the NV flow, this occurred after an NV Sales Order approval was rejected; in the UV flow, it occurred while the UV Sales Order remained Pending. The issue was fixed in UAT1, validated with test sales orders, and released to Production in the 13 September FDP release.
important_findings: Revision 2 of NV Quote# 1-UJYUK synchronized after approval and generated PO# F000110671 although the associated order# A000109884 had been rejected.
The Trade-In synchronization process did not account for an NV Sales Order in Rejected status.
For NV Quotes, revising and approving a quote after rejecting the generated NV Sales Order triggered creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In.
For UV Quotes, revising and approving a quote triggered creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In while the UV Sales Order remained Pending.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Employee 6882 had two inactive employee master records for Okayama-Production. A department master update during the 22 July 2024 FDPO Release caused both records to be sent to KB. The existing MFTBCFFR-1978 solution covered only one active and one inactive record, so a new rule was implemented in the 26 August 2024 FDP Release to send the latest inactive record to KB.
important_findings: Employee 6882 had two inactive records in the employee master for Okayama-Production.
The department master update during the 22 July 2024 FDPO Release triggered transmission of the inactive records to KB.
MFTBCFFR-1978 handled multiple records only when one record was active and one was inactive.
The new behavior for multiple inactive records is to send the latest inactive record to KB.
The solution was released to Prod in the 26 August 2024 FDP Release.
investigation_report.root_cause: The existing multiple-record handling logic from MFTBCFFR-1978 did not support cases where an employee had two inactive employee master records.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented and released a Prod change in the 26 August 2024 FDP Release to send the latest inactive record to KB when multiple inactive records exist.

We have analyzed this issue and we have found that in this record, there was an assessment created with the same vehicle, in cancelled status. When an assessment is cancelled, a flag is set to 'Y' for all the POs mapped to that vehicle, so that when another assessment is created with same VIN# and their purchase orders are created, only the newest POs get mapped in the sales order.
