investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Delivery Request creation error occurred when purchase orders associated with a vehicle were not all mapped. Investigation found that a previously cancelled assessment for the same vehicle set a flag to 'Y' on all mapped POs; this flag was handled during sales order mapping but was not checked during Delivery Request creation. The Delivery Request logic was corrected, validated in UAT1 on AR# H000030031, and released to Prod.
important_findings: A cancelled assessment sets a flag to 'Y' for all POs mapped to the associated vehicle.
For a subsequent assessment with the same VIN#, only the newest purchase orders are mapped in the sales order.
Delivery Request creation did not check the cancellation-related PO flag, causing the error that all purchase orders were not mapped.
The condition was fixed for Delivery Request creation and deployed to UAT1.
UAT passed on AR# H000030031, and the fix was released to Prod.
investigation_report.root_cause: Delivery Request creation did not check the 'Y' flag set on POs mapped to a vehicle when a prior assessment was cancelled, resulting in validation that all purchase orders were not mapped.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated Delivery Request creation logic to check the cancellation-related PO flag; the change passed UAT1 validation and was released to Prod.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: C/# data was not visible in the NV_Report after a column was added to W_ASSET_D for incident MFTBCFFR-2350. important_findings: A column added to W_ASSET_D for MFTBCFFR-2350 required a full load of W_ASSET_D.
The dependent table of W_ASSET_D was not fully loaded, causing it to be out of sync.
The same issue occurred in FDP UAT and was resolved by fully loading the dependent table of W_ASSET_D.
The production full load was deferred until after business hours because it could impact the Siebel database.
After the dependent-table full load, C/# data displayed correctly in the NV report.
investigation_report.root_cause: The dependent table of W_ASSET_D was not fully loaded after W_ASSET_D was changed and fully loaded, leaving the dependent table out of sync.
investigation_report.resolution: Performed a full load of the dependent table of W_ASSET_D after business hours; C/# data was then correctly displayed in the NV report.

investigation_report.root_cause: The Service Request was created by UserID D8FORF19 with Position Type HQ-Gn-Affairs-GMgr, which does not trigger the Approval Flow. The existing functionality requires a creator with Position Type Branch-Parts-Staff for the Service Request status to change to Completed.
investigation_report.resolution: Removed the no-longer-required additional field, validated Service Request completion in UAT-1 using a Branch-Parts-Staff user, and released the incident to Prod.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The D21L received from TOB was not executed on 11 June because an ODI package failed. The DMS_Inbound directory contained too many files, causing an "Argument List too long" error. Recovery of the chassis order was completed after unnecessary files were moved to the Archive folder.
important_findings: The D21L received from TOB was not executed on 11 June.
ODI reported an "Argument List too long" error and the package failed.
The failure occurred because the number of files in DMS_Inbound was too large.
Unnecessary files were moved from DMS_Inbound to the Archive folder.
Recovery for the affected chassis order was completed.
DMS_Inbound will be regularly cleaned by moving unnecessary files to the Archive folder.
investigation_report.root_cause: Excessive file volume in DMS_Inbound caused an ODI package to fail with "Argument List too long", preventing execution of the D21L received from TOB.
investigation_report.resolution: Moved unnecessary files from DMS_Inbound to the Archive folder and completed recovery of the affected chassis order; regular archival will be performed to prevent recurrence.

comments.author: Bhisham
comments.text:
We have replicated the issue.
Approval rule Present are following the rule correctly and sending the approver to 'service manager'.
This Approval rule works according to "Sales Rep Position Type".It takes the "Sales Rep Position Type" position of the user who has created the JC,and send the approval according to it.The flow work given below as
Created                                    Approver
MF Branch-Service-Mgr          MF Branch-Head
MF Branch-Service-Staff         MF Branch-Service-Mgr
For refrence in RT2
JC#                    Created                                  Approver
I000035277     MF Branch-Service-Mgr          MF Branch-Head
I000035278     MF Branch-Service-Staff          MF Branch-Service-Mgr
The records which is present in Prod
JC#->I000050053
This Record which is created by User ID-:D8SAKIYE(MF Branch-Service-Mgr) and requestor is D8SAYAGI(MF Branch-Service-Staff) so the approver goes to D8HIRHIR(MF Branch-Head).
Regards,
Bhisham

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The approval-routing behavior was replicated and verified as operating according to the configured approval rule. The rule determines the approver from the Sales Rep Position Type of the user who created the JC, rather than the requestor. For JC I000050053 in Prod, the creator's MF Branch-Service-Mgr position routed approval to an MF Branch-Head.
important_findings: The approval rule routes approvals based on the JC creator's Sales Rep Position Type.
MF Branch-Service-Mgr creators route to MF Branch-Head approvers.
MF Branch-Service-Staff creators route to MF Branch-Service-Mgr approvers.
In RT2, JC I000035277 created by MF Branch-Service-Mgr routed to MF Branch-Head, while JC I000035278 created by MF Branch-Service-Staff routed to MF Branch-Service-Mgr.
In Prod, JC I000050053 was created by D8SAKIYE (MF Branch-Service-Mgr); therefore, approval routed to D8HIRHIR (MF Branch-Head), despite the requestor D8SAYAGI being MF Branch-Service-Staff.
investigation_report.root_cause: Approval routing is determined by the JC creator's Sales Rep Position Type, not by the requestor's position type.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The reported behavior was that users could select option codes in a quote even when the options were not configured as valid. Engineering stated that this behavior exists in both FDP and SC versions of Force and that no change had been made for this issue. The business disputed that this was expected quote behavior, but no corrective change or agreed resolution was recorded.
important_findings: TCH02 entries that are not configured normally display an amount of 0.
The TCH02 price file processed in production under SR MFTBCFFR-2176 populated prices according to the supplied file.
WDWH042 created an option price for option code "GY" with Product code "220", MC "1", M_Body null, and model codes beginning with "F", including model code "FV80GJXD2B" in Option Price Master.
Engineering reported that users can select any option code from quotes in both FDP and SC versions of Force, regardless of whether the option is configured as valid.
Engineering stated that restricting quote selection to configured options would require a Change Request (CR) / AMS CR.
The business rejected the assertion that unrestricted option selection in quotes was existing functionality, and the comments do not record an agreed outcome.

The cause of the error was that last night (around 20:20) Okafusa was carrying out the "period-end balance carryover" process.
Since the processing screen was in the starting state, an error occurred when starting the daily processing.
(This morning (around 6:40), it seems that the person in charge of Okafugo closed the screen, and as a result, this error has been resolved.)
 
Also, due to the above error, the IF file and controller file linked from Siebel
Because file management (file backup processing, etc.) has become irregular,

The data import process was performed again and completed successfully.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Daily processing failed because the "period-end balance carryover" processing screen was left active in Okafusa. The failure caused irregular file management for IF files and control files received from Siebel, preventing proper control-file validation. After the screen was closed, the data import was rerun and completed successfully.
important_findings: Okafusa was running the "period-end balance carryover" process at approximately 20:20, and its processing screen remained active.
Starting daily processing while the "period-end balance carryover" screen was active caused the initial error.
The failure caused irregular file management, including file backup processing, for IF files and control files linked from Siebel.
Irregular control-file handling prevented proper control-file validation.
The issue was cleared after the processing screen was closed, and the data import process completed successfully when rerun.
investigation_report.root_cause: The "period-end balance carryover" processing screen in Okafusa remained active when daily processing was started.
investigation_report.resolution: The active "period-end balance carryover" screen was closed, and the data import process was rerun successfully.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: SV FDP data was not updated on 27 April 2024 because the 5-02 Stock inventory details and SV dataset refreshes failed, leaving 26 April data missing until the 28 April report refresh. ODI load completed without issues, and Microsoft investigation identified a Microsoft-side Power BI Gateway/service issue. The April 2024 gateway version was suspected to contain a bug; Microsoft recommended upgrading to the May 2024 version, but the comments do not confirm final remediation completion.
important_findings: The 5-02 Stock inventory details and SV dataset did not refresh on 27 April 2024, causing 26 April data to be missing from SV FDP reports.
The missing 26 April data was reflected after the 28 April report refresh.
ODI load completed on time with no reported issues.
PBI reports do not retain backup data; report data is inserted and updated on each refresh.
Microsoft reported that PBI Gateway version 3000.178.9 / April 2024 was not syncing properly with the PBI service, producing Gateway unreachable/Offline refresh failures.
Upgrading to the April 2024 gateway version did not resolve the error; Microsoft suspected a bug and recommended the May 2024 On-premises gateway version.
investigation_report.root_cause: Microsoft-side Power BI Gateway/service issue, with the April 2024 gateway version suspected to contain a bug causing synchronization and Gateway unreachable/Offline refresh failures.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The "Last DB Refresh Time" in the Okayama Power BI UAT report remained at the previous successful load time despite daytime report refreshes. Investigation found that the 12:00 PM ODI Load plan failed because duplicate database data was not permitted at an ODI processing step. The Load plan issue was fixed and monitored successfully for three days, after which daytime Power BI refreshes displayed the correct "Last DB Refresh Time".
important_findings: The Power BI report refresh itself could complete while "Last DB Refresh Time" continued to show the last successful ODI daily Load plan run.
The 12:00 PM ODI Load plan failure was caused by duplicate data in the database that was not permitted at an ODI step.
The 21:30 Load plan run completed successfully after the duplicate-data issue was resolved.
The Load plan for UAT Okayama was fixed and ran successfully for three days during monitoring.
Scheduled Power BI refresh failures requiring manual refresh were identified as a separate issue tracked in MFTBCFFR-2274.
investigation_report.root_cause: Duplicate data in the database caused the 12:00 PM ODI Load plan to fail at a step where duplicates were not permitted, preventing "Last DB Refresh Time" from being updated.
investigation_report.resolution: The UAT Okayama Load plan issue was fixed, the successful load runs updated "Last DB Refresh Time" correctly in daytime Power BI report refreshes, and the fix was monitored successfully for three days.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A Service Request selected an incorrect Responsible shop code from employee details. The employee master initially contained an incorrect Location code from the first employee-code file, resulting in shop code 7203 for the Default organization instead of 00. A corrected business file updated the employee data, and a newly created SR reflected the correct values and would populate the correct Responsible shop code in account master.
important_findings: The incorrect Responsible shop code was sourced from employee details during Service Request creation.
The employee record had shop code 7203 for the Default organization; the expected shop code was 00.
The initial employee-code file contained an incorrect Location code.
A second file received from the business corrected the employee master data.
A newly created SR reflected the correct values and, upon completion, would update account master with the correct Responsible shop code.
Employee master reruns will be monitored, with validation of the Location code.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect Location code in the initial employee-code file caused an erroneous employee master update, resulting in Responsible shop code 7203 being selected instead of 00.
investigation_report.resolution: The business provided a corrected employee-code file that corrected the employee master data. A new Service Request was created with correct values and would populate the correct Responsible shop code in account master upon completion; future employee master reruns will be monitored for Location code accuracy.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: No employee was assigned to the Branch-CS-Head position in Division 10, causing no user to appear for that role in approval flow history. Analysis of the April 1, 2024 employee master execution on Prod found that Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, so D8TMASAA received the Branch-Service-Mgr role instead. The position mapping was corrected and the employee master file was re-executed, assigning D8TMASAA to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
important_findings: D8ISHDA1 was assigned to the Branch-Head position, not the Branch-CS-Head position, in Okayama Higashi Branch with 10 Dealer Code.
The April 1, 2024 employee master file execution removed D8TOTAKE from the Branch-CS-Head position and intended to assign D8TMASAA.
The employee master file operation for D8TMASAA was specified as "Assign" although the investigation stated it should have been "Change".
Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, resulting in D8TMASAA being assigned Branch-Service-Mgr rather than Branch-CS-Head.
Because no employee held Branch-CS-Head in Division 10, no user appeared for that role in approval flow history.
investigation_report.root_cause: Position Type Mapping incorrectly mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr during employee master processing, leaving no employee assigned to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the position mapping on Prod and re-executed the employee master file for D8TMASAA, which correctly assigned the user to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders was not correctly sourced after SC SIEBEL changes to "Change Order Completion Date/Time". Investigation found that the SC Siebel changes under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel, requiring an AMS CR on the FDP Okayama Siebel side and a corresponding FDP PBI mapping update. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to FDP PROD on July 20, 2024.
important_findings: SC SIEBEL changes for "Change Order Completion Date/Time" under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel.
FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders needed to source the "Change Order Completion date" column from Siebel.
An AMS CR was required for FDP Okayama Siebel in addition to the PBI change.
The PROD release added a new column to the ODI mapping and required a full load of Daily Load Plan.
The fix was verified in FDP UAT for reports SV_101, 1_10A, 1_12A, and 1_15A, and the issue could not be reproduced in UAT after the change.
investigation_report.root_cause: The "Change Order Completion Date/Time" changes made in SC SIEBEL were not reflected in FDP Siebel, so FDP PBI could not source the correct Settlement Date for change orders.
investigation_report.resolution: Applied the required FDP Okayama Siebel AMS CR and updated the FDP PBI ODI mapping to source change-order Settlement Date from the Siebel "Change Order Completion date" column; performed a full Daily Load Plan load and deployed the fix to FDP PROD.

The Line Number field was changed to read-only in UAT1 and then deployed to PROD.
investigation_report.root_cause: The editable Line Number field in the Chassis Tab of the Quote was changed during Quote revision and Model Code change, preventing the Quote from syncing to the Sales Order.
investigation_report.resolution: Set the Line Number field to read-only in UAT1, obtained approval, and released the change to PROD on 19th April.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident affected creation of return orders for Parts Internal Orders and required temporary status reversions of related NV Sales Orders to enable returns. UAT1 validation identified that the Create Return Order button could be pressed when return quantity and return reason were blank, but no return order was created. Changes were validated in UAT1, approved for PROD, and released to PROD on 19 April.
important_findings: NV Sales Orders were temporarily reverted from "Sales Posting Completed" to "Registration Completed" so users could create return orders for associated Parts Internal Orders.
After return processing, the affected NV Sales Orders were restored to "Sales Posting Completed".
The Create Return Order button was enabled when return quantity and return reason were blank, although no return order was created in that condition.
A return order is created only when returned quantity is greater than 0; return reason is required to save the returned quantity.
The issue was fixed in UAT1, validated by the user, approved for PROD, and released on 19 April.
investigation_report.root_cause: A defect in Create Return Order button validation allowed the button to be pressed when return quantity and return reason were blank, while no return order could be created.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the return-order behavior in UAT1, obtained validation and PROD approval, and released the fix to PROD on 19 April. Related NV Sales Orders were temporarily reverted to "Registration Completed" for return processing and restored to "Sales Posting Completed" afterward.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Incorrect values were recovered and initially required verification in the PBI Report. Analysis confirmed that the issue was related to the recovery for Incident Jira 2182. The recovery used an incorrect ROW_ID, causing the latest Model Master Price for Model Code SO# A000090515 to be fetched incorrectly; values were subsequently confirmed as correct in the PBI Report.
important_findings: Model Master Price execution was performed in production on 8th March.
The Model Master Price for Model Code SO# A000090515 was updated with the latest price.
During recovery for Jira 2182, the wrong ROW_ID was used for the record that fetched the latest Model Master Price for the model code.
After recovery, values were confirmed as correct in the PBI Report.
The team planned preventive steps to avoid recurrence.
investigation_report.root_cause: Recovery for Jira 2182 was executed using the wrong ROW_ID for the record that fetched the latest price from Model Master Price for Model Code SO# A000090515.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery was completed and the values were verified as correct in the PBI Report; no further PBI update was required.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PBI 1_10A Report populated Settlement Date from the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date, causing dates to appear for Change Orders that were still in progress. Analysis confirmed that the PBI logic differs from Siebel, where the relevant field is Change Order Completion date and only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date. A change to PBI SV_1_10A was identified as necessary, and an AMS-CR was requested.
important_findings: The settlement date in PBI was populated using the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date.
For JC# I000097002 / Change Order# K000121869, LAST_UPD changed from March 18 to March 19 after an update, and PBI reflected March 19.
Using LAST_UPD causes in-progress Change Orders, including recently created and unapproved Change Orders, to receive a settlement date in PBI.
Siebel uses Change Order Completion date for the settlement date requirement.
Only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date and be displayed in PBI reports.
PBI SV_1_10A requires logic changes to align with Siebel.
investigation_report.root_cause: PBI 1_10A mapped Settlement Date to the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date instead of the Siebel Change Order Completion date, resulting in settlement dates for in-progress, unapproved Change Orders.
investigation_report.resolution: An AMS-CR was requested to implement Settlement Date logic changes in PBI SV_1_10A to align with Siebel and populate settlement dates only for approved Change Orders.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident concerned changing Adjustment Amount values in Siebel. Directly changing and saving the Adjustment Amount on an existing record was identified as an incorrect operation. Users must end-date the old record and create a new record with the revised amount and corresponding effective dates.
important_findings: Directly changing and saving Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record is an incorrect operation.
The old record must have its Effective To date populated before the Adjustment Amount is changed.
A new record must be created for the revised Adjustment Amount.
The new record must have the appropriate Effective From date populated.
The required handling was classified as an operation rule rather than a system issue.
investigation_report.root_cause: Users attempted to directly change and save Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record instead of end-dating the old record and creating a new effective-dated record.
investigation_report.resolution: Users were instructed to populate Effective To on the old record, then create a new record with the updated Adjustment Amount and an appropriate Effective From date.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Journal Voucher creation failed in Sales Posting and for Individual Purchase Order B000060944 because the IBOS shipment workflow did not meet the existing trigger conditions. The change was developed and tested in UAT, approved after UAT validation, and released to Prod on 8 March 2024.
important_findings: Sales Posting did not trigger a Journal Voucher when Body Building Order-IBOS was not Shipped, even though the related Sales Order status was Acceptance Verification done.
Individual Purchase Order B000060944 did not create a Journal Voucher because the Inbound Process of IBOS-Shipment could not trigger the JV.
The revised Sales Posting logic triggers a Journal Voucher when Body Building Order-IBOS is either Shipped or Acceptance Verification done.
The GR case was handled so that the Journal Voucher is triggered when the status is Shipped.
The change was tested in UAT, UAT passed, and the release was deployed to Prod on 8 March 2024.
investigation_report.root_cause: Journal Voucher trigger logic required Body Building Order-IBOS to be Shipped and did not handle the Acceptance Verification done status or the IBOS-Shipment inbound process scenario.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated Journal Voucher trigger logic so Sales Posting triggers for Body Building Order-IBOS statuses Shipped or Acceptance Verification done, and handled the GR case to trigger the Journal Voucher when status is Shipped; released to Prod on 8 March 2024.

Dear Shiromoto san,
We have analyzed this issue and we've found that Assessment purpose is editable even when the status of the assessment is 'Assessment Completed'. Since it is editable, user can change the assessment purpose, and in that process, if we set the assessment purpose to null, although it will not be saved, but its purchase type will be set to null. And then as soon as we press Esc, the assessment purpose will be set back to its previous value, but now, its purchase type has been set to null. Thus, causing this issue.
User steps would be:
 # Create an assessment and approve it
 # Since assessment purpose is editable, trying to change it.
 # Changing the assessment purpose mid process back to its previous value(Pressing Esc)
 # Now, on UI, Assessment purpose is set back to its original value. But in that process, the purchase type for that assessment is set to null.
Let us know if you have any queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Purchase type values were incorrect or null in PBI reports because of both report LOV inconsistencies and a Siebel assessment update defect. In Siebel, Assessment purpose remained editable after an assessment reached "Assessment Completed"; cancelling a purpose change with Esc could leave the associated purchase type as null. The fix was validated in UAT1, released to Prod, and affected Prod records were recovered; the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was subsequently rectified.
important_findings: UV_2B had different LOVs between PBI and SIEBEL, causing purchase-type discrepancies for records H000000801, H000002802, and H000003406.
UV_2_01_2_02 did not display a value in the SIEBEL UI, so the value was not reflected in the PBI report.
Assessment purpose was editable when assessment status was "Assessment Completed".
If a user began changing Assessment purpose and pressed Esc to restore the prior value, the UI restored the purpose but set the assessment purchase type to null.
UAT initially showed "UV Trade-in" for purchase classifications in 2-01, 2-02, 2-05, 2-06, and 2-01(History), rather than "Magotori".
After the Prod release, the Purchase Type filter in 2-01 and 2-02 incorrectly included "SV reception category" LOV values; this was rectified.
investigation_report.root_cause: In Siebel, Assessment purpose could be edited after an assessment was "Assessment Completed". Cancelling an in-progress Assessment purpose change with Esc restored the displayed purpose but left the associated purchase type set to null. Separate PBI and SIEBEL LOV differences also caused UV_2B purchase-type discrepancies.
investigation_report.resolution: The issue was fixed and validated in UAT1, then released to Prod. Affected Prod records were recovered, PBI reports were refreshed, and the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was rectified.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A deleted line item in UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) caused a line-number mismatch between the quote and the UV Sales Order created through the auto order button. During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), the mismatch deleted order line items and child records, causing the sync to fail when updating Line Item# 5. The corrective change disabled deletion from the Line Items tab while retaining deletion of Liability Insurance through the Taxes and Expenses tab; the change was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD.
important_findings: Deleting Line Item# 4, Expense (S07), from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) removed Line Item# 4 from the Backend Column.
The UV Sales Order created through the auto order button still contained Line Item# 4 for Recycle Fee(YN5Z).
During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), Line Item# 4 and its child records were deleted from the order, which also deleted Line Item# 5.
The sync failed when UV Sales Quote Line Item# 5 attempted to update the already deleted UV Sales Order Line Item# 5.
The FDP fix disables the Delete button on the Line Items tab; Liability Insurance can only be deleted from the Taxes and Expenses tab.
The change passed UAT1 validation and was implemented on PROD.
investigation_report.root_cause: Deletion of Line Item# 4 from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) created a Backend Column line-number mismatch with the UV Sales Order, which retained Line Item# 4 after auto-order creation. Synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3) then deleted order lines and child records, including Line Item# 5, causing the subsequent Line Item# 5 update to fail.
investigation_report.resolution: Disabled the Delete button on the Line Items tab and restricted deletion of Liability Insurance to the Taxes and Expenses tab. The change was implemented in UAT1, passed UAT, and was deployed to PROD.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Rejected and incomplete used-car sales orders appeared in reports because users manually populated date fields used by report filters. UV SO# E000087121 appeared in the Order Report despite Rejected status because Approval Date was manually entered; UV SO# E000037797 appeared in the sales report because Delivery Completion Approved Date was manually entered. The incident was classified as user misoperation and closed with no system fix required.
important_findings: Approval Date is normally auto-populated when an approver approves a Sales Order, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000087121 before approval was requested.
The Order Report filters approved orders based on Approval Date, so UV SO# E000087121 appeared even after rejection by the Branch Head.
Delivery Completion Approved Date is normally populated when the Delivery Request is completed, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000037797.
The Sales Order Reporting screen filters sales-posting-completed orders based on Delivery Completion Approved Date, causing UV SO# E000037797 to appear in the sales report.
Making the two date fields Read Only was confirmed as possible and not expected to affect functionality, but no change was implemented because the issue was handled through user operation.
investigation_report.root_cause: User misoperation: manual entry of Approval Date and Delivery Completion Approved Date caused orders to satisfy date-based report filters regardless of their actual approval or delivery-completion status.
investigation_report.resolution: No system fix was implemented. The incident was handled through user operation and the Jira was rejected/closed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Profit values differed between PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 because repair fee cost was sourced from UV Inventory under the recorded transaction sequence. A UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory before sales posting status, while the corresponding UV Sales Quote had a repair fee cost of zero. No corrective system change was documented; the ticket was requested to be closed after the cause was identified.
important_findings: The issue was not caused by Siebel or the Sales order reporting screen calculation.
PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 fetch repair fee cost from UV Inventory.
A UV Sales Quote was created before a UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory.
Because the UV Body Building PO was created before sales posting status, the repair fee cost was sourced from UV Inventory.
The repair fee cost value in the Sales quote was zero, causing the reported values to differ.
investigation_report.root_cause: The UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory before sales posting status, causing PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 to use the repair fee cost from UV Inventory while the Sales quote value was zero.

comments.author: Divyesh Ghiya
comments.text:
We investigated this issue thorughly and below are our findings:
In Sales Order, tax percent comes from the sales quote but there is a logic written behind Generate Approval button. In this logic, Whenever user clicks generate approval, tax rate is being searched in Consumption Tax Master in following manner:
First, query by acknowledgment date in consumption master, 
if acknowledgment date is >= Today then:
Condition 1: Last Contract Date <= Acknowledgment Date
Condition 2: Last Contract Date >= Acknowledgment Date
else,
Condition 3: acknowledgment date < Today
For condition 1 and 3, we then query start date <= Last Contract Date <= End Date
For condition 2, we query start date <= Planned Delivery Date <= End Date
In FDP-Okayama, Acknowledgment date is 2020/11/30(which is less then today), so condition 3 will be followed and query will be done on the basis of Last Contract Date in Sales Order. In all the orders we shared with you, you can find that last contract date was less then start date(2023/07/29), hence there were 0 results of the query and tax percent was set to null.
*This logic is same as in SC.*
We replicated the same test case in SC UAT1 where se set Last Contract Date(2018/01/31) less then Start Date (2020/11/30) in Order A025013709. In this case also, tax percent was set to null and order sheet bip was failed.
one solution to avoid this in FDP is to set Start Date same as SC so that query will not give null result and tax percent is set properly.
Kindly, confirm this RCA and let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report.investigation_summary: BIP generation failed because the Tax Rate column in NV Sales Order was set to null. The Generate Approval logic queried Consumption Tax Master using the Sales Order Last Contract Date for FDP-Okayama orders with an acknowledgment date earlier than the current date; no matching tax-master record was found. The Consumption Tax Master start date was changed in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version, allowing tax percent to be set correctly.
important_findings: Tax percent in Sales Order originates from the sales quote but is recalculated by logic behind the Generate Approval button.
For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the logic queries Consumption Tax Master using Start Date <= Last Contract Date <= End Date.
In FDP-Okayama, the acknowledgment date was 2020/11/30 and affected orders had a Last Contract Date earlier than the Consumption Tax Master start date of 2023/07/29.
The Consumption Tax Master query returned zero records, causing tax percent and the NV Sales Order Tax Rate column to be set to null.
The same behavior was reproduced in SC UAT1 using Order A025013709 with Last Contract Date 2018/01/31 earlier than Start Date 2020/11/30, resulting in Order Sheet BIP failure.
The logic was confirmed to be the same as in SC.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama was later than the affected Sales Order Last Contract Date. For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the Generate Approval logic queried tax records by Last Contract Date and returned no result, setting tax percent to null and causing BIP generation failure.
investigation_report.resolution: Changed the Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version: 2019/10/01.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Parts Quote estimation action failed because the user set the record Active flag to N before attempting estimation. An inactive record cannot be updated, so the status could not change and the system displayed "The record in not editable". The behavior was confirmed in UAT1 and is existing functionality consistent with SC; the incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
important_findings: Parts sub-quotes created from the NV sub-quotes screen have a null branch Id, so no branch name is displayed on the Parts Quote screen.
Setting the Active flag to N makes the Parts Quote record inactive and non-editable.
The Estimate button cannot update an inactive record; therefore, the Parts Quote status does not change.
With the Active flag set to Y, the estimation process works correctly.
The behavior was replicated and confirmed in UAT1 and is consistent with SC.
investigation_report.root_cause: The user set the Parts Quote Active flag to N before estimation, making the record inactive and preventing the Estimate action from updating its status.
investigation_report.resolution: Set the Active flag to Y before clicking the Estimate button. No system change was required; the incident was rejected as expected business functionality.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Approval routing for Quote and Job Card was using the total of all Non-chargeable costs when a Free Cost line item was present, causing approval escalation up to HQ for JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71. The required logic was to evaluate only the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the applicable line item type: 42 (Free Cost) or 45 (Reworking). Separate total fields were created, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.
important_findings: For JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71, the presence of a Free Cost line item caused all Non-chargable values to be summed to 19190, exceeding the 10000 approval threshold.
The approval flow must use Non Chargeable Cost Total for Line Item Type 42 only when Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) exists.
The same line-item-specific calculation logic is required for Line Item Type 45 (Reworking).
The existing configuration behaved the same in UAT and required both Siebel configuration and approval flow changes.
New Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields were created for Line Item Type 42 and Line Item Type 45 and used for Quote and Job Card approver selection.
FDP UAT-1 confirmed that approvers were judged using only the Free Cost total before PROD deployment.
investigation_report.root_cause: The approval rule summed all Non-chargable costs whenever a Free Cost line item was present, rather than calculating and using the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the relevant line item type only.
investigation_report.resolution: Created separate Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields for Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) and Line Item Type 45 (Reworking), updated Quote and Job Card approver selection to use the applicable line-item-specific total, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PO return and PO to Supplier orders created by Branch-Parts-Mgr failed to create the required actions and transactions after Generate Approval, preventing Shipment creation and the Accept process. The issue did not occur when Branch-Parts-Staff generated approval. A fix was validated in UAT-1 using PO returns N001239454 (PO to Supplier) and N001239455 (PO to D2S), then released to Prod; affected historical orders were manually recovered.
important_findings: Branch-Parts-Mgr order creation and Generate Approval did not create required actions and transactions.
Branch-Parts-Staff order creation and Generate Approval created the correct actions and transactions.
The issue affected both PO return and PO to Supplier orders, including N000050556 in Prod.
Missing Shipment creation prevented users from proceeding with the Accept process.
The fix was validated on UAT-1 and released to Prod.
investigation_report.root_cause: Generate Approval for orders created by Branch-Parts-Mgr did not create the required actions and transactions.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented and validated a fix in UAT-1, then released it to Prod. Manually recovered actions and transactions for affected PO return and PO to Supplier orders.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Employee records were being interfaced to KB despite the relevant data having been last updated in August. Investigation confirmed that records with the same employee code could include active and inactive entries, with HMCP004 identifying the active/inactive status in the outbound file. The interface logic was changed so records are sent to KB only when the employee master is updated, and duplicate employee-code records use the latest updated record. The fix was tested in UAT and released to Prod on December 15.
important_findings: The reported records were not duplicate records in the initial assessment: one employee record was inactive and another was active.
HMCP004 identifies whether an employee record is active or inactive and was sent in the file accordingly.
The incident required clarification of why data last updated in August was sent to the accounting magistrate on the prior day.
The interface to KB was changed to send affected records only when the employee master is updated.
For duplicate employee code records, the most recently updated record is interfaced to KB.
The fix was validated in UAT before release to Prod.
investigation_report.root_cause: The KB interface logic did not restrict outbound records to employee-master updates and did not select the latest updated record when employee codes were duplicated.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the KB interface so it sends affected records only when the employee master is updated and selects the latest updated record for duplicate employee codes; tested in UAT and deployed to Prod on December 15.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: VIN selection in the vehicle-search pick applet was blocked when the Quote vehicle allocation flag was set to 'Y'. The implemented vehicle-search validation excluded assessments with this flag value, including Stocked Vehicles that needed to be related to Opportunity. The fix sets the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag to 'N' when a vehicle status becomes 'Stocked-In' with sub-status 'Available'; it passed UAT and was released to Prod on 5 Dec.
important_findings: Vehicle search displayed only assessments whose Quote vehicle allocation flag was not 'Y', preventing the VIN from appearing in the pick applet.
The validation affected the function to relate an already Stocked Vehicle to Opportunity and was identified as not being a stated Opportunity BRD requirement.
The affected record was recovered through SR MFTBCFFR-1975.
The implemented fix automatically sets the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag to 'N' when vehicle status is 'Stocked-In' and sub-status is 'Available'.
The fix was validated in UAT using Assessment#H000024836, approved, and released to Prod.
investigation_report.root_cause: Vehicle-search validation excluded assessments with the Quote vehicle allocation flag set to 'Y', blocking selection of Stocked Vehicle VINs for Opportunity.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified the logic so the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag is set to 'N' when a vehicle is set to status 'Stocked-In' and sub-status 'Available'; the change passed UAT and was deployed to Prod.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was investigated in relation to vehicle and account details used in the Job Card (JC) during quote creation. The implemented fix populates missing finance account codes from JC fields. The change was validated in UAT-1, approved for production, and released in the 5th Dec FDP Release.
important_findings: Quote creation from JC required validation of Bill To Finance Account Code and Sold To Finance Account Code.
When Bill To Finance Account Code is null, it is populated using the Bill To Basic Account Code from the JC.
When Sold To Finance Account Code is null, it is populated using the Customer Code from the JC.
The change was deployed to UAT-1 before production approval.
The fix is available in Prod following the 5th Dec FDP Release.
investigation_report.root_cause: Bill To Finance Account Code and Sold To Finance Account Code could be null during quote creation from a Job Card (JC).
investigation_report.resolution: Updated quote creation from JC to populate Bill To Finance Account Code from the JC Bill To Basic Account Code and Sold To Finance Account Code from the JC Customer Code when the respective finance account code is null; deployed to Prod.

Validation found that BZDO008 was generated using D/N price * Qty for price revision, while KB processes price revision and cycle count with the same logic. KB processes cycle count and price revision using the same logic.
BZDO008 must contain D/N price only for both cycle count and price revision.
Records must not be created when D/N price is 0, because they cause an error on the KB side.
Price revision recovery data must use the same Posting date for all records; September 30 data must not include an October 1 Posting date.

investigation_report.root_cause: BZDO008 generation for price revision used D/N price * Qty and allowed records with D/N price of 0, which was incompatible with the shared KB processing logic used for cycle count and price revision.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the UAT and Prod program for both cycle count and price revision so BZDO008 is created with D/N price only, records with D/N price of 0 are not created, and recovery-data Posting dates are consistent across records. The change was tested in UAT and released to Prod.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was replicated in UAT1 using Quote 1-40NT88 and Job Card I001236399. The investigation found that the user changed the editable Print Order value in quote line items after selecting Generate Approval, causing the approval status to become Approved while the Quote itself was not Approved. The incident was classified as an operational/user error rather than a system defect.
important_findings: The issue was replicated in UAT1.
After Generate Approval was selected, the user changed Print Order in the quote line items.
The Approval Tab status became Approved, but the Quote was not Approved.
Quote data must not be changed after Generate Approval; required changes must be made before submitting the approval request.
The incident was approved for denial because it was an operational error, not a system issue.
investigation_report.root_cause: A user changed the editable Print Order value in quote line items after clicking Generate Approval.
investigation_report.resolution: Make all required quote changes before clicking Generate Approval and do not modify the Quote during the approval request.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: After final Sales Order approval, Shipment PoolCost Order creation completed, but the Sales Order status was not updated and the Journal Voucher (JV) was not generated. Analysis determined that a user edited the UI during the delivery request approval window before the status was set to Sales Posting Completed, interfering with the workflow. The issue was replicated in UAT using SO#E001236280, and the affected record was recovered and a JV was created successfully.
important_findings: The process completed through creation of the Shipment PoolCost Order after final Sales Order approval.
The Sales Order status did not update and the associated Journal Voucher (JV) was not generated.
During delivery request approval, the UI remained editable before the workflow set the status to Sales Posting Completed.
A user change during this window caused the error: "The selected record has been modified by another user since it was retrieved."
The issue was replicated in UAT with SO#E001236280.
The affected record was recovered and a JV was created successfully.
investigation_report.root_cause: User misoperation: editing the UI during the delivery request approval window interfered with the workflow that sets the Sales Order status to Sales Posting Completed, causing a concurrent-modification error.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered the affected record and successfully created the JV.
technical_entities: "The selected record has been modified by another user since it was retrieved."

No new journal voucher was created during re-edit because the Job Card amount was unchanged, while the existing journal voucher retained the first closure date. Recovery was completed under SR MFTBCFFR-1887, and the incident was closed.
important_findings: Re-editing the Job Card without changing its amount did not create a new journal voucher.
The journal voucher had been created when the Job Card was first closed, so its posting date remained the first completion date.
Closing the re-edited Job Card on a later date changed the Job Card settlement date.
The differing journal voucher posting date and Job Card settlement date caused the mismatch.
Re-edit functionality was disabled.
Recovery for Job Card I000011402 was completed in SR MFTBCFFR-1887.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Job Card was re-edited without an amount change and closed on a later date. Because no new journal voucher was created for an unchanged Job Card amount, the existing journal voucher retained the first completion date while the Job Card settlement date changed.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovery of Job Card I000011402 was completed in SR MFTBCFFR-1887.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Actual Labour Hour values in Power BI were initially discrepant because the column was aggregated differently from the SC (1-10 report). After removing the aggregation, a further issue was identified: cancelled work order labour hours were included in the 1-10A report. An ODI Package filter was implemented and validated in UAT and PROD to exclude cancelled work order status; historical JC values were provided in an Excel recovery file.
important_findings: Actual Labour Hour was incorrectly summarized in Power BI, while the corresponding SC (1-10 report) column was not summarized.
Removing the Power BI aggregation corrected the initial discrepancy and did not require data recovery because values were recalculated using the revised logic.
The 1-10A report and SC PBI included labour hours from cancelled work orders, including JC I000013477 and JC I022120457.
An ODI Package filter was added to exclude work orders with cancelled status.
The ODI filter affected JCs updated after implementation; earlier JCs required corresponding DB_LAST_UPD updates for recalculation.
UAT validation using JCs I001235533 and I001235538 confirmed that cancelled work order labour hours were excluded from PBI.
investigation_report.root_cause: The ODI Package did not filter out cancelled work order status, causing cancelled work order labour hours to be included in Actual Labour Hour calculations. The initial discrepancy was additionally caused by aggregation of the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI.
investigation_report.resolution: Removed aggregation from the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI and deployed an ODI Package filter in PROD on 13-OCT-2023 to exclude cancelled work orders. An Excel file was provided with updated and previous Actual Labor Hour values for earlier JCs.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: In the affected service quote, External WO line item ML254826 was included in Service Quote Header Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax). Investigation determined that the user changed the outsourcing carry in Flag from 'N' to 'Y' after customer approval and created a PO without running the Update Quote Header Process. This was classified as a user operation issue rather than a system bug.
important_findings: The External WO line item ML254826 was calculated in Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) on the Service Quote Header.
The External WO was initially created with outsourcing carry in Flag value 'N'; a Parts Internal order would have been required to complete the WO after customer approval.
After the quote was customer approved, the user changed the Outsourcing flag to 'Y' and created the PO.
The Update Quote Header Process was not run after the flag change, leaving Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) unchanged.
Calculated fields caused Chargeable Cost on the quote line items to change to 0.
The scenario was replicated in UAT1 using Quote# 1-3Y0ZUP and JC# I001235319.
investigation_report.root_cause: The Outsourcing flag was changed from 'N' to 'Y' after customer approval and PO creation without running the Update Quote Header Process, leaving the Service Quote Header Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) unchanged.
investigation_report.resolution: No system fix was required; the issue was rejected as a user operation error. The Update Quote Header Process must be followed after changing the Outsourcing flag.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PBI Report SV 1_01 and 1_10A showed inflated Sales Price for affected JCs because Warranty Claim data introduced multiple claim records per work order through a report join. Canceled historical claims and newly generated Submitted claims were both associated with the same JC. Okayama Fuso agreed to remove the FALCON column, and an AMS-CR would be submitted before closing the incident.
important_findings: A change associated with MFTBCFFR-1524 added Warranty Claim fields, including CLAIM_PAID_DATE, CLAIM_STATUS, ACCEPTED_TOTAL_AMOUNT, Claim Status, and Claim Number, to the FDP SV PBI report through a join.
For JC I000011334, multiple claims existed for a work order because initial claims were canceled and new claims were generated with Claim Status "Submitted."
The Warranty Claim-derived "FALCON Status" field produced multiple PBI records for a JC, resulting in multiple Sales Price values and inflated Sales Price.
The issue affected JCs beyond the initially reported cases, including I000018287.
Filtering Field Fix Status to exclude "Canceled" was considered, but could remove JCs such as I000018287 and was not confirmed as a suitable general solution.
Okayama Fuso agreed to remove the FALCON column rather than apply an alternative filtering solution.
investigation_report.root_cause: The join introduced for Warranty Claim/FALCON fields returned multiple claim records for the same work order and JC, including canceled and Submitted claims, causing duplicate PBI records and inflated Sales Price.
investigation_report.resolution: Remove the FALCON column via an AMS-CR.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync excluded cases where a revised quote was created before Sales Posting, allowing quote changes to remain linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed. An AMS-CR was implemented for NV and UV to handle revised quotes created before Sales Posting, including cancellation, active/sub-quote reassignment, and validation for pending approvals. The change was validated on UAT1, including a corrected UV rejection-status case, and released to PROD on 5 December.
important_findings: The original sync logic ignored Sales Order sync when the 3rd revised quote was created before NV SO Sales Order.
Revised quotes created before Sales Posting could allow edits to Model Code, option, color, and tire while linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed.

For In Progress or Rejected quotes created before Sales Posting, Delivery Completion approval must cancel the quote and move the active flag and only sub quotes created in the previous revision to the Sales Posting-synced quote revision.

For Pending Approval quotes created before Sales Posting, approval generation or Delivery Completion Approval must show: "There is a correction request request for approval for this order, please check."
During UAT1 validation, UV Quote 1-431G92 rev.5 remained Rejected after Sales Posting; this was resolved and retested with SO E001239841 and Quote 1-43BOUX.
Impacted NV and UV data was extracted after the PROD release for recovery through SRs where applicable.
investigation_report.root_cause: NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync was conditioned on whether a revised quote was created before or after Sales Posting, causing sync processing to be skipped for revised quotes created before Sales Posting.
investigation_report.resolution: Released an AMS-CR for NV and UV that syncs all NV SO Sales Posting Completed cases regardless of revised-quote creation timing; it cancels applicable In Progress/Rejected quotes, updates active flags and prior-revision sub quotes, and blocks Pending Approval quotes with a validation error. The UV UAT1 status-handling defect was corrected before PROD release.

"Latest_flg" in the ODI mapping is sourced from the "Active_Flg" field in the Siebel "s_doc_quote" table.

SO# A000012064 remained unavailable because its status is canceled.
investigation_report.root_cause: A "Latest_flg" filter added for validation purposes was unintentionally left applied in the PBI FDP 3_06 Report.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The incident involved incorrect or ambiguous part-number handling for Parts PO#: N000013519 when allocations changed. Monitoring alone could not determine the correct part number after a change, and CPI had no alternate solution. An AMS CR introduced a D2S Allocation creation timestamp tag so allocations are processed according to the D2S Timestamp; the change was released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.
important_findings: Recovery was completed for Parts PO#: N000013519.
A 2 sec time delay was considered for D2S, matching the implementation on the SC side, but D2S/CPI could not implement an alternate solution.
Cubastion monitoring could not reliably identify the correct part number when a part number changed.
SQL monitoring was prepared and used to monitor the case.
The AMS CR added a tag carrying the Allocation creation timestamp from D2S, enabling processing based on the D2S Timestamp.
The change was released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.
investigation_report.root_cause: D2S allocations did not provide an Allocation creation timestamp for reliable processing order, leaving Cubastion unable to determine the correct part number when part-number changes occurred; CPI had no alternate solution.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented an AMS CR that adds a D2S Allocation creation timestamp tag and processes allocations according to the D2S Timestamp; released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PO Allocation requests received while the material master and Siebel production version creation job was executing failed because the required product version was not yet available. The issue was related to MFTBCFFR-1690; after EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023 reduced job timing, the issue did not recur.
important_findings: PO Allocation requests conflicted with the Product creation job.
The allocation failed when it arrived while the material master and Siebel production version creation job was running.
The product version was unavailable at the time the PO Allocation request was processed.
EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023 reduced job timing and prevented recurrence.
investigation_report.root_cause: A timing conflict between PO Allocation processing and the material master and Siebel production version creation job caused allocation requests to be processed before the product version was available.
investigation_report.resolution: Performed EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023, reducing job timing; the issue did not occur again afterward.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Sales orders A000001195 and A000003231 were investigated for absence from the NV 3-06 report. Both are Child Order Sales Order cases with Required Quantity greater than 1, and the current report configuration filters out sales orders with Required Quantity greater than 1. The behavior matches the SC configuration, so the issue was not a defect.
important_findings: Sales orders A000001195 and A000003231 have Required Quantity greater than 1.
The affected orders are Child Order Sales Order cases.
The NV 3-06 report configuration filters Sales Orders based on Required Quantity.
Sales Orders with Required Quantity greater than 1 do not appear in the NV 3-06 report.
The configuration behaves the same as SC.
investigation_report.root_cause: The NV 3-06 report's current Required Quantity filter excludes Child Order Sales Orders with Required Quantity greater than 1.
investigation_report.resolution: Confirmed expected behavior consistent with SC and rejected the bug.

D21A, D21C, and D21E processing populated Vin Number and Serial Number but omitted the Key value.

UAT1 verification confirmed no chassis orders created after September 8 had a blank Vehicle identification number before the Production release.
investigation_report.root_cause: System configuration for D21A, D21C, and D21E omitted mapping/population of the vehicle master Key field with the VIN# value.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the D21A, D21C, and D21E configuration so Vin Number, Serial Number, and Key are populated with VIN#, validated the change in UAT1, and implemented it in Production. Impacted records were recovered until the Production fix was applied.

Here is the root cause of why this issue happened.
 # During Initial development of Real Time Invoice API, both Planned Delivery Date and Requested Registration Date field were mapped to the Invoice.
 # This mapping failed when Real Time Invoice was tested for the orders where Registration and Delivery was completed (In this case Actual Delivery/Registration dates should have been displayed in Invoice).
 # To fix the above issue, Actual Delivery/Registration Date was mapped to Invoice. However this solution was also incorrect as the logic should have been created as per the completion/Pending of registration and delivery.
 # As this logic was partially implemented in UAT itself, the same code was migrated to production and hence this issue occurred.

Hi Takaya San,
We have implemented changes on production environment. Please check and confirm.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The Real Time Invoice API returned incorrect invoice delivery and registration dates because date mappings did not account for whether registration and delivery were completed or pending. The initial UAT logic was partially implemented and migrated to production. A fix was validated in UAT1 for NV and UV sample requests and then deployed to the production environment.
important_findings: During initial Real Time Invoice API development, Planned Delivery Date and Requested Registration Date were mapped to the Invoice.
The initial mapping failed for orders where Registration and Delivery were completed, for which Actual Delivery/Registration Date should have been displayed in the Invoice.
Mapping Actual Delivery/Registration Date unconditionally was also incorrect; the logic needed to distinguish completed versus pending registration and delivery.
The partially implemented UAT logic was migrated to production, causing the incident.
UAT1 validation for NV order A001233104 and UV order E001233107 returned "Invoice details returned successfully." with DeliveryDate and RegisteredDate values.
investigation_report.root_cause: Invoice date-mapping logic in the Real Time Invoice API was partially implemented and did not conditionally select Planned/Requested dates versus Actual Delivery/Registration dates based on registration and delivery completion status.
investigation_report.resolution: The fix was implemented in UAT1, validated by UAT testing, approved for release, and deployed to the production environment.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: BIP reports for Quote 34 omitted expected line items when cancelled items occupied the page-2 positions. The existing BIP template logic paginated 22 line items per page before excluding cancelled lines, resulting in an empty page. The filtering logic was moved from the BIP template to Siebel so that only non-cancelled line items are sent to BI Publisher. The change was tested in UAT1 and deployed to Prod after validation.
important_findings: Quote 34 had cancelled line items from line 15 through line 53.
The BIP Report logic printed 22 line items per page and ignored line items with Cancelled status.
All line items allocated to page 2 were cancelled, so no line items were printed on that page.
Filtering of cancelled line items was moved from the BIP template to Siebel.
Siebel now sends only non-cancelled line items to BI Publisher.
The change was tested in UAT1 and implemented in Prod Environment.
investigation_report.root_cause: The BIP template paginated line items before excluding Cancelled items; because all items assigned to page 2 were cancelled, the page printed no line items.
investigation_report.resolution: Moved cancelled-line filtering from the BIP template to Siebel, so Siebel sends only non-cancelled line items to BI Publisher; the change was tested in UAT1 and deployed to Prod Environment.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: A cancelled Assessment record required recovery after the vehicle was restocked. The Assessment Request vehicle-value update depends on a change to the UV Inventory vehicle value. Because UV Inventory already contained the same value, 1,034,500, no inventory update occurred and the downstream Assessment Request update was not triggered. Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered, and the proposed recovery approach was to null the UV Inventory vehicle value before recovery.
important_findings: The issue could not be replicated in UAT1 or RT2, and other Assessment Requests worked correctly in PROD.
Vehicle H000000001 was restocked and cancelled through SR#MFTBCFFR-1637.
The workflow is: Assessment Request Stock in Verification Completed; UV Inventory vehicle value updated from UV Purchase Order; Assessment Request vehicle value updated from the UV Inventory update.
UV Inventory already held vehicle value 1,034,500 after Assessment #H000000001 completed a re-evaluation request with the same value.
Because the UV Inventory value did not change, the downstream Assessment Request update trigger did not execute.
Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered with Vehicle Value 1,034,500.
investigation_report.root_cause: UV Inventory already contained vehicle value 1,034,500, so the update from UV Purchase Order produced no value change and did not trigger the downstream Assessment Request vehicle-value update during recovery of a cancelled Assessment.
investigation_report.resolution: Recovered Assessment Number H000000037 with Vehicle Value 1,034,500. For cancelled-Assessment recovery cases, add a recovery step to set the UV Inventory vehicle value to null so the subsequent update triggers the Assessment Request update.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: PO Creation outbound calls to D2S intermittently failed with an internal error and affected PO records were initially recovered by repushing. D2S identified DNS anycast route instability caused by flapping of the track associated with the IP route. D2S removed the track from the static route, after which the DNS anycast route stabilized; no further D2S failures were recorded during one-day monitoring.
important_findings: The DMS_PO_CREATION outbound call failed at DMS_PO_CREATIONPort with an internal error referencing MPL ID AGTuzXKF0wh4rvW5ufoSPGKUIqtU.
Repushing failed PO Creation requests processed successfully, and all records through 31 August were recovered.
D2S initially reported a timeout and increased the read timeout in CPI.
D2S later identified DNS anycast route flapping caused by flapping of the track associated with the IP route.
Removing the track from the static route stabilized the DNS anycast route; the reconfigured track remained under monitoring and was not yet reattached to the static route.
investigation_report.root_cause: Flapping of the track associated with the IP route caused DNS anycast route flapping on the D2S side, resulting in intermittent D2S PO Creation failures.
investigation_report.resolution: D2S removed the track from the static route, stabilizing the DNS anycast route. Failed requests were repushed and recovered, and the incident was closed after one day without further D2S failures.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Order Allocation and Shipment notification issues were attributed to a technical issue in the CPI Middleware configuration (#520341066). Although the configuration fix and order recovery were completed, some FDP Sales Orders created in D2S from 17-Aug-2023 through 23-Aug-2023 experienced shipment notifications before order allocations due to warehouse processing timing. A follow-up AMS CR, MFTBCFFR-1656, was raised to assess applying the SC countermeasure to FDP Force.
important_findings: The CPI Middleware configuration issue (#520341066) caused the Order Allocation and Shipment notification issues.
For recovered orders, warehouse shipment document creation could cause DMS to receive Shipment notification before Order Allocation recovery completed.
Shipment-before-allocation sequencing creates a risk of part number mismatch.
Some FDP Sales Orders created in D2S between 17-Aug-2023 and 23-Aug-2023 were affected despite completed order recovery.
FDP orders created from 24-Aug-2023 onward were stated not to have this issue.
SC AMS CR#610008069 was released as a countermeasure, and deployment to UAT for FDP Force was planned by 4-Sep-2023 under a separate AMS CR.
investigation_report.root_cause: Technical issue with configuring the CPI Middleware configuration (#520341066), which delayed Order Allocation relative to Shipment notification processing.
investigation_report.resolution: The CPI Middleware configuration fix was applied and fully implemented. Follow-up work to apply the SC countermeasure to FDP Force was raised as MFTBCFFR-1656.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Chassis Orders created from TOB files had Chassis Order Line Items with blank status, reproduced in UAT1 and SC UAT and observed in SC PROD. When a DJ2B Change Order was sent to TOB, line items with null status were not processed, so Product Code and Model Code were omitted from the request. The handling was changed in UAT1 and deployed to Production to include blank-status line items in Change Orders; existing chassis orders were recovered.
important_findings: Chassis Orders created from TOB files could have Chassis Order Line Items with blank status.
The issue existed in both SC and FDP and was reproduced in UAT1 and SC UAT; blank status was also observed in SC PROD.
When sending a DJ2B Change Order to TOB, Product Code and Model Code were not sent for line items with null status.
The corrective change handles null Line Item status and includes Product Code and Model Code in the TOB request string.
Existing Chassis Orders raised up to the prior day were recovered; production verification was pending the next PO change.
investigation_report.root_cause: Change Order processing did not handle Chassis Order Line Items with blank/null status, causing Product Code and Model Code to be omitted when sending the Change Order to TOB.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented and deployed a change that allows Change Orders for blank-status line items and includes their Product Code and Model Code in the TOB request; recovered affected existing Chassis Orders.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was replicated on UAT2 for NV Quote#1-1CMP1N, where sales orders with status "Pending" or "Cancel" were considered unexpectedly. Investigation confirmed that the implemented business files maintain only two SO status categories: "Before Sale posting" and "After sales posting", matching UAT behavior. important_findings: The behavior was replicated on UAT2 for NV Quote#1-1CMP1N.
Sales orders with status "Pending" or "Cancel" were reported as not ordered and expected to be excluded from counting.
The business files maintain only two SO status categories: "Before Sale posting" and "After sales posting".
The UAT implementation matches the configured business-file status handling.
Additional status cases require separate handling: Pending, Pending approval, Cancelled, Rejected, and Sales cancellation.
A separate SR was raised as MFTBCFFR-1631.
investigation_report.root_cause: The requested handling for Pending, Pending approval, Cancelled, Rejected, and Sales cancellation SO statuses was not included in the existing business-file scope, which only maintains "Before Sale posting" and "After sales posting" statuses.
investigation_report.resolution: MFTBCFFR-1628 was rejected, and the additional sales-order status cases were raised in SR MFTBCFFR-1631.

Mr. Ikezawa, Mr. Sasaki,
(The following is a Japanese translation of Ravi's comment)
We have confirmed this matter, and below are our confirmation results and proposed solution. Please give us your feedback on this.
 
Case 1. When uploading a vehicle inspection certificate, if the creation date is greater than the existing vehicle inspection certificate, there is no problem even if the expiration date is blank.
 Case 2. When uploading a vehicle inspection certificate, if the creation date is older than the existing vehicle inspection certificate and the expiration date is blank, the vehicle inspection expiration date will not be updated correctly.
 
Solution 1: Solve the Okayama Fuso problem by patching the data. Since the program will not be changed, it is necessary to check whether there is an expiration date for future FDPs.
Solution 2: Change the program to ignore the vehicle inspection certificate if the expiration date is blank.
Solution 3: If the expiration date is blank, set the current date as the expiration date.
Solution 4: Before uploading a new vehicle inspection certificate, add validation so that the user manually sets the expiration date on the vehicle inspection certificate correction screen.
Note: The field in the file that we are using for the expiration date is ON_EXPIRTN_DT_VBALIDITY_PERIOD.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The vehicle inspection expiration date was not updated correctly when an uploaded vehicle inspection certificate had an issuance date older than the existing certificate and a blank expiration date. Certificates with a newer issuance date did not cause the issue even when the expiration date was blank. The agreed approach was to prioritize a data patch for Okayama Fuso and raise an AMS CR for a code change to ignore certificates with blank expiration dates.
important_findings: The issue occurs when an uploaded vehicle inspection certificate has an issuance date older than the existing certificate and a blank expiration date.
Certificates with an issuance date greater than the existing certificate do not cause an issue when the expiration date is blank.
The file field used for the expiration date is ON_EXPIRTN_DT_VBALIDITY_PERIOD.
Solution 1, a data patch for Okayama Fuso, was prioritized.
Solution 2 requires a code change to ignore vehicle inspection certificates with blank expiration dates.
investigation_report.root_cause: A vehicle inspection certificate with a blank expiration date was processed when its issuance date was older than the existing certificate, causing the vehicle inspection expiration date to be updated incorrectly.
investigation_report.resolution: Prioritize a data patch for Okayama Fuso (Solution 1) and raise an AMS CR for a code change to ignore vehicle inspection certificates with blank expiration dates (Solution 2).

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The "Manager Position" and "Position Type JPN" fields displayed SC-version position names instead of FDP-version position names. Their LOV values were sourced from database views migrated from SC FORCE with a hardcoded workspace ID and SC-to-FDP position mappings. important_findings: "Manager Position" and "Position Type JPN" values were sourced from a database view used by the LOV.
The database view was migrated from SC FORCE, carrying a hardcoded workspace ID into all FDP environments.
UAT1 validation initially showed SC-version position names in both affected fields rather than FDP-version names.
"Position Type JPN" and "Manager Name" used Position Type values retained from SC and mapped to FDP positions.
The LOV condition was changed to remove the hardcoded workspace-ID condition and fetch values for the correct workspace ID.
The change was validated in UAT1 and UAT2 (RT2), deployed to Production, and confirmed operational.
investigation_report.root_cause: Database views migrated from SC FORCE contained a hardcoded LOV workspace ID, causing the affected fields to retrieve SC-version position values rather than the correct FDP workspace values.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the LOV condition to remove the hardcoded workspace-ID condition and retrieve values using the correct workspace ID; deployed the validated change to Production.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The scheduled TCB01 package incorrectly changed Chassis Orders from "Shipment Instructed" to "Ordered". The package behavior was based on SC Force/SC Force 2.0 logic involving RF status, which was not appropriate for FDP where RF is disconnected. The corrected TCB01 behavior was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD; the package was scheduled and the latest file was processed successfully.
important_findings: TCB01 selected Chassis Orders with status "Shipment Instructed" and RF status "Send Shipment to RF", then changed the order status to "Ordered".
In FDP, RF is disconnected, and Chassis Order status must not be updated by the TCB01 file.
The agreed TCB01 scope was to update Planned Completion Date and K1_1_OK_Actual_Date, while preventing status updates.
Some UAT1 records were not updated because update_date in column 127 was not today or yesterday; updating update_date to the current date allowed the changes to be reflected.
The PROD fix was deployed, the package was scheduled, and the latest TCB01 file was processed successfully after update_date was updated.
investigation_report.root_cause: The TCB01 package retained SC Force/SC Force 2.0 logic that updated Chassis Order status from "Shipment Instructed" to "Ordered" based on RF status, although this status update was not valid for FDP.
investigation_report.resolution: Modified TCB01 processing so that it does not update Chassis Order status and only updates Planned Completion Date and K1_1_OK_Actual_Date. The fix was validated in UAT1, deployed to PROD, and the TCB01 update_date column was set to the current date before processing the latest file.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Printing to OKYF_10_P03 failed and was investigated through DIS printer and printer-object re-registration. The printer object was recreated on dms-0 and dms-1, and an incorrectly configured DIS port on dms-1 was subsequently corrected. After the recreated object was reflected on August 24, business testing confirmed successful printing; Canon RCA investigation remained ongoing.
important_findings: OKYF_10_P03 was deleted from and re-registered to DISU using del_OKYF_10_P03.txt and add_OKYF_10_P03.txt through web monitor.
The printer object was deleted and recreated on dms-0 and dms-1 using prnmngr.vbs with the Canon Generic Plus LIPSLX driver and LPT1: port.
The DIS port on dms-1 was found to be incorrectly configured and was corrected.
