important_findings: Purchase Quote was created from Assessment Request H000002111 on 18 July, and the Recycle Fee on the UV Purchase Quote was manually changed to zero.

A new Assessment Request was created on 4 August after the previous Assessment Request expired; the displayed Assessment Number on UV Purchase Quote is joined from Vehicle data and updated in Vehicle Master after the Stock-In Process.
The Recycle Fee on UV Purchase Quote is sourced from UV Inventory (Vehicle Master) as the sum of highlighted fields.
During the second stock-in, the Recycle Fee was set to 0 JPY but Vehicle Master still showed 10 JPY.
The defect is common to SC version and FDP: updating Recycle Fee from Vehicle Master with a previous value can populate incorrect values.
investigation_report.root_cause: Recycle Fee updates sourced from Vehicle Master can retain and populate a previous Vehicle Master value instead of the updated value.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The batch job process differed from the SC version. The Interface data extraction was changed to run after the Siebel-side job completes and the Annual Cycle count status is updated to "Completed". The Interface now includes data updated in the previous 24 hours with Cycle count status "Completed".
important_findings: The batch job process differed from the SC version.
Interface data extraction must occur after the Siebel-side job executes.
The Cycle count Type: Annual must have status "Completed" before extraction.
Interface data is limited to records updated in the previous 24 hours with Cycle count status "Completed".
investigation_report.root_cause: Interface data extraction timing and selection criteria did not align with the required post-Siebel job execution and completed Annual Cycle count status.
investigation_report.resolution: Updated the Interface extraction process to run after the Siebel-side job and include only previous-24-hour data where the Annual Cycle count status is "Completed".

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Five records were held from import because four were received with tax rates of 15 or 9, and one with a tax rate of 0%. The receiving system supports tax rates 5, 8, and 10 only. FROCE master-data controls were identified as the mechanism to prevent transmission of unsupported tax-rate data.
important_findings: Four of five received records contained tax rates of 15 or 9.
The remaining record contained a tax rate of 0%, and import was placed on hold.
The receiving system can register tax rates 5, 8, and 10.
Tax-rate changes require a program update.
FROCE master controls can restrict the input data sent to the receiving system.
investigation_report.root_cause: FROCE transmitted records with unsupported tax rates of 15, 9, and 0%.
investigation_report.resolution: Configured master-data controls on the FROCE side to prevent transmission of the same unsupported tax-rate data.

comments.text_enu:
It was necessary to send the recycling confirmation message using DJ2NA1TB with the FDP name, but since it was sent with the SC name DJ2NA1TG, the reply destination was the SC version of FORCE.
A similar error occurred in Pre SIT, and the modified contents have been reverted to the original, so I have requested a check to see if there are other versions for SC.

comments.text: 再テストの結果、リサイクル確定の受信を確認
comments.text_enu: As a result of the retest, confirmation of receipt of recycling confirmation was confirmed.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The recycling confirmation message was sent using the SC name DJ2NA1TG instead of the required FDP name DJ2NA1TB, causing replies to be routed to the SC version of FORCE. The issue had also occurred in Pre SIT because a prior modification had been reverted. After correction and retesting, receipt of the recycling confirmation was confirmed.
important_findings: Recycling confirmation messages must use FDP name DJ2NA1TB.
The message was incorrectly sent using SC name DJ2NA1TG.
Using DJ2NA1TG caused the reply destination to be the SC version of FORCE.
A similar issue occurred in Pre SIT after previously modified content was reverted.
Retesting confirmed receipt of the recycling confirmation.
investigation_report.root_cause: The recycling confirmation message configuration was reverted and used SC name DJ2NA1TG instead of FDP name DJ2NA1TB, routing replies to the SC version of FORCE.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the recycling confirmation message to use FDP name DJ2NA1TB and confirmed successful receipt through retesting.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: Tax Journal entries were created, but account code mappings were incorrectly configured and some required account codes were missing from journal lines. The account code master initially stored concatenated values such as 25580 instead of separating account and sub-account codes as 255-80. After correcting the master configuration and addressing the remaining missing-code and zero-value journal issues, the incident was confirmed fixed.
important_findings: Tax Journal can be searched using the Job card# in Project code.
All expense items require accounting codes if they must be journalized.
Account code and Sub-account code must be maintained separately; for example, 255 and 80 must produce 255-80 rather than 25580.
For JC# I001215124, account codes 255-80 and 255-03 were initially absent from the required credit and debit journal lines.
A 0-yen journal entry was created for recycling fee even though no recycling fee existed.
The account code master was corrected and the issue was subsequently fixed.
investigation_report.root_cause: Incorrect and incomplete account-code master configuration: account and sub-account codes were stored as concatenated values instead of separated hyphenated values, causing incorrect or missing journal account-code mappings.
investigation_report.resolution: Corrected the account codes in the master so account and sub-account codes are separated with a hyphen, and fixed the remaining missing account-code and 0-yen journal-entry behavior.

investigation_report.investigation_summary: The issue was reclassified as an additional change request to support configurable approval thresholds based on delta amount total. The requested behavior is to create an approval flow when the delta amount total exceeds 100,000 and automatically approve when the absolute delta amount total is below 100,000. The change request was planned for Sprint D and placed on hold.
important_findings: Approval behavior must be configurable for FDPs that require approval setup.
Approval flow should be created when the delta amount total exceeds 100,000.
Automatic approval should occur when the Absolute delta amount total is less than 100,000.
For Okayama, setting the threshold to 99,999,999 results in automatic approval unless the threshold is exceeded.
When the Okayama threshold is exceeded, SCHQ-CS-Parts-Mgr should be included in the approval flow.

investigation_report.root_cause: The flag behavior did not correctly update based on JC Type transitions between Claim and non-Claim types.
investigation_report.resolution: Implemented logic to set Replacement parts storage fee /minor part Flag to 'N' for JC Type Claim and automatically change it to 'Y' when JC Type changes to a non-Claim type.
